title: Welcome: Why Visualize QA Evidence?

introduction.dilemma: “My dashboard has forty charts. Why does nobody know whether to release?” Before reading the reply, privately predict what the reader still needs. This is unscored; save your response, not a credential or source identifier.
introduction.reply: A chart collection is not a decision. Start by identifying the comparison a reader needs, then make the scope, date, missing evidence, and next action visible. A reassuring pattern deserves investigation, not automatic applause.

outcomes: Choose visualization, report, dashboard or story by its primary decision job and explain a limitation.
Build one cumulative M02 stakeholder decision and two M17 visual beats using exact headers, individual source reconciliation and justified blanks.
Keep recorded outcomes, missing evidence, readiness, observation and interpretation distinct.
Execute seven actionable insight-pathway sentences, including a concrete falsifying condition, named owner and evidence review rule.
prerequisites: Basic spreadsheet editing and filtering, software-testing vocabulary, identifiers, dates and percentages; Python is not required.
Use learner copies of qa_matrices_governance.xlsx / Stakeholder Decision and qa_matrices_quality.xlsx / Chart Decision, supplied by the parent package in templates. Do not edit shared masters.

For verified practical completion, obtain an access-approved authentic Azure DevOps scenario/export spanning 8–12 weeks with a small relevant Boards slice, scope manifests, local state dictionaries, dated source records, provenance, saved OData $metadata XML or documented REST operation/version, and authoritative same-grain distinct-ID answers. Authentic datasets and real reviewers still require provision.

planning.note: Inherited v2 facilitated/applied C01 planning estimate within the 66-hour program, not measured self-paced duration or required seat-time. Micro means resumable roughly 5–12-minute lecture/practice segments, not a complete evidence build in a few minutes. Elapsed work varies; pause at checkpoint outputs. Follow-up is separate; program follow-up estimate is 258 minutes (4h18m).

topics.title: Pattern, not paint

prediction.prompt: Before discussion, write: The release owner asks which candidate-scope exceptions need investigation. A designer offers a larger green percentage card. What must you ask the owner before choosing a form, and what might the card conceal?

topics.lecture_markdown:
Dear Evidence Desk: our release meeting opens with a large pass percentage. The testers want a dated exception list, the release owner wants a recommendation, and the dashboard designer wants another filter. Which one should I build?

Start with the owner's decision, not the designer's available controls. Ask the owner to finish: ‘At this meeting I must decide whether to ___, and I would change my choice if ___.’ ‘See quality’ leaves the request unfinished. A request to investigate unresolved candidate-scope defects before a readiness meeting gives you a comparison to inspect, an action to support and contrary evidence to seek. Put that agreement in M02; decoration cannot supply it.

A visualization encodes a comparison: outcome categories, dates or scoped groups. A report records status at a stated observation, letting a reader locate individual records and their recorded dispositions. A dashboard selects views for repeated monitoring. A story explains how evidence and limits support an owner's next action. One artifact can do several jobs. Classify it by the job the reader needs most, not by its filename, chart count or interactivity. A dated exception report can be exactly right for lookup while a category stack makes concentration easier to see. Neither is universally better.

**Approved worked illustration only — fictional arithmetic, not organization data.** A fixed inventory has ten distinct required checks: six passing outcomes, two failing outcomes and two with no recorded outcome. Assume at most one outcome per check; authentic test attempts are more complicated. The recorded pass/fail share is 6/(6+2), or 75%. The passing share of the required inventory is 6/10, or 60%. Those denominators answer different questions. A percentage card can describe recorded outcomes without describing inventory completeness. Keep the failing and missing categories separate; the missing outcomes are not favorable, neutral evidence to hide, or proof that every check failed. With no eligible recorded pass/fail outcomes, that share is N/A rather than a success percentage. This illustration claims neither authentic QA010 recorded-attempt measurement nor QA011 acceptance/inventory measurement.

Your source handoff matters as much as the sketch. A Boards view of open work items can show recorded candidate exceptions; it cannot establish missing required test executions by itself. Request the inventory/execution evidence necessary for that broader question. A test-case work item is not an execution result. Map documented identifiers and states into local analytical labels only after inspecting approved metadata or the documented REST response. A successful endpoint request is not a reconciled population, and today's state does not establish yesterday's observation.

Build a scoped pattern with traceable dated detail. Beneath your sketch, name the decision, observation, eligible population, missing evidence and limitation. Link the comparison to authorized contributing IDs, not merely another design matrix. In M17, MatrixId=M02 names the decision origin; SourceRef locates the real evidence. Keep MetricId blank with a ledger justification if you have not claimed a registered metric.

Finally, test a counterexample: complete outcome evidence can contain only failures. Completeness is not readiness. A reconciled failed outcome is still measured evidence, while a missing outcome remains missing. A filter that removes required exceptions makes the view reassuring by changing what it shows, not by improving the product. Choose the form that preserves the needed comparison and enables an owned next request, then let a real reader challenge what your caption permits them to infer.

visual.alt: C01 concept map: owner decision defines a scoped comparison; pattern, dated exceptions and scope investigation qualify a bounded claim, followed by owned action, review and revision or pending evidence.
visual.trace_prompt: Trace Owner decision → Scoped comparison, then both Pattern view and Dated exceptions to Bounded claim. Describe what the two branches contribute. Point to where your first sketch must keep a missing-outcome caveat; explain what is lost if the exception branch is removed.
visual.text_equivalent: Owner decision defines Scoped comparison. Scoped comparison feeds Pattern view, Dated exceptions, and Investigate scope. Pattern view shows the comparison and Dated exceptions qualify it; both feed Bounded claim. Investigate scope checks comparability and feeds Bounded claim. Bounded claim informs Owned next action, which sets Review evidence. Review evidence leads to Revise or pending; Revise or pending returns to Scoped comparison to amend the comparison and its labels. These are evidence/design relationships, not causal claims about product improvement.

preconditions: Save your prediction before reading feedback. Tool work remains open-document/open-source; retrieval never requires memorizing secrets or endpoint syntax.

Use provided learner workbook copies and the approved single-observation Boards export with scope, observation semantics, local open-state dictionary, provenance, metadata/REST contract and authoritative distinct-ID answer. If absent, label all sketches design-only; authentic evidence pending, and list the exact missing provision in the companion Markdown Evidence Ledger page claim boundaries.

M02 Stakeholder Decision grain: one stakeholder information need and decision. Exact columns: NeedId, Audience, Decision, AffectedGroup, ActionOwner, EvidenceNeeded, CommunicationForm, AccessNeed, CounterEvidence, ReviewDate.

M17 Chart Decision grain: one message/evidence beat and visual-to-decision mapping. Exact columns: VisualId, Audience, Decision, Claim, MetricId, MatrixId, Comparison, VisualForm, FilterScope, DenominatorRule, CounterEvidence, EvidenceStatus, SourceRef, ActionOwner. Do not add columns or rename sheets.

steps.title: Confirm the handoff and native field boundary
steps.instructions: Inspect the supplied saved OData $metadata XML for the entity/properties actually used; WorkItemId, Title and State are documented OData source names, not a claim that any guessed entity exists in your environment. OData v2.0 is a released reporting version; test/pipeline Analytics entities require preview-version and metadata validation. The documented REST alternative uses id and fields, including System.Id and System.State; record the actual operation/version. In claim boundaries map LOCAL_RecordKey and LOCAL_StateText from the documented identifier/state; take LOCAL_ObservationUTC and LOCAL_CohortLabel from the dated export manifest; derive LOCAL_OpenFlag only from the approved open-state dictionary. These LOCAL names are notebook labels, not native Azure properties or extra workbook columns. Confirm whether the manifest represents an as-of population: extraction time is not automatically observation time. Do not replace a test result with a test-case work item, or store tokens, private endpoints or personal identities in submissions.
steps.checkpoint_output: A supplied/missing handoff list and native-to-LOCAL mapping in claim boundaries, with observation semantics and dictionary version; no invented records or connection claim.

steps.title: Write the actionable M02 decision
steps.instructions: Open qa_matrices_governance.xlsx → Stakeholder Decision. Create one row with local NeedId C01-NEED-01. Complete Audience, actionable Decision, AffectedGroup and actual person or named instructor-scenario ActionOwner. In EvidenceNeeded describe the supplied export, contributing IDs, distinct-work-item single-observation grain, cohort, observation UTC and unanswered missing-evidence question. Select CommunicationForm for the decision; state text/keyboard needs in AccessNeed; specify what could change the action in CounterEvidence and the agreed date in ReviewDate. Example decision wording only: ‘Should the release owner request investigation of unresolved candidate-scope defects before the readiness meeting?’ Do not convert this wording into an observed outcome.
steps.checkpoint_output: One M02 row addressing all ten exact columns and an explanation of why its form serves the decision.

steps.title: Reconcile the contributing population
steps.instructions: In a temporary filtered view of the supplied source, apply the manifest's project/candidate, work-item-type eligibility and approved open-state mapping. Use one record per distinct source identifier at the stated observation. Check one ID's inclusion against the manifest, then explain the next ID's inclusion/exclusion yourself. Resolve duplicate identifiers against the source; do not remove them for cosmetic benefit. Compare the whole contributing ID set AND count with the authoritative same-grain answer. Record approved locators, exclusions/reasons, duplicates, missing or unexpected IDs and unresolved discrepancies in claim boundaries. Count equality alone is insufficient if the sets differ.
steps.checkpoint_output: Your eligible-ID set/count comparison and one justified eligibility decision, or an explicit unreconciled/provision blocker.

steps.title: Map the first visual beat in M17
steps.instructions: Open qa_matrices_quality.xlsx → Chart Decision. Create C01-VIS-01; copy Audience, Decision and ActionOwner from M02. Set MatrixId=M02 as decision origin, not raw Azure source. Leave MetricId blank when no registered metric is claimed, with ledger note ‘scoped count comparison; no registered metric claimed.’ Fill Comparison with the relevant source-supported category/count comparison, VisualForm with the primary communication job and Claim with only the conclusion supported. In FilterScope declare cohort/type, observation UTC and exclusions. In DenominatorRule state ‘distinct eligible IDs at the stated observation; open-state mapping [dictionary version]; counts shown; any percentage requires its declared population.’ SourceRef includes approved filename, provenance/hash if supplied, metadata/REST reference, authorized contributing-row locators and reconciliation note. Complete CounterEvidence. Measured means this bounded observation exactly reconciled; Conditional/proxy needs explicit qualification; Not Measured means unavailable/invalid evidence; Not Applicable needs a reason. Measured failure is not a pass.
steps.checkpoint_output: All fourteen M17 columns addressed or blanks explicitly justified, with no Measured label before exact source reconciliation.

steps.title: Make and test the first accessible sketch
steps.instructions: Create a labelled text sketch or simple Excel chart/report from the reconciled source view. Put scope, observation UTC, eligible population, source locator and evidence gaps beside the finding in words. Use the map's pattern/detail relationship to identify what needs comparison and what needs lookup. Ask an actual reviewer using text/keyboard only to locate the decision, owner, comparison and limitation; record what they really find and repair the exact caption and Claim if needed. Do not assert that this access/comprehension observation has occurred until it has. A sketch is not a deployed dashboard.
steps.checkpoint_output: First sketch and bounded caption; actual reader task/comment and repair, or a visibly pending reader request.

steps.title: Save one cumulative Desk Test
steps.instructions: Save your learner workbook copies, C01-VIS-01 sketch and claim boundaries ledger. Keep the same rows for review and Your Turn; retain prior wording and scope versions in the ledger rather than creating inconsistent replacements. Missing native fields stay blank and disclosed. Use approved pseudonymous locators that an authorized reviewer can resolve to real dated IDs, not credentials or private raw rows in an exchange channel.
steps.checkpoint_output: Resumable individual draft with cumulative IDs, supplied evidence/blockers and prior-to-revised claim trail.

completion_checks: All ten M02 and fourteen M17 headers preserved; one decision and one evidence beat per row; all blanks justified.
Audience, Decision and ActionOwner agree; MatrixId=M02 is decision origin, while SourceRef resolves authentic evidence.
Exact controlled distinct-ID set/count reconciliation, declared observation/scope/dictionary and authorized locators; discrepancies block Measured.
Caption preserves population, recorded failures and missing-evidence boundary without claiming readiness; real text/keyboard comprehension observation is recorded or pending.
Design-only illustration practice is useful but cannot clear the authentic-evidence gate.

your_turn.task: Finish original Desk Test source-check, first mapping and sketch yourself on a different approved candidate/area subset. Revise the SAME M02/C01-VIS-01 rows and sketch, preserving the guided-scope version and reason in claim boundaries. Choose the form, reconcile the new eligible set and explain its limitation without a completed caption or inclusion hints.

Only its real manifest and controlled same-grain answer are supplied. If missing, use labelled conceptual practice ‘a different candidate subset is proposed but its eligibility manifest is missing’; request it, invent no subset or count, and retain the pending authentic gate.
submission: Own cumulative M02 and first M17 row plus first accessible sketch.
Ledger: alternate manifest, included/excluded ID reasons, exact set/count check or blocker, prior-scope revision trail and independent form/limitation explanation.
Private precommit, two labelled self-review passes, actual reviewer comment and own post-explanation, or clearly pending review request.

Headers/grains and consistent decision/owner are retained; sketch explicitly states scope/date/population/missing boundary.
Explain one ID inclusion/exclusion yourself and why the form cannot establish a broader readiness claim; shared work does not replace your evidence.

self_review_steps: Pass 1 — Navigator/Decision Reviewer: save ‘I would use [form] for [decision]; it cannot prove [limit]; request [evidence].’ Check headers/grains, owner, counter-evidence and where pattern and dated detail meet. Identify the exact caption/cell to repair. Label this self-review, not peer work.

Pass 2 — Verifier: independently revisit the controlled source answer, eligible ID set, observation, state mapping, denominator and missing boundary. Read the sketch without color and check the text/keyboard route. Record discrepancies and revise the same rows; this self-check is not actual source competence verification by a reviewer.
asynchronous_review.request_prompt: Send only an approved redacted first sketch, exact-header table extract and claim-boundary summary to a real peer or instructor in an agreed flexible window: ‘Help this owner find what needs investigation without calling the reassuring pattern readiness. Please locate the decision, owner, comparison and limitation without color or screen sharing, identify one exact caption/cell to repair, and challenge whether SourceRef reaches real dated rows.’ For a solo route send both self-review passes to the actual instructor.
asynchronous_review.reviewer_prompt: Actual instructor challenge: ‘Point to the declared population and missing-evidence boundary; what must the owner obtain before readiness can be discussed?’ Reply with artifact locations, the needed inventory/execution evidence and a proposed bounded owner action. The reviewer checks an individual eligibility decision and gives a specific source/caption/cell correction. Repair it in the same draft, retain prior wording, and write why you kept or changed your choice. A real peer annotation can support learning but does not replace authorized instructor acceptance.
required_real_evidence: Dated actual request/reply and reviewer role or approved pseudonymous identity; never fabricate participants or AI-simulated peer credit.
Real text/keyboard reader's reported decision/owner/comparison/limitation, actual annotation and exact repair/recheck; no invented access observation.
Your own precommit, labelled self-review notes, revision and post-explanation outside matrix columns; actual instructor's source check/acceptance or pending decision.
asynchronous_review.pending_message: You may browse 1.2 and practice ahead while authentic provision or evidence review is pending. recall.prompt: Close notes. Explain why a clear pattern and a dated exception list can serve the same decision but do different jobs. What must both preserve? Commit your response and confidence before requesting feedback; then correct one sentence and re-rate confidence.

questions.prompt: The release coordinator receives a dated list of unresolved candidate-scope records, each with its source locator and recorded disposition. Its main purpose is to tell the coordinator what is currently recorded. What is its primary communication job?

options.text: Report: record status at a stated point.
Visualization: encode a comparison as its primary purpose.
Dashboard: support repeated monitoring through selected views.
Story: explain a recommended decision from evidence.

questions.prompt: Worked illustration only: a fixed inventory has six passing outcomes, two failing outcomes, and two missing outcomes. A card reports 75% = 6/8. Which caption preserves the card's actual denominator and its boundary?

options.text: 75% of all ten required checks passed; release approved.
75% passing among eight recorded pass/fail outcomes; two inventory checks have no recorded outcome.
75% product quality, because recorded outcomes represent the product.
75% complete evidence; the missing checks are neutral and may be hidden.

questions.prompt: A required check has a recorded failing result. A second required check has no recorded result. How should a decision sketch represent them?

options.text: Treat both as passes until someone challenges the sketch.
Delete both from the displayed inventory to keep the chart focused.
Keep the failing outcome and the missing-evidence category separate within the required inventory.
Mark both Not Applicable without asking about their requirement.

games.title: The four trays
games.objective: Choose a communication form by the decision work it performs, not its appearance.
games.rules: Play three rounds in order, untimed. Type V for visualization, R for report, D for dashboard, or S for story. Choose the primary job specified on each card; forms can overlap in real artifacts. Record your answer before reading the solution. After each round compare your reason with the explanation, then retry if helpful. There is no mouse, animation, or sound requirement.

rounds.prompt: Round 1. A release owner asks where the declared inventory's outcomes are concentrated. The artifact is a labelled stack comparing passing, failing, and missing counts, with population and date beside it. Choose V, R, D, or S.

Round 2. A coordinator needs to look up each unresolved candidate record's disposition at yesterday's agreed observation. The artifact is a dated list with source locators and no recommendation. Choose V, R, D, or S.
Round 3. A coordinator returns weekly to the same selected overview, dated exceptions, and evidence-gap views to monitor the same release-scope question. Choose V, R, D, or S.

games.scoring: One practice point for each correct label; maximum 3. No point is lost for taking time or retrying. Record the first attempt separately if you want to see progress. Feedback is explanatory, not a ranking; this score never enters an exam grade.
games.accessible_alternative: Read or have the cards read aloud, then type the full word instead of a letter. An instructor may record a spoken selection. All information and feedback are text; no time limit, drag action, sound cue, or color decoding is necessary.

games.title: Caption repair desk
games.objective: Repair a misleading caption while preserving the comparison and missing-evidence boundary.
games.rules: Play all three untimed rounds. For each draft choose exactly one repair by typing A, B, or C. The winning repair must fix the specified fault without inventing a decision or result. Say in one sentence what changed, then reveal the solution. Retries are welcome; the explanation is the learning feedback, not a judgment of the player.

rounds.prompt: Round 1. Draft: '75% of the full inventory passed.' Worked illustration only: 6 passing, 2 failing, 2 missing; card calculation 6/8. Repairs: A '75% of eight recorded pass/fail outcomes passed; two of ten inventory outcomes are missing.' B '75% of ten passed because missing outcomes do not count.' C '100% quality once missing outcomes are removed.' Choose A, B, or C.

Round 2. Draft: 'No results means no failures.' There are required checks but zero eligible recorded pass/fail outcomes. Repairs: A '0% pass and therefore definitely poor quality.' B 'N/A recorded-outcome pass share; eligible denominator is zero and required outcomes remain missing.' C '100% pass because no failed outcomes were recorded.' Choose A, B, or C.

Round 3. Draft: 'Interactive means decision-ready.' The release owner needs to identify missing candidate evidence before a meeting. Repairs: A 'Add more filters and leave out source rows.' B 'Use a larger green card to simplify the decision.' C 'Choose a scoped evidence-gap view with dated source locators and the owner's next action; interactivity is optional.' Choose A, B, or C.

games.scoring: One practice point per correct repair, maximum 3. Your explanatory sentence is for discussion, not an additional graded hurdle. Untimed retries and instructor clarification are available. Game points do not contribute to quiz or final scores.
games.accessible_alternative: Type the repair letter or copy its full sentence into a text response. A facilitator can read the options and record a spoken answer. Each option, key, and explanation is available without color, dragging, animation, or audio cues.

returns.prompt: Closed-note: A coordinator needs to locate unresolved records, while a release owner needs to see where exceptions cluster. How could one artifact meet both needs without pretending that those needs are identical? State confidence, then check your answer.

Closed-note: All recorded outcomes pass, but required-inventory evidence is unavailable. Say what can be reported, what must remain unknown, and the owner's next evidence request. State confidence, then check.

Closed-note: A useful sketch becomes reassuring only after a filter removes required exceptions. Give a decision-centered test for accepting or rejecting that filtered view, and explain the difference between complete evidence and readiness. State confidence, then check.

remediation.task: Repair the mistaken Claim, Comparison or DenominatorRule in the SAME M17 row and its caption; ask ‘Which population does the caption actually describe, and where is missing evidence visible?’ Use exact-header text/CSV and typed or learner-confirmed scribed explanation if chart access is a barrier.
remediation.recheck: Recheck the controlled contributing-ID set, explain the form's primary job and population/missing boundary to the actual instructor, and record the specific feedback and repair. Retake topic practice after correction; all evidence gates still apply.

topics.stretch: Explain how a repeated-monitoring dashboard sketch and a recommendation story could use the same bounded pattern/detail pair for different primary jobs. Name an inference each cannot support; do not add a dataset or claim deployment.
topics.resume_checkpoint: Save C01-NEED-01, C01-VIS-01, first sketch, current changed-scope manifest and claim boundaries; note last completed step, unresolved source/reader check and next action. Resume that step without rebuilding the assignment.

Labelled text sketch and exact-header long-format UTF-8 CSV; keyboard and non-screen-sharing work are equivalent.
Typed or accurately scribed explanations with learner confirmation retain individual authorship; practice/games untimed.

topics.title: The insight pathway

prediction.prompt: Individually predict: A dated open-bug count line points downward, but a colleague says the candidate scope narrowed. What sentence can you keep now, and which check must come before a quality-improvement headline?

topics.lecture_markdown:
Dear Evidence Desk: our open-bug chart slopes downward. I wrote ‘Quality improved’ above it. My colleague says the project scope changed. How do I find out whether the headline survives?

Treat the downward line as an observation, not a verdict. Work through observe → question → investigate → interpret → decide → measure → revise. Each action changes the sentence you may responsibly write. You can observe a lower recorded count at a labelled second date without knowing its cause. Your question asks whether the same population and conditions were observed. Resolution, changed candidate scope, a different open-state definition or weaker detection could produce a similar shape; you need not choose an explanation before testing it.

Investigation recovers each observation's scope manifest, contributing ID set and state dictionary. Check one distinct identifier per observation, equivalent eligibility and the source meaning of the date. Compare each whole set and count against its authoritative same-grain answer. Do not force a match by removing inconvenient exceptions. A matched subset is useful only when authentic evidence supports its membership. If scope differs, preserve that difference beside the observation instead of silently redrawing history. Percentages do not repair incomparable populations.

**Approved worked illustration only — fictional arithmetic, not organization data.** At observation A, forty recorded defects include eight open. At differently scoped observation B, eight recorded defects include four open. The count falls from eight to four, a 50% count reduction. Open shares of those recorded inventories are 20% and 50%. These are distinct-defect observations, not test histories or customer-failure denominators. The smaller count and larger share can both be arithmetically true. Neither establishes product quality across changed scopes. Reversing the headline into a deterioration verdict repeats the original error: you have changed the verdict without repairing comparability.

Interpret only within checked boundaries. A matched recorded comparison may support reviewing unresolved exposure; it does not prove fewer customer failures. Make your claim able to lose. Name a concrete source fact, such as dated manifests revealing different eligibility rules, that would make you withdraw or narrow it. ‘More data would be interesting’ gives the owner no test. A colleague's disagreement raises a question; disagreement alone is not the falsifying evidence. Likewise, an owner's signature cannot make a claim immune to source facts.

Decide on an accountable action that the evidence can support. Requesting the missing dated evidence can be a useful decision even when reassurance remains unjustified. Name the owner and agree ReviewDate in M02. Measure at that review whether valid comparable evidence actually arrived. A sent request is not receipt or validation. Revise according to checked evidence, or keep the historic claim Not Measured/pending and update the request when it does not arrive. Preserve the earlier observation, warning and rejected headline in claim boundaries; revision changes the interpretation, not original source history.

Current work-item State cannot recreate an earlier as-of population. Azure Boards current work items, revisions and snapshots have different meanings; this course uses controlled dated observations and leaves historical modelling to later lessons. Relabelling today's JSON or extraction timestamp as last month's observation would fabricate evidence. Finish by comparing two genuinely different sketches serving the same decision: a dated category/detail view and a bounded two-date comparison, for example. Put scope, date, population, source and missing evidence beside both. Let an actual reader separate observation from interpretation and challenge your review rule before the instructor verifies your individual evidence.

These are evidence/design relationships, not causal claims about product improvement.

steps.title: Recover the decision and begin seven actions
steps.instructions: In claim boundaries retain the current claim and counterclaim. Write seven labelled actionable sentences: Observe, Question, Investigate, Interpret, Decide, Measure, Revise. Begin Observe with the supplied recorded pattern and labelled date; Question asks whether both dates have equivalent populations/definitions. Leave unsupported interpretation and future review results unavailable, not allegedly completed. State the precise source evidence that could defeat the proposed headline.
steps.checkpoint_output: Preserved original wording plus Observe/Question and an explicit investigation request; seven action labels ready for completion.

steps.title: Check the paired dated source contract
steps.instructions: Inspect each export's saved OData $metadata or documented REST response/operation/version. Retain native WorkItemId/Title/State or REST id and fields System.Id/System.State; map LOCAL_RecordKey/LOCAL_StateText explicitly and derive LOCAL_OpenFlag from the approved dictionary. LOCAL_ObservationUTC and LOCAL_CohortLabel come from each manifest, not invented source properties or new columns. Confirm as-of semantics rather than treating extraction time as observation time. OData v2.0 is released reporting; test/pipeline entities require preview metadata validation and a test case is not an execution. If earlier evidence is absent, assign the request to M02 ActionOwner with ReviewDate and keep historical counts Not Measured.
steps.checkpoint_output: Two observation contracts and native/LOCAL mappings, or an owned historic-evidence blocker with no fabricated date/count.

steps.title: Independently reconcile both populations
steps.instructions: For each date create a temporary source view at distinct-identifier, single-observation grain. Apply declared candidate/type eligibility and the approved local open mapping, with equivalent meanings across dictionary versions. Save included IDs/authorized locators, every duplicate, exclusion/reason, missing and unexpected ID. Compare each exact set AND count to its controlled answer; explain an inclusion/exclusion at each date. Document any scope change and whether an authentic matched subset exists. Do not omit required IDs to manufacture agreement. If population is unavailable leave any share blank/N/A with its reason; counts still need a stated population. A percentage requires its named numerator and eligible denominator; zero denominator yields N/A.
steps.checkpoint_output: Two exact dated set/count checks or explicit blockers, plus your comparability verdict and supporting source fact.

steps.title: Repair C01-VIS-01 without erasing history
steps.instructions: Update Comparison to say whether the first sketch is a category/detail view at one date or a matched two-date comparison. Repair Claim, FilterScope, DenominatorRule, CounterEvidence, EvidenceStatus and SourceRef together. Preserve Audience, Decision, MatrixId=M02 and ActionOwner. SourceRef must reach real dated evidence, not merely M02. Keep MetricId blank with its no-registered-metric justification when appropriate. Retain the rejected headline and reason in claim boundaries. Measured applies only to a reconciled bounded observation; changed-scope limits remain visible and absent history stays Not Measured, not a reversed quality verdict.
steps.checkpoint_output: Revised first M17 row and caption with observation/inference distinction, source boundary and retained prior wording.

steps.title: Add one genuinely different visual beat
steps.instructions: Add C01-VIS-02 to the SAME Chart Decision sheet. Address all fourteen exact columns: VisualId, Audience, Decision, Claim, MetricId, MatrixId, Comparison, VisualForm, FilterScope, DenominatorRule, CounterEvidence, EvidenceStatus, SourceRef, ActionOwner. Use the same M02 decision/owner; justify any blank MetricId. Make a genuinely different form, such as a labelled two-date count sketch paired against a dated exception report. Both must serve one decision/cohort contract, not unrelated questions or different themes alone. Include text scope, observation UTC, denominator/population, source reference and unresolved evidence beside each sketch; summarize without color.

steps.title: Complete the investigation and owned review rule
steps.instructions: Finish all seven ledger actions from supplied evidence. Investigate tests comparability; Interpret states only its bounded meaning and a concrete falsifying condition. Measure specifies what valid evidence to inspect at ReviewDate; Revise specifies how to narrow/withdraw the claim or keep it pending if evidence is absent. games.title: Route the evidence letter

games.rules: There are three untimed rounds. Each round supplies scrambled lettered cards from consecutive sections of the pathway. Type their letters in the correct action order. rounds.prompt: Round 1. A 'Question whether the lower count uses the same scope.' B 'Observe the recorded lower count at the second labelled date.' Type the two letters in order.

title: Why Tell QA Stories?

introduction.dilemma: The numbers speak for themselves. Why write anything?
introduction.reply: Numbers can report what was recorded; they cannot appoint a decision owner, explain a missing population, or request the next check. A QA story supplies those connections without inventing certainty.

outcomes: Write an individually authored scoped claim → evidence → action with distinct decision holder and action owner, consistent with one M02 decision need and six cumulative M17 message beats.
Explain and reconcile contextual published-result attempts against approved distinct inventory members without inventing missing outcomes.
Test three different rival explanations, retain rejected reasoning and use actual counter-evidence to revise the smallest owned evidence request.
Submit one accessible, source-linked 150-word evidence editorial and demonstrate its reasoning to a real authorized reviewer.
prerequisites: Basic testing vocabulary, spreadsheet filtering and understanding of identifiers, dates and percentages.
Learner copies of qa_matrices_governance.xlsx / Stakeholder Decision (M02) and qa_matrices_quality.xlsx / Chart Decision (M17), supplied by the parent package under templates.

An instructor-controlled authorized 8–12-week scenario or anonymized authentic exports, actual stakeholder brief and decision rights, approved inventories and member-to-result mapping, selection/publication records where available, source locators and same-grain reconciliation controls.
Instructor-reserved different authentic configuration for topic 2.1 and frozen adjacent UTC comparison window for topic 2.2; real reviewer availability and permitted artifact-sharing route.

If authentic sources, mapping, held-out controls or reviewer are unavailable, continue only a labelled design-only evidence request. Source-backed assessment remains blocked. No connected Azure tenant or organizational observation is supplied.

Topic allocations were 45 minutes each; checkpoint 6, final 9, integration/review 15. Micro means resumable roughly 5–12-minute reading/practice portions, not a complete evidence build in a few minutes. Follow-up is separate; self-paced elapsed workload and authentic review waits vary.

topics.title: A decision-ready argument

prediction.prompt: Before discussion, write two sentences: a team presents a reassuring published-results percentage but cannot account for an expected configuration. What can that observation tell the release holder, and what must the next sentence request? Name one thing you must not infer. This is conceptual practice, not a source-backed finding; rate your confidence low/medium/high.

topics.lecture_markdown:
### Your letter to the Evidence Desk

“Dear Evidence Desk: our published pass share is higher. My slide says ‘Quality improved.’ The release owner asks what to do, but surely the percentage is the answer?”

### The reply: give the evidence a decision job

A percentage answers a calculation question. Your release owner asked a decision question. Those questions may share a meeting, but they are not interchangeable. Start by writing the choice: “Should the release owner defer candidate R until the missing regression suite is accounted for?” Now your evidence has a job other than looking pleased with itself.

Build the argument in three sentences: claim → evidence → action. The claim states the narrow finding, not the conclusion you hope to earn. “The published pass share increased in the recorded cohort” is narrower than “quality improved.” The evidence sentence names the period, candidate, recorded population and important gap. The action sentence names the person who can do something, what they should do, and when the result returns to the decision holder. Do not promote the analyst into release owner merely because the analyst owns the spreadsheet.

Use the reporter's questions as a repair tool. Who decides, and who performs the next check? What choice is pending? When was the evidence recorded, and when is review? Where does the claim apply—project, candidate, suite or configuration? Why does the gap matter to this choice? How was the recorded population selected? Then add “so what?” to explain the decision consequence, and “now what?” to request a concrete action. Put a missing answer in the matrix as a question to resolve, not a sentence to quietly omit.

Compare two endings. “Pass share rose; excellent work” asks for admiration. “Release owner: defer the candidate decision until the QA lead reconciles the missing suite against the approved inventory” asks for action. The second does not assert that the missing suite failed. It says the current evidence cannot settle a material release question. That distinction makes the recommendation stronger, not gloomier.

Keep the affected users in view without inventing their outcomes. A passing recorded test can inform a release discussion, but no customer experience has been observed merely because a card turned green. A decision-ready story connects what is known to a proportionate next step and leaves the unknown visible.

### Labelled conceptual proof: the percentage became less informative

This is the approved invented tiny arithmetic, **not an organizational dataset or assessed finding**. Assume one published attempt per expected member, no reruns and no other outcomes. Before: 18 Passed and 2 Failed, out of 20 expected members. After: 12 Passed and 0 Failed, with 20 still expected. The published pass share is 90% before and 100% after: 10 percentage points higher, despite six fewer passing attempts and eight expected after members lacking results. Neither eight failures nor twenty passes follows.

The published Passed-or-Failed denominator and expected inventory answer different questions. In authentic exports, reruns invalidate that simple subtraction: match approved distinct-member keys to contextual project/run/result-attempt keys first. Preserve unknowns when mapping is missing. M02 records the stakeholder choice and requested evidence; M17 records three decision/evidence beats with scope, denominator, status and locators. Neither is a source-result fact table. Your next steps put this bounded reasoning into the existing matrices, not into a prettier but unsupported headline.

visual.alt: A named decision scopes published attempts and approved inventory; reconciliation bounds the finding and rivals inform an owned next action.
visual.trace_prompt: Trace Named decision → Published attempts → Reconcile keys and Named decision → Approved inventory → Reconcile keys. Why are there two incoming paths instead of one total? Then trace Reconcile keys → Bounded finding → Owned next action. Point to the relationship that prevents the percentage alone becoming a release instruction. Annotate the paths in text; read the preserved Reply and Proof alongside the map.
visual.text_equivalent: Named decision scopes Published attempts as a recorded cohort and Approved inventory as expected distinct members. Published attempts supplies retained attempt keys to Reconcile keys; Approved inventory supplies its approved member mapping to the same node. Reconcile keys supplies counts and visible gaps to Bounded finding. Bounded finding invites Rival predictions, which predict and request Discriminating records. Discriminating records qualify or revise Bounded finding. Bounded finding supplies claim/evidence to Owned next action; Rival predictions supply remaining uncertainty to that action. Owned next action requests the next discriminating check. These arrows describe reasoning and requests, not a demonstrated causal effect.

preconditions: Open learner copies, not master workbooks. M02 grain: one stakeholder information need and decision; M17 grain: one message/evidence beat and visual-to-decision mapping. Keep all exact headers listed in the course resource section.

Use the actual brief's narrow authorized configuration A and declared candidate/UTC comparison windows. A and B are teaching labels, not invented source IDs. Reserve the real different configuration B for Your Turn.

Use documented Test Runs List / Test Results List REST JSON exports retaining project/run context and native id/outcome. Approved inventory and selection/publication completeness require separate records. Alternatively require Analytics XML $metadata and response exports validating the actual entity/properties/version; released OData v2.0 Boards WorkItemId/Title/State are not execution evidence, and test/pipeline Analytics needs appropriate preview validation.
Keep credentials, tokens, private raw rows and public tenant URLs out of drafts and uploads. Store only approved anonymized locators; no live source request or connection is claimed here.

Exact M02 — Stakeholder Decision, workbook qa_matrices_governance.xlsx, sheet Stakeholder Decision; columns in order: NeedId, Audience, Decision, AffectedGroup, ActionOwner, EvidenceNeeded, CommunicationForm, AccessNeed, CounterEvidence, ReviewDate. Grain: One stakeholder information need and decision.

steps.instructions: Open qa_matrices_governance.xlsx, sheet Stakeholder Decision. Filter for a relevant existing NeedId, including a cumulative C01 need; retain it or assign one unique local NeedId. steps.title: Separate the choice from the communication
steps.instructions: From the real brief fill M02 Audience with the decision holder, Decision with the choice/candidate, AffectedGroup, ActionOwner for the next evidence check and ReviewDate. Ask who/what/when/where/why/how/so what/now what. Put source/candidate/UTC window, inventory version, selection definition and requested row locators in EvidenceNeeded. Use CommunicationForm='150-word evidence editorial with source-linked table'; use actual AccessNeed, including readable keyboard-accessible table. steps.title: Map native results and approved inventory
steps.instructions: Inspect the authorized REST response/export manifest. Native JSON id is a result ID, not automatically a distinct expected inventory member; native outcome is its recorded outcome. Document LOCAL ResultKey = retained project/run request context + result id; LOCAL RecordedOutcome = outcome; LOCAL ExpectedMemberKey = instructor inventory key using its approved point/member-to-result mapping. These are modeled concepts, not native Azure fields or added matrix columns. Record mapping and grain in M17 SourceRef/DenominatorRule. Retain reruns at project/run/result-attempt grain. Use the approved mapping to list unmatched expected members and results outside the cohort in the permitted source appendix; do not subtract attempts from distinct-member counts. With missing mapping request it and stop before an assessed finding.
steps.checkpoint_output: An authorized ID-level comparison with contextual attempts, expected-member mapping and unmatched keys, or a disclosed missing-mapping request.

steps.title: Build the recorded QA010 beat
steps.instructions: In the first M17 row align Audience/Decision/ActionOwner with M02. Set Claim to the narrow recorded finding, MetricId=QA010, MatrixId=M02, Comparison to the two explicitly defined recorded cohorts and VisualForm='source-linked text table'. Set FilterScope to actual candidate/suite/configuration/UTC windows. DenominatorRule: Published Passed attempts / published Passed-or-Failed attempts × 100; retain reruns, show other outcomes separately, and zero denominator=N/A with counts/reason. Count actual source attempts, never message rows. Record native/context/mapping locators in SourceRef. QA010 is a local illustrative evidence argument, not an ISO-mandated KPI or whole-product score.
steps.checkpoint_output: One bounded QA010 beat with explicit source grain, stable denominator, exclusions and authorized locators.

steps.title: Complete the gap and action beats yourself
steps.instructions: Use the second row for the approved-inventory gap and the third for the next evidence action. Leave MetricId blank on non-rate beats; put 'no calculated measure for this beat' in DenominatorRule. Write the third Claim/ActionOwner yourself from the actual brief: what owned check follows without inventing omitted outcomes? Keep CounterEvidence visible. EvidenceStatus is Measured, Conditional/proxy, Not Measured or justified Not Applicable according to supporting evidence, not belief. SourceRef retains exact authorized response/file locator, project/run/result keys, inventory version and review-note locator. Requested unavailable evidence is Not Measured; unknown expected counts stay blank and disclosed.
steps.checkpoint_output: The same three M17 rows now express observation, bounded gap and owned next action; no absent outcome is imputed.

steps.title: Reconcile, trace and export

topics.lecture_markdown:
### Your letter to the Evidence Desk

“Dear Evidence Desk: I drafted a story about our code improvement before checking the missing suite. The story is persuasive. Do I really need rival explanations?”

### The reply: a story must risk revision

Yes. A story is a record of reasoning, not a shelter for your favorite explanation. Start with the observation that survived reconciliation: the recorded pass share changed. Now write three rivals beside it: the code improved, easier tests were selected, or executed results were not published. None wins because it sounds agreeable. Each needs a prediction that records could confirm or weaken.

For better code, ask whether comparable assertions on matched scope show fewer failures after the documented correction. For easier selection, ask whether versioned selection records removed demanding members from the after cohort. For missing publication, ask whether retained execution or publication records account for expected members absent from the result export. These requests differ. A manager's confidence cannot substitute for any of them, and finding one selection record cannot dispose of every publication question.

Write the weakening condition before the check. “If the omitted members have retained failed results, the reassuring published-only story is incomplete.” “If the approved selection scope is unchanged, easier selection becomes less plausible, although publication remains open.” This makes revision possible without requiring you to pretend you predicted everything. An analyst who changes a conclusion in response to relevant evidence has not lost the argument; the argument has done its work.

Keep interpretation status separate from evidence status. You might measure that a selection configuration changed while leaving its effect on product behavior uncertain. Record the observed change and source locator, then mark the explanation as supported only within that boundary. When records cannot be obtained, retain “unresolved”; absence of the record is not disproof of the rival. Keep rejected interpretations with the reason for rejection instead of quietly removing them from the ledger.

The final action need not be release or cancel. “Not ready to recommend; QA lead, obtain retained publication records before the release review” can be the responsible conclusion. Explain why that collection could change the decision and who owns it. Do not request every imaginable dataset. Request the smallest discriminating check for the actual choice. Honest uncertainty narrows the action; it need not paralyze it.

### Labelled conceptual proof: three rivals, three different checks

The following is the approved conceptual demonstration, **not collected Azure records**. These are requests and weakening conditions, not supplied file locators.

| Rival | Prediction and discriminating request | What would weaken it | Before collection |
|---|---|---|---|
| Better code | Documented correction aligns with fewer failures on matched test/configuration assertions; request revision/build context and comparable retained results | Matched results do not improve, or scope/environment/publication changed materially | Live explanation, not established cause |
| Easier test selection | Versioned selection and inventories show demanding members excluded from the after scope | Approved selection records and mapped inventory members match both cohorts | Live explanation until comparison is checked |
| Missing publication | Retained run/publication records account for executions absent from the export | Complete retained records reconcile to the full approved cohort without unmatched executions | Unresolved when retention/completeness is unknown |

A fictional card confirming exclusion would support a scope-change observation, not an excluded failure. A different fictional card revealing retained failed results within the same cohort would require reconciliation and revision. Neither observes all customer outcomes. In your actual build, record supporting evidence as Measured, Conditional/proxy, Not Measured or justified Not Applicable in M17 EvidenceStatus. Keep the interpretation's unresolved/weakened/supported-within-scope disposition, previous wording, reason and locator in CounterEvidence. Add three rival message beats to your existing three—not a rival worksheet—and return the smallest remaining owned request to the same M02 need.

topics.title: Problem, Goal, Action, Impact

prediction.prompt: Before discussion, predict: a reporting channel is narrowed and recorded customer failures fall, while the release process is unchanged. What business conclusion can the director draw, and what evidence would you request before funding an intervention? Write one observation, one hypothesis and one request.

topics.lecture_markdown:
### The Letter

‘Dear Evidence Desk: our director wants half as many bugs next quarter. Support keeps handling the same customer failure after releases. I can add regression checks, but I cannot make customers report fewer problems. What belongs in a business case?’

### The Evidence Desk reply: give the proposal a way to lose honestly

Start with the business harm, not the easiest count. You want fewer disruptive customer failures without unacceptable delivery, security or user harm. That organization outcome sits above a service outcome: preventing recurrence of the specified failure in a stated release context. Below it, put a process objective: make the release review examine evidence for the affected risk. Finally name an operational action and its owner. This Business Goal Hierarchy explains how each level might support the next; it does not prove that it will.

PGAI makes that reasoning inspectable. Your Problem is an observed condition or explicitly unverified gap, with a source and scope. ‘Bugs are high’ names a symptom. ‘The required regression condition is absent from this candidate’s reviewed evidence’ identifies a possible controllable gap. Your Goal describes the desired outcome and guardrails. Your Action says who changes which process, against which baseline, and by when. Your Impact states the expected consequence, assumptions and exclusions. Keep the word ‘if’: a proposed mechanism is not an observed benefit.

Try an incentive counterexample. If testers stop publishing failures, recorded bugs may fall although customers remain exposed. That action satisfies a count target while defeating its purpose. Retain detection completeness and adverse outcomes as guardrails. Also distinguish observation from cause: repeated reports may be documented, but an omitted check need not explain every report. A changed supplier configuration or ambiguous requirement could offer a rival explanation. Ask for evidence that distinguishes them before announcing a root cause.

Write a risk as cause or condition → possible event → business consequence. In M03, each row represents a risk-objective/control relationship. A prevention control changes the conditions that allow harm; a detection control reveals a problem or its consequences. Baseline approval may prevent configuration drift; a regression assertion may detect it. Keep both relationships when they address the same RiskId, but reconcile the distinct risk objectives rather than counting rows. A retained unmeasured objective improves inventory honesty without demonstrating an adequate control.

**Conceptual illustration only—not organizational observations.** The approved example assumes a control needs eight staff hours at $80/hour and each avoided failure avoids six support hours at that rate. The conditional net is -$160, $320 or $800 for one, two or three assumed avoided failures. Other costs and customer, security and delivery effects are excluded. These are assumption checks, not realized savings or a forecast interval. Do not transfer those numbers to your authentic build. Similarly, locally defined ordinal Impact=4 and Likelihood=3 yield LocalPriority=12: an ordering aid, not a probability, expected loss or ISO threshold.

Predeclare how you will challenge Impact in M18. For this review-focused intervention, QA004 means corrective-action effectiveness verification: compare scoped follow-up with a specific criterion, baseline and cohort. Keep guardrails, confounders, a stop/revise rule and a day-30 review date. Before reviewed follow-up exists, the outcome is pending and EvidenceStatus is Not Measured. Task closure only establishes implementation. You can recommend examining a bounded intervention while honestly leaving effectiveness, costs or approval unresolved.

visual.alt: Business harm motivates PGAI; M03 controls and M01 decision rights meet baseline evidence and qualified M15 review at a policy gate, with owned gaps and later M18 effectiveness review.
visual.trace_prompt: Trace Business harm -> PGAI proposal -> M03 risk controls -> Baseline evidence, then M18 follow-up rule -> Effectiveness review -> PGAI proposal. Which link describes a proposed mechanism, and which later review could challenge the Impact? Explain why the return arrow is not proof of savings. Locate the corresponding M03 Control/EvidenceRef and M18 SuccessCriterion/Confounders fields. Record your observation before checking your own plan.
visual.text_equivalent: Business harm motivates PGAI proposal. PGAI names M03 risk controls and assigns M01 decision rights in parallel. M03 requires baseline evidence and, if applicable, M15 qualified threat/hazard review. Baseline evidence supports that review and informs the policy gate with evidence and disposition; qualified review supplies scoped approval or pending status, while M01 names gate authority. Absent/inadequate evidence becomes an owned gap routed through M01. Unresolved gate risk returns to M03. Gate review may authorize or revise M18's intervention/follow-up rule. M18's criterion and cohort feed effectiveness review, which supports, revises or stops PGAI, not automatic release permission or proven savings.

steps.title: Inspect native source properties and retain provenance
steps.instructions: Read the authorized supplied Boards export only after its .../_odata/v2.0/$metadata XML validates WorkItems properties such as WorkItemId, Title and State. Alternatively read documented REST GET .../_apis/wit/workitems?ids={ids}&api-version=7.1 JSON: value[].id and System.Id/System.Title/System.State in fields. steps.title: Populate the exact M03 relationship rows
steps.instructions: Keep headers in this exact order: RiskId, RiskStatement, Impact, Likelihood, LocalPriority, Control, RequirementId, TestId, Owner, ResidualRisk, EvidenceStatus, EvidenceRef. Enter one risk-objective/control relationship per row. Copy the governed RiskId from the inventory; it need not be an Azure ID. Write cause/condition -> event -> consequence. steps.title: Apply the actual local priority formula
steps.instructions: Document the approved local ordinal Impact and Likelihood 1–5 anchors, reviewer and effective scope in the plan. Use integers within approved scales. In existing LocalPriority use =[@Impact]*[@Likelihood] for an Excel Table, or =C2*D2 in the first data row with the manifest-order columns and fill down. If either input or anchors are missing/unapproved, leave priority blank and explain why rather than letting a blank become zero. RiskId, Impact, Likelihood and LocalPriority are LOCAL governed fields, not guaranteed Azure properties. Repeated RiskId rows must have consistent statements/scoring; do not sum repeated priorities or treat the product as probability, money or an ISO score.
steps.checkpoint_output: Formula-bearing approved rows and documented blank-score reasons, plus a distinct RiskId inventory check separate from relationship-row count.

steps.title: Read results, not just links
steps.instructions: Inspect the actual referenced assertion/result, baseline/configuration and review disposition. Supplied REST GET .../_apis/test/Runs/{runId}/results?api-version=7.1 JSON uses value[].id and value[].outcome; LOCAL_ResultId/LOCAL_Outcome are staging labels, with project/run context retained. Supplied GET .../_apis/build/builds?api-version=7.1 uses value[].id and value[].result; LOCAL_BuildId/LOCAL_BuildResult do not mean supplier approval or validation. Use EvidenceStatus Measured, Conditional/proxy, Not Measured or justified Not Applicable. Measured means the declared evidence requirement was checked, not test passed or risk eliminated. A link with no reviewed result stays Not Measured, with link present; result absent in EvidenceRef. A reviewed Failed result may be evidence; keep its failed disposition and residual risk, never convert it to a passed control. Explain limited proxies; nonapplicability needs approved justification. Each reference must resolve to a restricted package/file/operation or register, context, record key, revision/baseline, period, extraction time and reviewer disposition.
steps.checkpoint_output: Evidence decisions and resolvable references or precise owner/date gaps for every M03 row; outcomes remain distinct from adequacy.

steps.title: Write four substantive PGAI paragraphs
steps.instructions: In the supporting plan, write Problem with source/gap and rival explanation; Goal hierarchy with detection and adverse-effect guardrails; controllable Action with owner/date/baseline; and conditional Impact with assumptions/exclusions. Compare prevention and detection alternatives and name the assumption that would reverse preference. Use only supplied authentic cost inputs. If absent, state cost-benefit not estimated—inputs requested. Do not create a PGAI matrix or transplant the illustration’s numbers. Any rate requires authentic numerator/denominator/cohort/exclusions; denominator zero means N/A with zero count and reason, not zero or 100%.
steps.checkpoint_output: Four-paragraph case that distinguishes observation, hypothesis and conditional consequence, with bounded cost evidence or owned requests.

steps.title: Predeclare the M18 review before outcomes
steps.instructions: Keep exact headers: ExperimentId, Decision, Owner, BaselineCohort, BaselineSource, Intervention, SuccessMeasureId, SuccessCriterion, Guardrail, StopRule, ReviewDate, EvidenceStatus, OutcomeEvidence, Confounders. One row is one predeclared intervention/follow-up rule. Link Decision to the M03 RiskId and plan objective. Use the same service/risk scope in BaselineCohort, genuine baseline reference or explicit missing baseline, and owned Intervention. Set SuccessMeasureId to QA004 — Corrective-action effectiveness verification. Complete SuccessCriterion with specific comparable effectiveness evidence and review-date cohort, not action closed. Record delivery/security/user adverse effects in Guardrail, evidence-triggered stop/revise conditions in StopRule, and a day-30 ReviewDate tied to planned start in the plan. SuccessCriterion is LOCAL governed text, not a native Azure property. Before follow-up, OutcomeEvidence remains pending and EvidenceStatus=Not Measured. Record detection changes, other fixes and release mix in Confounders.
steps.checkpoint_output: A predeclared QA004 row with baseline or owned gap, criterion/cohort/owner/guardrail/stop/date/confounders and pending outcome.

steps.title: Reconcile and export the cumulative work
steps.instructions: Compare the distinct M03 RiskId set to the full approved risk-objective inventory; list missing/extra IDs and repair or explicitly block them. Check each relationship against approved requirements; explain blanks and consistent repeated RiskId scores. Count each objective once for inventory coverage while retaining every control relationship. Cross-check M18 RiskId links, baseline scope and owners against M03 and the brief. Export Risk Control and Improvement Experiment as separate exact-header long-format CSVs, all rows and blanks retained, no merged cells. Keep a plain-text gap/action summary and restricted source appendix. Complete the reserved slice in Your Turn rather than repeating the whole build.

games.title: Route the PGAI Letter
games.objective: Separate a problem, an owned action, and a bounded impact rather than turning a symptom into a target.
games.rules: Play the three rounds in order. Enter one letter or type its full label: P=Problem, G=Goal, A=Action, I=Impact. Each card has one intended PGAI function in its stated context. Read the solution only after answering. No timer; revise after feedback.

rounds.prompt: C03-T1-G1-R1: Card: 'Customers repeat the same checkout failure after a release; we must investigate whether the release check omitted the affected condition.' Choose P, G, A, or I.
C03-T1-G1-R2: Card: 'The QA Lead will restore and review the omitted regression check against the candidate baseline before the next release gate.' Choose P, G, A, or I.

C03-T1-G1-R3: Card: 'If the change avoids two failures at the stated support cost, its illustrative net benefit is $320; security and customer effects remain outside this calculation.' Choose P, G, A, or I.

games.scoring: One point for each correct first response; maximum 3. Practice only, not an exam grade. After feedback, replay any round to repair the reasoning; record first-response and revised scores separately if desired.
games.accessible_alternative: Read or have the cards read aloud and type P/G/A/I, the full label, or dictate it to a facilitator. All information and feedback are text; no time limit, dragging, colour, sound, or animation is required.

games.title: Budget Boundary Desk
games.objective: Compute conditional impact and choose a claim that survives uncertainty.
games.rules: The numbers are a worked illustration only, not a learner or organization dataset. Keep these assumptions on screen: control=8 hours at $80/hour; each avoided failure=6 support hours at $80/hour; no other costs or benefits included. For each of three rounds choose A, B, or C, or type the option text. Use paper or a calculator freely. Reveal each solution after the response; no timer.

rounds.prompt: C03-T1-G2-R1: Assume two avoided failures. What is net benefit? A: $960. B: $320. C: $640.
C03-T1-G2-R2: Now assume just one avoided failure with all other inputs unchanged. What is net benefit? A: -$160. B: $160. C: $480.

C03-T1-G2-R3: Which sentence may enter the decision memo? A: 'The change has already saved $320.' B: 'ISO guarantees a positive return.' C: 'Under one-to-three assumed avoided failures the net ranges from -$160 to $800; actual avoided failures and omitted effects need review.'

games.scoring: One point per correct first response; maximum 3. This is ungraded practice. Recalculate or revise after feedback without penalty. Arithmetic and interpretation can be discussed separately.
games.accessible_alternative: Use the written assumptions and type A/B/C or the complete option. A facilitator may read inputs and accept spoken answers. Calculators are allowed; there is no compulsory speed, pointer gesture, colour cue, sound, or motion.

returns.prompt: Closed notes: a team changes only who is allowed to report a customer failure. Why can the recorded count change without the business harm changing, and what guardrail should a quality goal keep? State confidence before checking.

Closed notes: two controls address the same risk objective. Explain which unit checks inventory completeness, which unit retains the controls, and why the local priority must not be doubled. State confidence before checking.

Closed notes: an intervention is implemented and outcomes later improve while detection also changes. What must a predeclared effectiveness review examine before supporting the Impact, and what may it conclude if evidence is immature? State confidence before checking.

remediation.task: Use the original reporting-suppression counterexample. Mark observation/hypothesis/conditional consequence in your own PGAI; with the actual instructor, trace and repair one unsupported M03 key or M18 outcome/criterion using the precise source gap. Reuse the same rows; no fictional cost inputs enter the authentic build.
remediation.recheck: Explain why the repair is honest, restate the immediate recall without notes, and retry the unchanged topic quiz without penalty. Source blockers remain pending despite a knowledge pass.

topics.stretch: Using only the supplied scope, compare prevention and detection alternatives with a downside and discriminating evidence request. Name the assumption that would reverse preference. Absent authentic cost inputs call for evidence-needs analysis, not invented savings.

topics.title: QA governance, not just testing

prediction.prompt: Predict individually: the correct named specialist is assigned to review residual risk, and a supplier approval for an earlier component version is on file. Neither has reviewed the current candidate. What is established, what remains pending and who must act next? Do not assume a release policy not supplied.

topics.lecture_markdown:
### The Letter

‘Dear Evidence Desk: the pipeline is green, the action is closed, and our supplier emailed “approved.” Can the QA Lead release the candidate? We have no intended-use review and two people are marked accountable.’

### The Evidence Desk reply: evidence, authority and permission differ

A green test log answers a limited execution question. Your QA management plan must answer who controls quality-related work throughout the life cycle, which evidence is required, and what happens when that evidence is inadequate. ISO 9001 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207 supply QMS and life-cycle context, not this course’s local operating model. Neither a dashboard nor an operational measure demonstrates organizational conformity. Detailed crosswalking requires licensed texts and qualified review; course completion is not ISO certification or an auditor qualification.

Begin each M01 row with a governed activity. Assign exactly one accountable role and at least one responsible role. R/A includes both, so it already counts toward accountability. If a specialist decides security residual risk while a release owner decides overall release, create separate activities. You preserve each decision right without creating two competing As. Map roles to named people or authorized delegates in your plan and record limitations. The AccountabilityCheck formula only checks role consistency: ‘Valid assignment’ cannot tell you that anyone actually reviewed or approved the candidate.

Next separate verification, validation and testing. Verification examines specified requirements; validation examines fitness for intended use. Testing supplies some evidence for these judgments. Passing assertions may show specified export behaviour, yet leave unanswered whether intended operations users can complete their business task in context. Keep the validation review as its own owned evidence gap. Do not fill it with a test URL or add an accountable letter as if that were an observation.

Bind every evidence record to the candidate baseline: source revision, build definition, relevant dependencies/configuration, test context and identifiable artifact. A supplier email needs the approved component version, scope, exclusions, date and authorized reviewer. An earlier version’s approval is not universal permission. Historical review requires retained historical records; today’s work-item link cannot reconstruct what the decision maker saw then. Nor does a documented baseline prove a rebuild was performed.

**Conceptual illustration only—not a learner or organization dataset.** The approved example freezes five required checks. Four have approved evidence and dispositions; supplier approval lacks version and scope. One evidenced regression assertion is Failed. QA002 evidence completeness is 80%, not ‘80% ready.’ With adequate supplier evidence, completeness becomes 100%, but the failed mandatory assertion can still block release under the stated local policy. Completeness counts evidence plus disposition against the full required inventory; readiness applies outcomes, remaining risk and authority. Removing a missing check changes the denominator rather than solving it. With denominator zero, report N/A and its reason.

Where applicable, M15 retains the reviewed threat/hazard-control chain, actual witnessed result and qualified residual-risk owner/approver. It is not a complete threat model or safety case. A link or named specialist without current scoped review leaves a pending decision. Failed evidence and absent evidence need distinct records; policy determines their consequences. You recommend within that policy, not waive a mandatory control yourself.

Finally, a correction repairs a defect; corrective action changes a process to address its reviewed cause. Closure records implementation. Keep two distinct QA004 effectiveness rules for the omitted regression condition and supplier/configuration drift. Each needs its own baseline, criterion, cohort, guardrails, stop rule and scheduled review. Missing follow-up leaves effectiveness pending, not ineffective or successful. Preserve due reviews and justified date-change history. Governance becomes useful when another authorized reader can trace the uncomfortable decision safely, understand its limits and identify the next owner action.

visual.alt: Parallel decision-rights and baseline-bound control/qualified-review paths meet at the policy gate; absent evidence routes to owned gaps, and effectiveness returns to PGAI.
visual.trace_prompt: Trace the parallel paths M01 decision rights -> Policy gate decision and M03 risk controls -> M15 qualified review -> Policy gate decision, with Baseline evidence feeding review. Then trace Baseline evidence -> Owned evidence gaps -> M01 decision rights. Why can role consistency and complete evidence still leave a gate unresolved? Locate M01 EvidenceSource/AccountabilityCheck and M15 WitnessedResult/Approver/EvidenceRef; write which record supplies authority and which supplies reviewed evidence.
visual.text_equivalent: Business harm motivates PGAI proposal. PGAI names M03 risk controls and assigns M01 decision rights in parallel. M03 requires baseline evidence and, if applicable, M15 qualified threat/hazard review. Baseline evidence supports that review and informs the policy gate with evidence and disposition; qualified review supplies scoped approval or pending status, while M01 names gate authority. Absent/inadequate evidence becomes an owned gap routed through M01. Unresolved gate risk returns to M03. Gate review may authorize or revise M18's intervention/follow-up rule. M18's criterion and cohort feed effectiveness review, which supports, revises or stops PGAI, not automatic release permission or proven savings.

steps.instructions: Keep exact header order: ActivityId, Activity, QALead, EngineeringLead, ProductOwner, ReleaseOwner, SecurityOwner, EvidenceSource, ReviewDate, AccountabilityCheck. Retain separate rows for quality-objective approval, risk/control review, verification-evidence review, intended-use validation review, configuration-baseline review, supplier-evidence review, release decision, relevant specialist residual-risk approval, missing/failed-control escalation, corrective-action implementation review, effectiveness review and evidence retention/access review.
