steps.title: Assign RACI and use the unchanged consistency formula
steps.instructions: Use only R, A, C, I or R/A across QALead through SecurityOwner, based on the actual rights brief. Map every role to a named person/authorized delegate and limitations in the plan. Use Excel Data Validation/List for allowed tokens separately from the formula. In a Table, AccountabilityCheck is =IF(AND(COUNTIF([@[QALead]:[SecurityOwner]],"A")+COUNTIF([@[QALead]:[SecurityOwner]],"R/A")=1,COUNTIF([@[QALead]:[SecurityOwner]],"R")+COUNTIF([@[QALead]:[SecurityOwner]],"R/A")>=1),"Valid assignment","Repair assignment"). For a non-Table first data row use =IF(AND(COUNTIF(C2:G2,"A")+COUNTIF(C2:G2,"R/A")=1,COUNTIF(C2:G2,"R")+COUNTIF(C2:G2,"R/A")>=1),"Valid assignment","Repair assignment") and fill down. Exactly one accountable and at least one responsible role are required. Split distinct specialist/overall decisions rather than adding As or erasing rights. ReviewDate can be planned; EvidenceSource must distinguish planned work from an actual reviewed record. Complete an activity’s executor and source disposition yourself from the brief; Valid assignment is role consistency, not approval evidence.
steps.checkpoint_output: Token-validated RACI, formula outputs and named delegate map; actual reviews versus owner/date source gaps clearly separated.

steps.title: Separate verification, validation and testing
steps.instructions: For verification inspect the supplied controlled requirement/assertion and reviewed result against baseline. For testing retain actual result/run/build context and published outcome from the documented JSON/export. Keep native value[].id/outcome in test-result responses and id/result in build responses distinct from LOCAL_ResultId/LOCAL_Outcome/LOCAL_BuildId/LOCAL_BuildResult interpretations. For validation request separate intended-use criteria, context and real review record. If absent retain the validation activity and explicit Not Measured gap in M01 EvidenceSource text, with its evidence-request owner/date. Never use automated-test success as intended-use validation. Update M03 EvidenceStatus/EvidenceRef/ResidualRisk to actual evidence, not a desired result.
steps.checkpoint_output: Three separately sourced dispositions, retained actual failed outcomes and precise owned validation or other gaps.

steps.title: Bind configuration and supplier approvals to the candidate
steps.instructions: List the approved source revision, build definition, dependency/configuration manifests, tested configuration and artifact identifier in the plan using actual records. Trace them through build/test references, not build count. Request version-bound supplier approval, scope/exclusions/date and authorized reviewer. Record absence in M01 EvidenceSource and the related M03 control. A supplier email’s word approved or a successful build does not approve this baseline. QA006 context requires this operational baseline distinction; no new measure implementation is required. A documented baseline is not a demonstrated rebuild unless actually performed and recorded; current links do not establish past evidence.
steps.checkpoint_output: Candidate-bound baseline/supplier chain or precise adequacy gaps with next evidence owner, preserving historical/current differences.

steps.title: Populate applicable exact M15 evidence chains
steps.instructions: Keep exact order: ObjectiveId, Type, ThreatOrHazard, Impact, Control, RequirementId, TestId, WitnessedResult, ResidualRisk, EvidenceStatus, Owner, Approver, EvidenceRef. Use only instructor-approved applicable objectives; one row is one threat/hazard-control objective and reviewed chain. Map ObjectiveId to M03 RiskId in EvidenceRef text, no extra column. Copy supported real requirement/test keys. Put actual witnessed result and reviewer context in WitnessedResult; if absent, leave blank with a precise EvidenceRef gap, not pipeline green. Name qualified Owner/Approver and cite the current scoped approval or pending decision in ResidualRisk/EvidenceRef. Use Measured, Conditional/proxy, Not Measured or justified Not Applicable according to reviewed evidence, not desired outcome. If no objectives apply, retain M15 in the deliverable with qualified approved applicability explanation in the plan, not invented hazard rows. M15 is not a complete threat model/safety case or a performed user/security study.
steps.checkpoint_output: Applicable controlled M15 objective chains with real results/scoped approval or explicit qualified pending gaps, or approved nonapplicability evidence.

steps.title: Apply frozen policy without self-waivers
steps.instructions: In a supporting prose gate checklist state each required check, evidence requirement, acceptance rule, outcome, evidence status, accountable decision owner and missing/failed-evidence escalation. Link each governed review to M01 and applicable risk/control rows. Use the full frozen inventory. QA002 — Release gate evidence completeness counts required checks with approved evidence AND disposition divided by the frozen full required-check inventory; it is not a pass rate or readiness score. Any rate must use authentic records, show cohort/exclusions and numerator/denominator; zero denominator is N/A with zero count and reason. Apply actual policy to recommend hold, authorized bounded condition, approval or not ready to recommend. A reviewed failure can have complete evidence and still block release. A missing review is not a failed result; neither can be hidden. You cannot waive mandatory controls or self-approve specialist risk. State who must act next and requested response date.
steps.checkpoint_output: Plain-text policy-bound recommendation and owned escalation list distinguishing inventory completeness, outcomes and permission.

steps.title: Complete two independent effectiveness rules
steps.instructions: Retain the same exact M18 headers from 3.1: ExperimentId, Decision, Owner, BaselineCohort, BaselineSource, Intervention, SuccessMeasureId, SuccessCriterion, Guardrail, StopRule, ReviewDate, EvidenceStatus, OutcomeEvidence, Confounders. Use two actual instructor cases, or explicitly proposed/unexecuted process cases: omitted regression condition and supplier/configuration-baseline drift. Distinguish immediate correction, reviewed cause or cause uncertainty, process action and implementation. Keep one QA004 intervention/rule per case, each with its own baseline, scheduled cohort, owner, criterion, guardrail, stop rule, review date and confounders. For the first require reviewed comparable evidence about recurrence of the specific omission with stable detection and stated opportunities. For drift require reviewed version-bound approvals and matching baselines in the predeclared follow-up sample, with unresolved mismatches visible. Fit criteria to the local brief, not an invented ISO threshold. Missing/immature follow-up stays Not Measured with implementation/effectiveness pending in OutcomeEvidence. Keep due reviews and justified date-change reasons; do not select favourable cohorts after seeing results.
steps.checkpoint_output: Two cumulative QA004 cases with independent predeclared rules, genuine evidence or pending outcomes and preserved date-change history.

steps.title: Specify retention/access and reconcile all four sheets

questions.prompt: For one release-risk approval activity, M01 assigns QALead=R, EngineeringLead=C, ProductOwner=I, ReleaseOwner=A, SecurityOwner=R/A. What must be repaired?

options.text: Replace every consulted role with an accountable role.
Delete the evidence reference because roles are sufficient evidence.
Accept the row because two accountable roles provide more assurance.
Choose one accountable role under the approval policy; split distinct specialist and release decisions into separate activities if needed.

questions.prompt: A corrective action was closed after a missing regression check was restored. No follow-up evidence has been reviewed against its predeclared effectiveness criterion. What can the plan honestly state?

options.text: The action is demonstrably effective because it is closed.
Implementation is recorded; effectiveness remains pending evidence and review.
The action is ineffective because the follow-up is not yet available.
Remove the action from the review cohort until its result is favourable.

questions.prompt: In a worked illustration only, all five required gate checks have approved evidence and recorded dispositions; one test disposition is Failed. Which conclusion is justified?

games.title: Release Review Inbox
games.objective: Choose a bounded release-review disposition instead of translating every evidence link into permission to release.
games.rules: Each of three inbox cards states a local gate policy and available evidence. Choose exactly one of A, B, or C, or type its text. Do not assume facts outside the card. Read the solution and feedback after each choice. Untimed, with notes allowed.

rounds.prompt: C03-T2-G1-R1: Policy: a failed mandatory acceptance assertion blocks release until resolved and reviewed. Card: the correctly baselined test has a reviewed Failed result and defect disposition. A: Hide the failure because its evidence is complete. B: Hold release for the failed assertion while retaining its complete evidence status. C: Mark the evidence missing because it failed.

C03-T2-G1-R2: Policy: supplier configuration approval is required for this release baseline. Card: a supplier email says 'approved' but identifies neither component version nor approval scope. A: Record an adequacy gap and request version-bound approval from the supplier evidence owner. B: Treat the email as universal approval for every supplier version. C: Omit the supplier check from the frozen inventory.

C03-T2-G1-R3: Policy: intended-use validation review is required before approval. Card: automated tests verify the specification, but no intended-use review exists. A: Let test success stand in for validation. B: Announce zero user risk. C: Mark validation Not Measured, name its Product Owner, and escalate the missing review at the gate.

games.scoring: One point per correct first response; maximum 3. Games are practice, not exam scores. Replay with the evidence boundaries visible and explain why an incorrect disposition changed.
games.accessible_alternative: Type A/B/C or the full disposition, or use a reader/facilitator. Cards, solutions, and feedback remain available in text. No timer, drag-only operation, animation, audio, or colour-based scoring is required.

games.title: Repair the Responsibility Row
games.objective: Repair one governed activity at a time, preserving exactly one accountable role and responsible execution.
games.rules: Use this role order in every card: QALead, EngineeringLead, ProductOwner, ReleaseOwner, SecurityOwner. A and R/A each count as one accountable role; R and R/A each count as responsible execution. Choose one proposed repair A/B/C per round. Each card states its local policy; do not infer a universal role hierarchy. Answer by text or keyboard, without a timer.

rounds.prompt: C03-T2-G2-R1: Activity: approve overall release recommendation. Policy: ReleaseOwner owns this decision; QALead prepares evidence. Current row: R, C, C, I, C. A: Change ReleaseOwner from I to A. B: Change EngineeringLead from C to I. C: Change QALead from R to I.

C03-T2-G2-R2: Activity: approve security residual risk. Policy: SecurityOwner is accountable and performs the specialist review; ReleaseOwner is consulted for the overall release decision. Current row: C, C, I, A, R/A. A: Change QALead from C to A. B: Change ReleaseOwner from A to C. C: Change SecurityOwner from R/A to I.

C03-T2-G2-R3: Activity: execute configuration-baseline review. Policy: ReleaseOwner is accountable; EngineeringLead executes it. Current row: C, I, I, A, C. A: Change SecurityOwner from C to A. B: Change ReleaseOwner from A to I. C: Change EngineeringLead from I to R.

games.scoring: One point for each correct first repair; maximum 3, ungraded. After feedback, state the accountable and responsible roles for the repaired row. Unlimited replay; no deductions for revising an explanation.
games.accessible_alternative: Keep the role order as a written list and enter A/B/C or dictate the edit. A facilitator can read the row aloud. All solutions are textual; no speed, dragging, colour, sound, or motion requirement.

returns.prompt: Closed notes: an earlier supplier approval and a current green build exist. Explain the missing relationship needed for a current release recommendation and name who should receive the request under local decision rights. State confidence before checking.

Closed notes: specified assertions pass, but no intended-use review exists. Explain what is known, which judgment remains missing, and why adding another accountable role to the same decision does not supply the missing evidence. State confidence before checking.

Closed notes: an effectiveness review is due but comparable follow-up is absent. Why would deleting that review or moving its date without explanation distort governance, and what honest disposition/action should remain? State confidence before checking.

After both individually verified topic builds, take the separate protected checkpoint, 3/3, before assembling the final plan. Reuse the original six assembly actions and real request-challenge/revise step, then take the separate protected course final, 4/5. No public exam keys or duplicated final questions.

Original six cumulative assembly actions (reuse existing rows; not a duplicate assignment):

1. **Write the decision and PGAI case.** State the release/service/baseline/window, accountable decision owner, Business Goal Hierarchy, Problem and rival explanation, Goal with adverse-effect guardrails, controllable Action, and bounded Impact. Mark missing cost inputs and any hypothetical arithmetic. Reject a target that rewards concealing defects.
2. **Bind responsibilities to controls.** Include the local risk taxonomy—such as customer failure, configuration/supplier change, security exposure, and intended-use evidence gap only where applicable—along with locally approved ordinal scale anchors. Map each required review/control to the exact M01 activity and M03 risk/control relationship; include a qualified M15 chain where relevant. Explain prevention versus detection. Cite the named role-to-person/delegate mapping, decision scopes, and actual approvals or pending requests.
3. **Make release dispositions executable.** List every required gate in the plan with its frozen inventory source, evidence requirement, acceptance rule, outcome, evidence status, accountable owner, and failure/missing-evidence escalation. This prose checklist is supporting plan content, not an invented replacement Excel matrix. Separate verification, validation, and testing. Give a scoped recommendation: release, condition under authorized policy, hold, or not ready to recommend. Explain the residual risk and who may accept it; never self-approve a specialist risk. Include supplier version/scope and configuration/artifact boundaries.
4. **Finish the improvement and retention sections.** Include the two corrective-action cases, immediate correction, reviewed cause or explicit cause uncertainty, owned intervention, implementation disposition, predeclared effectiveness criterion, baseline/follow-up cohort, guardrail, stop rule, and review date. Cross-reference the existing M18 rows; retain pending or ineffective reviews. Add approved retention/access rules and evidence owner, or name the unresolved local policy decision.
5. **Perform row-level reconciliation.** In a supporting text appendix, list each source inventory ID and its matrix row/relationship, plus source file/record/revision and evidence disposition. Compare full required sets with distinct keys at each relevant grain; show missing/extra/duplicate IDs and how they were repaired or explicitly blocked. Repeated M03 objective/control rows must not inflate objective coverage. Preserve required unlinked objectives and failed results. Any claimed operational rate must state its numerator, denominator, cohort, and exclusions, use the register definition, return N/A for zero, and be calculated from authentic controlled records—not the proof's fictional inputs. No rate is required when the necessary source is absent.
6. **Request challenge and revise.** Ask a reviewer to find one concealed evidence gap and one contested approval right. Record the criticism, your specific row/plan change, and remaining uncertainty. Export the four sheets and a plain-text decision summary that a reader can use without colour, mouse-only interaction, or private-data disclosure. Instructor review determines whether authentic-source gates are met; missing inputs are blockers, not learner mistakes to cover with plausible values.
reviewer_checks: Authorized reviewer individually checks authentic sources, full inventories, changed scope and every original topic acceptance gate; no quiz, game, shared output or self-report replaces source competence.

Original local C03 rubric: score each of six criteria 0–3; competence is at least 2 in EVERY criterion, no compensation between dimensions. Original program technical/capstone threshold of at least 80% and all-area competence/all gates remain separate requirements.

Absolute gates: truthful data/connection/authorship; no exposed credentials; exact templates/grains; full inventories or explicit assessment blockers; no fabricated expected counts; row-level reconciliation; valid RACI; failed/missing evidence distinct; no inferred validation/specialist approval; no closure-as-effectiveness; accessible text/tabular output; no organizational ISO conformity claim.

Preserve two real substantive review cycles and their original separately weighted program components. Record actual received challenges, individual revisions/defences and source reasons; two-pass self-review is not peer credit. Preserve required actual access/comprehension reader observations elsewhere in the program: provision remains due and no readers or observed behaviour are invented here.

Original anchored six-criterion local C03 rubric, unchanged:

Score each criterion **0–3** using the anchored descriptions. Competent means **at least 2 in every criterion**; no strong dimension compensates for an unsafe gap elsewhere. The rubric is instructor-defined, not an ISO audit scoring scheme.

| Criterion | 0 — Missing/unsupported | 1 — Needs revision | 2 — Competent | 3 — Strong |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Business relevance and PGAI | No decision or unsupported outcome guarantee | Goal/count target with weak owner/action link | Explicit hierarchy, controllable owner/action, assumptions, rival explanation and guardrails | Also compares alternatives and identifies the impact assumption that reverses the recommendation |
| Matrix grain and reconciliation | Invented IDs or missing required objectives concealed | Relationship counts mistaken for objective counts; gaps unexplained | Exact template columns; full inventory reconciled at distinct key/relationship grain; blanks and evidence gaps retained | Row-level source/revision chain is independently reproducible and discrepancies are specifically resolved |

topics.lecture_markdown:
### Choose the decision, not the prettiest chart

“Dear Evidence Desk: our director wants one green summary, the shift lead wants a defect queue, and engineering wants the records. Customer support says none of those explains who is being hurt. Must we choose one audience?”

Choose one decision per message, not one audience for the whole evidence system. Start with a verb: authorize, allocate, investigate, defer or request evidence. Ask who can make that choice, what deadline matters and what evidence could change it. “Show quality” describes neither an action nor its authority. In M02, write the information need and the action owner before choosing the communication form. A chart can then serve the decision instead of substituting for it.

Build four distinct perspectives in the existing Stakeholder Decision matrix: decision-maker, operations user, investigator and affected-person representative. This is the Empathy Spectrum, a perspective-taking exercise rather than a psychological score. The director may allocate resources; operations may assign work; engineering may challenge a classification. An affected representative may request investigation or explain an unobserved consequence without controlling the budget. Verify these roles from the supplied brief. Do not invent authority to make a row look complete, or omit someone because they cannot authorize spending. Decision rights and affectedness are different.

Translate the finding only after freezing its evidence boundary. Your budget note can use finding → implication → owned action. Your operations version can use scoped queue → assignment → next review. Detail, wording and the requested action may differ, but cohort membership, numerator and denominator definitions, UTC observation and material limitations must survive. Restrict identifying row detail to authorized investigators. An executive can receive less personal information without receiving stronger certainty.

**Worked illustration only — fictional arithmetic, not organizational evidence:** at one declared UTC observation, twelve eligible open defects include three above a locally approved age threshold. The approved calculation is `100 * 3 / 12 = 25%`. A budget note can describe that bounded exposure and request investigation time. An operations queue can assign those same three items using restricted source references. Neither version establishes customer impact. Calling the remainder “75% healthy” changes the claim: not being above this age threshold is not verified product health or customer safety. Never enter these fictional counts as your assessed finding.

Make the communication testable. Before review, specify three reader tasks: locate the limitation without a mouse, interpret status without color, and find scope/counts in the text table. In M16, ExpectedBehavior describes what should happen. Only an actual authorized reader's task attempt can populate ObservedBehavior with a dated evidence reference. Your own inspection is useful self-review, not independent task evidence. A table does not guarantee understanding simply because it exists.

Finally ask who remains absent. Internal reported defects do not represent every affected customer. Keep missing user experience, terminology, numeracy, access and privacy needs visible, with a real collection owner and review date. If authentic records or readers are unavailable, submit a labelled design and blocked request. You can keep learning while that review is pending; you cannot label an unobserved result measured or a planned access test successful.

Missing or invalid support leads to Hold and request evidence, which returns to source capability for collection or to the contract for repair. A supported bounded indicator leads to Accessible audience versions, then Observed task review. A task barrier returns to the audience versions for repair; usable task evidence leads to Owned action and review, which reconsiders the decision and information need. None of these arrows proves product readiness or customer benefit.

topics.title: Selecting measures through 15939

prediction.prompt: A spreadsheet includes a returned state value and an author-created age flag. Because both are cells, can they be treated as equivalent raw observations when choosing an investigation indicator? Predict what must be documented first.

topics.lecture_markdown:
### Select a measure that can change a decision

“Dear Evidence Desk: I have sixty candidate measures and an executive asking for ten. Can I select the ten Azure fields that are easiest to obtain and call that a measurement process?”

Convenient data can help answer a question; it should not choose the question for you. ISO/IEC/IEEE 15939 supplies a tailorable measurement-process framework, not a universal scoreboard or the course's ten required KPIs. Here you use a local operational chain: information need → base observations → derived calculation → interpreted indicator → validity check → application → review. This teaching chain is not the complete licensed standard or a conformity checklist. Begin with the decision and affected people already recorded in M02.

For an aged-open investigation need, a recorded creation timestamp and state for an identified work item are possible base inputs. Validate them against supplied responses and metadata. `LOCAL_IsOpen` applies an approved workflow mapping; `LOCAL_AgeDays` calculates elapsed UTC days from creation to the declared observation instant. These are local model outputs, not Azure WorkItems properties. Scope membership, accepted-nonduplicate eligibility and classification above an approved threshold also require explicit local rules. Blank or unmapped inputs remain unknown, not conveniently closed or ineligible.

Only then can classified counts over a fixed eligible cohort form a derived share. The percentage is arithmetic; the indicator interprets it for an action under a justified local rule. “Investigate this scoped queue” is a bounded application. “Customers are safer” requires different outcome evidence. Correct arithmetic cannot bridge that gap. Attempt to invalidate your interpretation: could missing timestamps silently remove eligible items, incomplete duplicate dispositions change the count, or absent affected-user evidence undermine the proposed conclusion? State the source or inventory check that could overturn it, and its owner.

**Worked illustration only — fictional arithmetic, not organizational evidence:** a frozen inventory contains eight required gate checks. Six have current reviewed evidence with a recorded disposition, giving the approved calculation `100 * 6 / 8 = 75%` evidence completeness. One of those reviewed records documents a failed gate; two checks lack qualifying evidence. The useful application is to request the missing records and escalate the failure separately. Evidence completeness is not the percentage of correct product functionality or proof of readiness. If eight merely counts currently linked checks rather than the full required inventory, even this completeness rate loses its denominator authority.

Keep Availability separate from EvidenceStatus in M04. A register label such as Direct describes possible source support. It does not prove access, a received export, complete inventory or reconciliation in this project. Missing required evidence remains Not Measured with blank unknown results and an owned request. Not Applicable needs a reviewed scope reason, not a missing file. A usable qualified claim may be Conditional/proxy, with limitations explaining its boundary.

Select ten distinct exact register identities for at least three needs, including affected people. Use each candidate only where its question fits; reject a readily extracted candidate that cannot responsibly change the owner's choice. Explain base inputs, local derivation, interpretation and a validity threat in the accompanying note, not new matrix columns. These provisional rows become the completed contracts in 4.3. Review whether the indicator served its decision, preserving prior references when you change a definition rather than rewriting history to protect a favorable number.

A supported bounded indicator leads to Accessible audience versions, then Observed task review. topics.title: The measure contract

prediction.prompt: Two teams use the same metric name, but one includes items created during a month and the other takes all open items at one observation instant. Predict whether a shared label is enough for a comparison, and name the contract fields you would inspect.

topics.lecture_markdown:
### Publish a definition before a judgment

“Dear Evidence Desk: our two teams report the same metric name but different denominators. Management wants a ranking, and someone says ISO requires 95%. Can we publish first and explain later?”

A shared label is not a shared measurement contract. Write what one observation represents: an item at an instant, a frozen requirement, or an execution attempt. Define eligibility, the inventory authority and the UTC membership clock. A creation interval and a snapshot of all open items answer different questions even when both are called “monthly quality.” GrainCohort and PeriodUTC must expose that difference before you compare results.

Define populations, not spreadsheet cell addresses. For a share, the numerator is a subset of the declared eligible denominator. Keep required-but-unlinked units in inventory-based denominators, and preserve missingness and reviewed exclusion rules. Link rows cannot establish the full requirement inventory; attempts are not planned points. Do not force durations into a count ratio: define their input timestamps, aggregation and units. For a difference measure, state both group populations and denominators. Use the selected register's actual operational definition.

Three conditions need different treatment. A verified complete applicable cohort with no eligible opportunities supports count zero and an N/A rate with the empty-cohort reason visible. An absent required inventory supports neither count zero nor a percentage: leave the result unknown, record Not Measured and name the obtain/reconcile action. A reviewed out-of-scope information need can justify Not Applicable. None means automatic success. A favorable formula cannot substitute for evidence of the population.

**Worked illustration only — fictional arithmetic, not organizational evidence:** the earlier twelve-item cohort contains three aged items, giving 25%. A screen filter retains the same three aged items but only six eligible items, giving `100 * 3 / 6 = 50%`. No time passes. The denominator changes, so this is a changed-cohort question, not an aging trend or proof a team performed worse. Preserve both scope references and state noncomparability; match rules prospectively before interpreting change.

Complete the source and authority agreement. SourceRef holds controlled export/metadata/response references, transformation versions, expected refresh and latest reconciled extraction evidence. ReviewCadence instead asks when the contract and indicator should be reconsidered. Fresh data cannot validate an unjustified trigger. ThresholdRationale needs a real local decision/risk basis, approver reference and reassessment date, or an explicit pending blocker. Public standard descriptions do not establish a universal 95% QA target. Changing the threshold after seeing the result is not a defensible validity review.

Compare matched service-level contexts only with stated risk, workflow, size, exposure and instrumentation limits. Bugs and elapsed PR time are not individual productivity scores; changing proxies does not repair attribution. Use evidence to investigate process constraints, not make a people league table. Decide whether to publish, qualify or hold a bounded measurement, keeping software-release decisions separate.

Finish the same ten-contract pack, reconcile two authentic contracts at their actual grain and update the existing audience versions. A supported finding still needs usable text and keyboard access plus real M16 observations. Keep old and repaired references when a reader task fails. An authorized reviewer must accept each individual evidence gate: a complete worksheet or passed quiz cannot self-certify source competence, usability or ISO conformity.

steps.title: Complete the same ten contracts using the field guide
steps.instructions:
Reopen Metric Contract (M04) in qa_matrices_governance.xlsx. Preserve the same ten selected rows. Use the complete field-by-field guide below. Record actual contract/source review versions in SourceRef or Limitations, never a new Version column. Complete fields from supplied references, not inferred approvals.

| Exact column | What to enter and how to check it |
|---|---|
| `MetricId` | Exact register ID. Select ten distinct measures here; one contract per declared need/cohort. Retain intended grain if later courses reuse a metric. |
| `Domain` | Copy register domain. A domain label is not proof that the domain is comprehensively measured. |
| `MetricName` | Copy register name, not a newly invented composite quality score. |
| `InformationNeed` | M02 NeedId plus the decision question. Confirm the owner can take the stated action. |
| `FormulaDefinition` | Register operational definition adapted explicitly to local scope; include zero-denominator N/A. For durations, define aggregation/unit; for difference measures define both groups. |
| `GrainCohort` | Unit/key, service/context, fixed eligibility and denominator inventory. Keep required-but-unlinked units visible. |
| `Numerator` | Define eligible contributing population or duration/difference inputs. For QA058, state elapsed-time inputs rather than inventing a numerator count. |
| `Denominator` | Define eligible opportunities, exposure or aggregation population. Where no ratio applies, write “not a ratio” and the relevant population; a difference measure needs both group denominators. |
| `PeriodUTC` | Actual agreed boundaries/instant and membership timestamp. “Monthly” alone fails this check. |
| `Exclusions` | Declared rule and visible counts/reasons when supplied; use “unknown; evidence pending” rather than 0 for absent evidence. Unknown outcomes are not passes. |
| `Owner` | Named authorized action owner or approved named-role assignment. Include collection/remediation ownership in the gap note if different. |
| `ThresholdRationale` | Local decision/risk basis, approval reference and review date, or an explicit pending blocker. No universal ISO target assertion. |
| `ReviewCadence` | Frequency of contract/indicator review and next scheduled review. Distinguish this from data refresh. |
| `Availability` | Register potential capability plus local qualification; no implied connection. Direct, Conditional/proxy and Supplementary describe capability, not observed success. |
| `EvidenceStatus` | Measured, Conditional/proxy, Not Measured or justified Not Applicable; state evidence adequacy/validity decision in Limitations. Failure outcome does not automatically mean Not Measured. |
| `SourceRef` | Exact controlled export/metadata/response reference, query/operation design, source keys evidence attachment, source/transform version, refresh schedule and last reconciled extraction timestamp. If unavailable, state that explicitly. Never credentials. |
| `Limitations` | Missingness, selection, retention, uncertainty, applicability justification, local modeled-field rules, comparison constraints and owned next action. Empty text is not a claim of no uncertainty. |

**Selection scaffold tied to information needs, not additional domain lessons:** QA001 can support an objective-evidence funding decision but needs an approved objective inventory; QA002 supports requesting gate records with dispositions separate; QA008 needs a distinct frozen requirement inventory; QA009 needs a distinct planned-point inventory; QA010 concerns published attempts, not total planned scope; QA020 concerns an observed aged queue, not customer safety; QA050 requires matched group task observations and is N/A if either group denominator is zero; QA055 requires a locally agreed required-field opportunity inventory; QA058 requires a last successfully reconciled extraction, otherwise Not Measured; QA059 requires row-key/provenance evidence, not just filenames. Each candidate remains a local selection from the register, not a full measurement program or a universal ten-metric requirement. Other register choices must retain their own formulas and limitations.

Verify numerator subset of denominator for shares, not durations or difference measures. For nonratios specify relevant aggregation population; for differences specify both groups. Resolve one eligibility decision from the actual approved mapping yourself, cite the rule, and only then compare to the controlled reference. Unknown source fields remain unknown.

steps.title: Repair three rehearsal faults without rewriting observations
steps.instructions:
On a separate rehearsal draft of these same rows, retain before/after text for: zero denominator displayed as success; absent required evidence marked Measured; unsupported ISO target or unmatched-cohort comparison. Repair FormulaDefinition, EvidenceStatus, ThresholdRationale, GrainCohort and/or Limitations as applicable. Commit your repair first. Use the condition table to distinguish evidence, population, numeric presentation and owned next action. Label rehearsal faults separately; do not call them observed dataset faults unless they actually occurred.

| Condition | Numeric presentation | Evidence/applicability decision | Owned action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Applicable contract, complete verified cohort, eligible count zero | Rate N/A; count 0; verified empty-cohort reason | Measured evidence may establish the empty count; do not label a 100% pass | Review at the next declared observation |
| Applicable contract, required inventory absent | Result blank; “Not Measured”; no asserted zero | Availability may be Direct; local evidence remains Not Measured | Obtain and reconcile inventory through named owner |
| Information need outside reviewed scope | No invented result; documented scope rationale | Not Applicable only with reviewer/owner justification | Retain decision and review when scope changes |

A locally approved review/escalation rule is appropriate when no numeric trigger is justified; no invented ISO 95% authority. ReviewCadence governs reconsidering the contract/indicator. SourceRef governs expected refresh and last successful reconciliation. Preserve old rules for a prospective change. Compare only matched service-level risk/workflow/size/exposure/instrumentation contexts; prohibit people rankings by bugs, points or elapsed PR time. Write a publish/qualify/hold recommendation for the bounded measurement, not product release.

steps.title: Update the audience artifacts and retest access

topics.title: Access and source selection

prediction.prompt: Predict before discussion: an approved analyst can sign in on a desktop, but the intended refresh host and workbook recipients have not been reviewed. What may the analyst record now, and what must remain on hold?

topics.lecture_markdown:
## A working login is only one fact

“Dear Evidence Desk: I can see our bugs in Boards, but the report developer cannot refresh the workbook. I offered my token and filtered it to my Area Path. Is that the sensible shortcut?”

**Evidence Desk reply.** Choose the evidence object before you choose the identity. You need an access decision that survives a change of recipient, a disappearing filter and a different refresh host. A working login answers none of those questions by itself.

Start by writing the reporting purpose in ordinary language. “Current work-item state,” “retained work-item changes” and “published test attempt” describe different objects. A current item has project/item grain. A revision needs project/item/revision grain. An execution result needs project/run/result-attempt context. You cannot repair a wrong source choice by renaming its columns. Analytics Views and the Power BI connector provide flat Boards work items and periodic history, not every transition, hierarchy, pipeline execution or test attempt. Analytics is a copied reporting store, not a real-time mirror.

**Source-backed conceptual comparison, not a live observation.** Suppose your decision needs current in-scope work-item states. Released Boards WorkItems is a candidate, subject to metadata and access checks. If your decision instead needs published failures in a named run, documented Test Runs/Results REST is the relevant execution route, subject to publication, scope, permissions and retention checks. A Test Case work item with State = Ready describes a definition; it does not establish an attempt with Outcome = Passed. No available execution records may mean evidence is unavailable, not that no failures occurred.

For Azure DevOps Services reporting, validate the supported Entra Organizational account route in the actual reporting client. Select its supported authentication option and sign in through its credential interface. Keep credentials out of M expressions, cells, URLs, source files, screenshots, logs and submissions. Then validate the intended recipients and refresh environment separately. Desktop authentication is not proof that unattended refresh will work. Approved managed identity or service-principal automation is conditional on the actual client and environment supporting it. Server requires validation of its own collection, installed Analytics, identity, version and client behavior; do not transplant a Services assumption.

If the owner approves a PAT fallback, use only the minimum documented scopes required by the selected operations, a short lifetime, approved storage, rotation and revocation. If a secret has already been exposed, remove it from the artifact and follow the responsible owner's revocation or rotation process. Masking one screenshot does not revoke the credential or remove other copies. Your evidence describes the repair, never the secret.

Finally ask whether the recipient could receive the rows if the Area Path filter vanished. Analytics does not enforce Area Path security. A filter selects records and may support minimization; it cannot grant authorization. Record approved source/project, recipient restrictions, identity/client/refresh boundary and the named approval or action owner in M05 PermissionDecision and its linked record. Reporting access is not a promise of test-authoring or management entitlement. On the authentic export route, review the supplier's provenance and approval but say “export review,” not “connected.” Unknown retention and unresolved approval remain visible. An honest Not Measured hold protects the next reviewer from mistaking a plan for an observed source.

topics.lecture_markdown:
## The source contract comes before the friendly label

“Dear Evidence Desk: I copied an endpoint from an old sample, asked WIQL for states, and guessed a pull-request Analytics entity. The three URLs look convincing. Which should I trust?”

**Evidence Desk reply.** Trust the request whose method, version, response shape and native fields you can show in saved evidence. Slashes and familiar column names are not provenance.

For an OData source, inspect the chosen endpoint's actual $metadata XML. Find EntitySet Name="WorkItems", follow its entity type, and check each selected property's name and type. Save the version and environment provenance. Released v2.0 supplies a Boards reporting contract; test and pipeline Analytics need an appropriate approved preview version and actual metadata validation. A remembered property from another environment is not confirmed here. If a preview contract is unsuitable or unverified, hold it or use a documented REST alternative. Do not invent an Analytics pull-request entity.

Write a credential-free query definition with method, encoded organization/project placeholders, API version, selected properties or body, filters, intended grain and expected response shape. The approved REST examples use api-version=7.1; they do not assert that it is the newest version or supported by every Server installation. For Analytics, use a filter such as WorkItems?$filter=WorkItemId eq {id}; blocked key addressing WorkItems({id}) is not an interchangeable spelling. Placeholder URLs are designs, not connections.

WIQL separates selection from acquisition. POST /_apis/wit/wiql with a query body selects references and IDs. Retrieve current fields with the documented list or batch operation, at most 200 IDs per request. Retrieve retained revisions separately with GET /_apis/wit/workitems/{id}/revisions. Selecting System.State in a WIQL query does not make its reference response a state-history extract. Keep the distinct purposes and contracts in cumulative M05. Inspect each operation's actual response container rather than forcing every JSON response into one wrapper.

**Bounded structural illustration only, not tenant data.** The approved abbreviated XML shows WorkItemId as Edm.Int32 and Title and State as Edm.String. It omits entity-set declarations and other structure, so it cannot validate a real environment. The approved tiny current-response illustration is {"value":[{"id":101,"rev":2,"fields":{"System.Id":101,"System.State":"Active"}}]}. Here value[n].id can feed LOCAL_WorkItemCurrent.LOCAL_WorkItemId; value[n].fields['System.State'] can feed LOCAL_WorkItemCurrent.LOCAL_State. The n notation describes an array position locally, not a native property. The returned rev is one object's revision number, not a sequence of historical records. The ID is an identifier, not a quantity to sum.

In M06, SourceField names the verified native property or response path; TargetTable and TargetField name your staging destination. LOCAL names are explicitly local, not Azure properties. If you introduce LOCAL_ProjectContext, declare the approved query context as its source, not a returned native field. Current keys combine project and item ID; revision keys combine project, item ID and revision. OData State and REST fields['System.State'] require different source-specific paths even when they feed similarly named targets.

Document the response container, transformation, type and missingness rule. Preserve absent state as blank/null and flag it; never manufacture Passed. Use N/A — not a time field for non-time mappings and map timestamps only when actually verified. Owner and EvidenceRef make the trace accountable. Your acceptance test is simple: another authorized reader must locate the source value and reproduce its target under the declared rule. Without authentic XML or JSON, you can practice the design, but authentic validation remains Not Measured.

topics.lecture_markdown:
## A page is not a population

“Dear Evidence Desk: every request returned HTTP 200. The exported row count even matches our expected count. Why does the reviewer still want page logs and IDs?”

**Evidence Desk reply.** The last page proves an ending to an available chain. To accept an extract, you also need an independent account of which keys and values belonged in that bounded chain.

For Analytics OData, inspect the value array and @odata.nextLink. Check that a returned destination is approved before sending an authenticated request, then follow the server link until none remains. Do not construct client $top/$skip pages. Retain accepted pages and termination evidence. REST uses operation-specific controls: revisions, test runs, test results and completed PRs have documented offsets; builds and deployment records have documented continuation controls. Environment deployment records use top, not $top. A common JSON format does not imply a common paging protocol.

Selection completeness comes before field delivery. WIQL has a 20,000-result cap and no continuation paging for that cap. Use approved disjoint bounded queries, subdivide any capped partition, test boundary IDs and reconcile the union. A verified lower <= System.Id < upper interval can express nonoverlap, but a guessed ID domain cannot prove project coverage. Then retrieve selected IDs in list/batch requests of at most 200. Test Results has its separate limits: up to 1,000 without details and 200 with details. Freeze the comparison boundary or disclose that changing records make adjacent pages unreliable.

A returned Retry-After is operational evidence to respect, not a reason to append an accepted page twice. PageCount counts accepted data-response pages, not retry attempts. Keep sanitized retry and continuation evidence, never authorization headers. Record retention and publication limits: transport cannot recover records the source no longer retains or never published. On the export route you inspect supplied evidence; you do not claim to have captured live responses.

**Worked arithmetic illustration only, not an organizational result.** At current-item grain in one fixed project, expected IDs are {101,102,103,104}; pages are [101,102] and [102,104]. The approved calculation gives two pages, four raw rows, three distinct IDs, one extra duplicate row and missing key 103. Key 102 has multiplicity two; there are no unexpected keys. Distinct reference coverage is 75%, although raw count agreement is 100%. Equal totals hide a repeated key replacing an absent one. Corrected illustrative pages [101,102] and [103,104] agree only for that fixed current-ID comparison, not for revisions, retained-out history or organizational quality.

Stage raw evidence without replacing source files and apply M06 keys and mappings. Compare expected-minus-extracted, extracted-minus-expected, duplicate multiplicities and required field agreement. Never derive SourceExpectedRows from ExtractRows. C05 local dossier rubric retained verbatim below:

Score each area from **0 to 3**, using these concrete anchors. At least **2 — competent in every area** and all absolute gates are required. The rubric evaluates the dossier, not game points or ISO conformity.

| Area | 0 — absent/unsafe | 1 — developing | 2 — competent | 3 — strong |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Access and source fit | Exposed credential, fabricated access, or wrong object treated as evidence. | Route/purpose stated but approval, recipient boundary or refresh check missing. | Scoped permission decision with named owner; supported route/client and refresh boundary validated or accurately blocked; source fits purpose. | Also tests the Area Path/filter counterexample and records a defensible distribution decision for every required source. |
| Endpoint and schema contract | Invented entity/property or local field claimed native. | Methods/versions mostly right; metadata/JSON path evidence incomplete. | Every used request has correct documented method/version; authentic applicable XML/schema inspected; native paths and LOCAL targets distinguished. | Reviewer can reconstruct requests and explain rejected alternatives, including preview versus released and WIQL versus retrieval. |
| Paging and partition coverage | First successful page declared complete or unsupported universal pager. | Some pages logged, but termination, limits or partition boundaries untested. | Operation-specific controls/limits observed; consumed chain or disjoint partitions demonstrated; retries and retention recorded safely. | Independent boundary/union checks and retained failed/corrected chains make omissions and repeats reproducible. |
| Reconciliation and row evidence | Expected equals extracted by definition; fabricated IDs/values or hidden missingness. | Counts supplied without proper keys, same-grain reference, or discrepancy actions. | Independent same-grain inventory; raw/distinct/duplicate/missing/unexpected checks and required field agreement; row traces; owned unresolved gaps. | Another reviewer reproduces key sets and transforms, including all scope revisions and source-backed dispositions, from the evidence. |
| Reproducibility and truthful communication | False live claim, secret-bearing submission or missing required evidence concealed. | Artifacts exist but hashes, provenance, accessible exports or bounded conclusion incomplete. | Exact-template matrices, query/hash inputs, usable authorized evidence references, text/CSV access, no credentials, and correct live/export/blocked disposition. | Clear acceptance boundary and actionable next steps; a keyboard/text-only reviewer can inspect every material gate without color or mouse dependence. |

**Absolute gates override the rubric and test averages.** No credentials exposed; no fabricated authentic records or connection; no unsupported native entity/field claims; same-grain controlled-source reconciliation exact or honestly blocked; every required missing source/check visible with a named action owner; keyboard/text review and accessible long-format exports available. A breach requires correction, not a higher score elsewhere. A design-only dossier can receive feedback but cannot be called an authenticated/reconciled authentic build. Instructor feedback and revision are available without shame or penalty for learning.

topics.lecture_markdown:
### Reader’s dilemma

“Dear Evidence Desk: I joined bugs, tests, and deployments into one table. Now a bug has twelve rows and a deployment has six. The dashboard looks busy, which may be its most accurate feature. How do I recover the counts?”

### Evidence Desk reply

Begin by completing this sentence for every table: “One row asserts ___.” If the blank contains two different events, split the table. A work-item revision records one item's edit version; a daily snapshot records its state at an observation date. Neither is a test attempt. Keep current work items separately so today's description cannot silently overwrite the past. The approved source references describe Boards history and published execution records; our fact-table names are local design choices, not Azure endpoint names.

Declare a composite business key before loading. Include project context wherever source identifiers need it. Preserve test attempts at project/run/result-attempt grain; verify attempt identity from the supplied provenance rather than inventing an `AttemptNumber` property. Pipeline runs stay at run grain. Logical deployments require a governed service/production-event identity; several jobs or commits can describe one event. Incidents require their own incident identity and supplementary evidence. A build is not a deployment; a bug is not an incident.

Dimensions describe these facts: date, project/team, service, type/state, severity, test/configuration, pipeline, and environment. Give each dimension a unique local key and check that every populated foreign key resolves. Use explicit one-to-many relationships from dimensions to facts; avoid an automatic fact-to-fact join merely because both tables contain an item identifier. A join can be syntactically correct and numerically destructive.

For requirements and tests, preserve the full frozen requirement inventory first. Build unique relationship pairs separately; retain unlinked requirements with blank test/result keys. For commits and deployments, keep unique commit-event pairs, but count deployments from the unique event fact, not the bridge. Failed linked evidence remains evidence, not readiness.

Test the repair with keys and drillthrough, not an average divisor. Compare the event key set before and after relationship traversal. If a deployment becomes six rows, locate the six relationships and explain each; do not divide every future count by six. Multiplicity is a property of relationships, not a discount coupon attached to the database.

### Put the row assertion to work

You recover a count by restoring its identity, not by making the total smaller. Begin your model dictionary with a sentence for each table, then name the source-supported key that makes that sentence testable. Use the project context wherever an identifier's uniqueness depends on it. A revision number belongs to an item's history; an observation date belongs to a snapshot. Omitting either consequential component can silently combine records that make different assertions.

**Conceptual example — relationships are not events.** Imagine reviewing a production event with several legitimate commit links. You need all those links to explain the event's lineage, but you need only its governed event identity to count it. Removing every multi-link event would conceal valid delivery history. Retaining repeat delivery of the same pair would add no new relationship. Keep the raw capture available and distinguish that duplicate pair from genuinely different links in the modeled bridge.

In Power BI, look at relationship cardinality before accepting a visual. A dimension must have unique keys, and populated foreign keys must resolve. Single-direction dimension-to-fact filtering gives you an inspectable route without an unexplained fact-to-fact shortcut. Test the route using the actual qualifying composite fact keys before and after traversal. Equal totals alone can conceal a lost key and an unexpected replacement.

Start requirements from the frozen inventory, not from results. You can document valid failed evidence while still having incomplete requirements elsewhere. Keep absent keys blank and retain their owners. If the required source is unavailable, your accurate design can earn formative feedback, but it cannot establish an authentic measured count. The two aggregate proofs below belong to this same cumulative model and will later be reproduced at the identical scope.

### Reader’s dilemma

“Dear Evidence Desk: the dashboard says this bug took two days, but the team says five. It was resolved, reopened, and closed; our workflow also changed last month. Which clock is telling the truth?”

### Evidence Desk reply

A timestamp is an observation; its meaning is a contract. First identify the source event and the local rule that makes it a start or finish. “Resolved” might mean a proposed fix awaiting verification, not accepted closure. Ask the process owner to approve a dated mapping for each process, work-item type, and state. Record when that interpretation applied. Applying today's map to last month's revisions can move a completion boundary without changing a single source record.

Next order revisions by the declared item/revision identity and inspect state changes. A revision can edit a title without changing state. Snapshots answer what was observed on a date, not how many changes happened between dates. If an item completes, reactivates, and completes again, final elapsed resolution uses the agreed final closure within the observation rule, including the reopened interval. If it remains active at cutoff, retain its ongoing history as censored rather than inventing closure at refresh time.

Normalize event timestamps to UTC for storage and comparisons. Preserve the original offset or clock evidence in lineage. State the reporting window's timezone and use explicit inclusive-start/exclusive-end boundaries. Displaying UTC in a local timezone changes presentation, not elapsed duration. Elapsed hours include nights and weekends. Working time needs a documented calendar, holidays, pause rules, and approval; neither elapsed nor working time measures staff effort automatically. Reject negative intervals and investigate parsing or source semantics instead of taking an absolute value.

Keep custom-field meaning versioned too. If a severity scale or service assignment changed, explain which definition the historical row uses; do not interpret an old code using an unrecorded new dictionary. A field name alone does not supply its historical meaning.

Finally, apply the same discipline to links. A test linked today may have been linked after release. A dated frozen capture or retained link history can support a bounded past claim; a current export cannot. The correct answer may be “observed now; earlier linkage unknown.” That sentence is less decorative than a green matrix cell, but considerably more durable.

### Put the dated interpretation to work

You need two layers of evidence: the recorded history and the approved meaning that applied when each event occurred. Do not alter the raw state text to repair the interpretation. In your local model, a derived category or endpoint points back to its native timestamp and state inputs, its effective process map, and its approved selection rule. Keep these derivations visible in M06 rather than presenting their names as native Azure properties.

**Conceptual example — the boundary belongs to one version.** Consider two adjacent approved mappings for the same process, type and state. When an event falls exactly at their shared boundary, the old interval excludes it and the new interval includes it. That is why you test the half-open predicate and count map matches per revision key. No match exposes a missing interpretation; several matches expose conflicting interpretations. Either needs an owner, not an arbitrary dictionary choice.

Use the timeline to explain your endpoint selection in plain language before calculating a duration. Keep title-only edits in reconciliation even when they are not counted as transitions. Then ask whether a later reactivation exists before the declared cutoff. An ongoing record contributes visible ongoing exposure, not a fabricated completed interval. Moving the cutoff may change this disposition without changing any source event.

For your handoff, separate what the source recorded, what the dated approval permits you to derive, and what remains unknown. A timezone label is not a working calendar, and neither is an effort record. The changed-item activity asks you to defend these distinctions yourself; documentation stays open for the technical work, while recall asks for the concepts rather than memorized endpoint syntax.

rounds.prompt: Case 1: Two snapshots show Active at midnight and Completed the next midnight; no revisions are supplied. A: Exactly one transition happened. B: Completion occurred at the second midnight. C: Those are observed states; exact transition time/count is not established.

topics.lecture_markdown:
### Reader’s dilemma

“Dear Evidence Desk: the refresh succeeded this morning, but yesterday's totals changed and two old bugs vanished. Can I mark the data complete because the refresh icon is green?”

### Evidence Desk reply

A successful refresh proves that an operation completed, not that the intended evidence survived. Start with a full extract reconciled against an instructor-controlled source at the same grain and cohort. Save its key set, source/API version, query definition, and metadata. If the reference count is unknown, say so; copying the extract count into the expected-count column is a comparison between a number and its reflection.

Incremental extraction begins only after the source's watermark semantics are validated. A changed timestamp may describe item edits; it is not automatically a complete feed for new daily snapshots, results, or deployments. Each fact needs its own capture rule. Overlap a locally justified window to recapture late or boundary updates, then merge using the declared business key. Replaying the same batch should not multiply facts. Conflicting payloads at one key need deterministic precedence supported by source evidence, or quarantine—not whichever row happened to arrive last.

Do not mistake overlap for a deletion detector. A deleted item, a retained-out attempt, or a delayed update outside the overlap can disappear from the accessible source. Specify whether historical evidence is retained, tombstoned, or unavailable, under the approved retention/access policy. Periodic full reconciliation detects mismatches the incremental path can miss; it does not magically restore unavailable history. Preserve the gap and its decision impact. Published source retention and query behavior must be checked for the environment.

For every refresh, save extraction and completion UTC times, maximum observed source timestamp, API/source version, metadata capture, transformation version, query hash, page/partition counts, and key differences. Maximum timestamp alone is not completeness: a newer record can coexist with missing older records. Preview properties are usable only when the saved environment metadata confirms them.

Finally, reproduce two aggregates from their scoped keys and source rows after refresh. A changed total should have a traceable explanation: new events, corrected payload, mapping change, changed observation window, or disclosed evidence loss. If none is known, stop the claim and assign an investigation owner. The green refresh icon has a job; serving as an expert witness is not it.

### Make the reproduction test inspectable

You demonstrate reproducibility by saving enough controlled inputs and rules for another authorized person to repeat the same comparison. Treat your baseline, incoming batch and replay as separate evidence stages, not separate full assignments. Reference them from cumulative M08 rows and the same QA log. A query hash identifies the saved query definition; it is not a place for credentials, and it does not validate the data by itself.

**Conceptual example — three claims need three proofs.** An actual completion log can establish that extraction ran. Processing the identical input with the same transformation can establish stable modeled keys and payloads. Comparing those keys with an independent same-grain reference can establish reconciliation for that declared cohort. You may have the first two while the third remains unknown. Describe the supported claim and keep the remaining completeness limit visible.

In Power Query, append baseline and incoming data only in staging, then inspect groups at the declared business key. Identical repeated payloads and genuinely different revisions are not the same problem. Conflicting meaning at one key requires supported precedence or quarantine. Save the before-and-after key and payload evidence so a stable chart cannot disguise a nondeterministic choice.

Your later full comparison tests risks outside the overlap, including access and retention changes. It may expose a gap without recovering the missing history. Do not rebuild old states from today's fields or silently delete historical keys to make a comparison look clean. Finally, reuse your original observation-day item and scoped run aggregates at their fixed filters and clock rules. Explain each supported change or stop the affected claim with a named next action. The relationship-review visual is a readable handoff aid, not a release-readiness score.

games.title: Refresh Runbook Sequencer
games.objective: Put reproducibility controls in a defensible order.
games.rules: Untimed, three independent rounds. Each round lists three action cards A/B/C. Type the letters in order, such as B-A-C. Use only those cards; the sequence is not a full platform deployment procedure. Reveal the supplied solution after choosing.

rounds.prompt: Round 1 cards: A = Compare loaded business keys with the controlled expected set. B = Freeze query/source version and capture the full extraction inputs. C = Approve the reconciled baseline or record a blocking gap. Put them in order.

Round 2 cards: A = Upsert overlapping rows using the declared business key and deterministic rule. B = Validate source watermark semantics and define the overlap. C = Compare keys, counts, and replay results before publishing. Put them in order.

Round 3 cards: A = Assign a named owner's next action and block unsupported historical claims. B = Run the scheduled full controlled-source comparison. C = Investigate missing keys against retention/deletion and extraction evidence. Put them in order.

games.scoring: One point per completely correct sequence, 0-3 practice points. Feedback: identify the first action that depends on evidence not yet collected, then replay; no timing score.
games.accessible_alternative: Type a hyphenated sequence, say it aloud, or write the letters. Cards are plain text; no dragging, animation, or sound.

games.title: The Freshness Alarm Desk
games.objective: Choose a bounded response to missing, repeated, or unsupported refresh evidence.
games.rules: Untimed. Choose A/B/C for three independent fictional worked incidents. The objective is a defensible model decision, not the fastest publication. Keep the distinction between extraction success and evidence completeness.

rounds.prompt: Incident 1: Baseline has three unique revision keys. Incoming rows repeat one existing key twice and add one new key. A: Append and publish six rows. B: Deduplicate/upsert to four unique rows and test the key set. C: Delete all existing revisions.

Incident 2: Refresh completed now, but the expected history includes keys missing after source retention. A: Disclose missing history, investigate retention, and prevent unsupported historic claims. B: Mark history complete because refresh is recent. C: Fill missing states from today's item.

Incident 3: A copied preview query selects a property absent from the saved environment metadata. A: Rename a different property until totals look right. B: Claim the property is native because a sample query used it. C: Stop that mapping, record the gap, and revise against validated metadata or an approved documented REST export.

games.scoring: One point per correct action, 0-3 practice points. Feedback: record what remains unknown and who can resolve it; retry without penalty. Games never contribute exam scores.
games.accessible_alternative: Use keyboard letters, text, or spoken choices, one incident at a time. All feedback is textual; no timer, drag-only input, sound, or color is required.

topics.lecture_markdown:
### Reader’s topic dilemma

“Dear Evidence Desk: my plan has 120 test cases and the pipeline published 940 results. My manager wants a single total called ‘tests completed.’ Which number should I use?”

### The Evidence Desk reply

Use neither number until you specify what the noun means. A test identity describes an assertion or procedure. A planned point binds a case to a suite and configuration in an approved plan. A result attempt records an execution. One identity may create several points; one point may generate several attempts. Adding those populations produces a large number, not a defensible total. The 29119 family distinguishes testing concepts, process and documentation; our practical record design is local, not a reproduction of its licensed templates. [9] [36] [37] [38]

Start with the release candidate and its frozen plan. Ask the plan owner to identify the plan version, intended configurations, expected assertions and approval date. Keep every obligation, including one nobody ran. Then open an execution record and establish the tested build or artifact revision, environment, configuration, timing and result identity. A Test Case work item records a definition, not a published execution. Azure's documented result schema provides references that may support this chain, but missing references must be investigated rather than guessed. [21] [47]

Next distinguish the source observation from your interpretation. “Failed” belongs in Outcome; “build reference unavailable” belongs in the evidence review. Put the raw record path and review note in EvidenceRef. Record expected assertions, environment and defect disposition in the referenced test-management brief because the approved matrix has no dedicated columns for them. Do not add a convenient column and later call it native.

Consider a counterexample: the same test title passes on today's build after failing yesterday. A title match does not establish stable identity, identical configuration or the same build. Filling yesterday's blank BuildId from today's green run manufactures provenance. Retain both observations, mark the unresolved comparison, and ask a named owner for the build and environment records.

Finally reconcile keys, not just totals. Importing a response page twice creates duplicate records, not reruns. A genuine rerun requires a separate execution identity. The plan tells you what was owed; provenance tells you what was observed; neither alone tells you the release is safe.

### Apply the distinction yourself

**Conceptual example — not assessed rows.** Suppose you can open a published result but cannot connect it to an approved planned point. Treat the record as an observation with an unresolved relationship, not as evidence that the approved inventory grew. Keep its supported composite identity in publication reconciliation. Keep the plan obligation population separately. When you compare the two, explain the missing mapping in the brief and ask the QA lead for the retained record that would establish it. Do not fabricate a point to make the counts agree.

You can now read M10 as a provenance spine rather than a success scoreboard. Its grain is a planned-point/result-attempt relationship, so even a well-formed row count can exceed either population. An attempt deliberately related to several points needs a reviewed relationship explanation and must count once in attempt measures. Your next lab checkpoint is not a prettier total: it is two independently reconciled key sets and an auditable row-to-source trail. A reviewer needs to distinguish what you observed, what you expected, and which claim the available evidence cannot support.

### Approved source route and LOCAL meanings

Use the following design templates with approved saved responses or authorized access; they are not functioning user endpoints:

```text

GET https://dev.azure.com/{organization}/{project}/_apis/test/runs?api-version=7.1
```

Expand the REST response `value` array at result grain. Native `testRun.id` maps to LOCAL `RunId`; native `id` with project/run context maps to LOCAL `ResultId` such as `project/run/result`. Supported `configuration.id`, `build.id`, `completedDate` and `outcome` map to LOCAL `ConfigurationId`, `BuildId`, `CompletedUTC` and `Outcome`. Supported `testPoint.id` and `testSuite.id` map to LOCAL `PlannedPointId` and `SuiteId` only against the frozen inventory. Missing references stay blank. `testCase.id` may support a reviewed manual `TestId`; `testCaseReferenceId` is not automatically a Test Case work-item ID. Automated identities require a reviewed available method/storage mapping, not title similarity. Native `testCaseRevision` is test metadata, while result `revision` is a result-record update, not a source-code revision or rerun. Native `associatedBugs` is a link, not proof of closure/disposition.

LOCAL `AttemptNumber` is derived from actual executions after extraction deduplication by ordering within test/configuration/build/window using `CompletedUTC` then stable composite identity. LOCAL `InScope`, `EvidenceStatus` and `EvidenceRef` are eligibility/provenance decisions; `ReleaseId`, weights and approvals come from governed inventories. They are not native Azure matrix headers. Validate operation-specific paging and reconcile saved pages at result grain, not action/iteration grain. Supported JaCoCo/Cobertura coverage XML is supplementary build evidence, not REST JSON or Analytics metadata XML. Withhold unsupported claims and name the evidence owner. [12] [22] [46] [47]

topics.lecture_markdown:
### Reader’s topic dilemma

“Dear Evidence Desk: branch coverage is 90%, requirement traceability is lower, and the risk owner still objects. Which percentage should settle the release?”

### The Evidence Desk reply

None should settle it alone. Requirement traceability, planned execution and risk-weighted evidence ask three different questions. Code coverage asks a fourth, narrower question about instrumented code exercise. Their numerators cannot repair one another's denominators. A branch can execute while its business assertion is wrong; an approved failing test can supply traceable evidence without satisfying acceptance. Azure traceability and coverage features support evidence inspection, not a universal release verdict. [21] [22]

Begin with the complete frozen requirement inventory. For QA008, count distinct scoped requirements that have an approved linked test and a valid recorded result under the declared rule. A requirement linked to two tests still contributes at most one to that numerator. Keep unlinked requirements as blank-link rows, and review assertion adequacy separately. Do not make the denominator “requirements with links”: that turns every missing relationship into an invisible success.

Now open the planned-point inventory. QA009 counts points with valid Passed or Failed execution divided by all in-scope points. A retry contributes additional observations but no additional planned obligation. Blocked, skipped, not-run and inconclusive states remain visible and unexecuted for this contract. Preserve raw source outcomes and document local labels rather than assuming every publisher uses identical strings.

For QA013, ask the risk owner to approve objective weights before reviewing outcomes. Normalize repeated RiskId relationships, then count each qualifying objective's weight once. State whether one valid test is enough or a defined set of controls must execute. A valid failure can meet an executed-evidence rule while requiring residual-risk action. Local ordinal priorities are neither probabilities nor an ISO scoring system.

Finally inspect instrumented branch counts only for the named build, tool and eligible code scope. Missing artifacts mean Not Measured. Unsupported or excluded code must be stated, not quietly absorbed into a green percentage. Public testing-process and technique descriptions do not prescribe our weights or thresholds. [36] [38]

The counterexample is simple: repeatedly run two easy tests while leaving the highest-weight objective untouched. Attempt totals rise, but requirement gaps and risk exposure stay. Your next action is to fund the missing evidence, not average four incompatible percentages.

### Apply the distinction yourself

**Conceptual example — not assessed rows.** Imagine an approved requirement has a linked test with a defensible failing result. You can trace the requirement to its assertion and execution while still withholding a recommendation to release. The source `Outcome` stays Failed. The evidence can be Measured under the approved traceability rule. The requirement owner must address the failure, and the risk owner must review any residual-risk implication. Neither changing the status label nor dropping the requirement repairs the product.

In your calculation output, write a numerator key beside its complete frozen denominator before calculating a percentage. Use distinct requirements for QA008, distinct planned points for QA009, and consistent approved objective weights counted once for QA013. LocalPriority may use the approved ordinal Impact times Likelihood model; it is not probability or expected loss. You keep calculation flags outside the exact matrices. Known empty inventories give N/A with counts and reason, whereas absent inventories give Not Measured. A full-inventory Matrix or Excel pivot is useful precisely because unsupported obligations remain available to a keyboard or text-table reader.
