topics.title: Safety

prediction.prompt: A reviewed hazard has a warning assertion but no record that the hazardous state was inhibited. What evidence requirement should the reviewer challenge?

topics.lecture_markdown:
**Your domain dilemma:** “The safety cell is blank. Can we infer safety from a reliable pipeline?”

You are deciding what the supplied hazard evidence supports, not conducting hazardous experiments. Work from a qualified analysis and retained witness records. Your responsibility is to expose the missing mitigation or authority, not manufacture a safety case.

Safety needs a hazard-informed evidence chain. Ask a qualified domain owner what harms can arise from intended use, failures, misuse and interactions with the operating context. Begin with hazard analysis, not a list of test results. A product may execute consistently and still perform a hazardous action correctly according to a poor requirement. Safety is a product-quality characteristic in the approved 2023 model; this course supplies selected evidence instruction, not a safety case.

For each applicable hazard, identify the mitigation objective, required behavior, relevant test conditions and fail-safe or misuse assertions. Record who witnessed the result and which product revision and operating context were used. A test link says where to investigate; it does not establish that the mitigation works. A valid failing witnessed test is valuable evidence of a problem, not a reason to erase the hazard row.

Residual-risk disposition needs an authorized approver with appropriate domain competence. Record the rationale, restrictions and review conditions in the reference, rather than entering “accepted” because the software team wishes to ship. Hazard priority and residual-risk judgment are not an arithmetic ISO conformity score. A dashboard cannot replace specialist analysis or regulatory evidence.

QA048 counts identified applicable hazards with the complete reviewed mitigation/witnessed-test/disposition chain over identified applicable hazards. When several controls address one hazard, collapse relationships to the hazard identity for that denominator. Also review analysis completeness: a complete chain for a narrow inventory may still miss material hazards. In M13 a missing analysis is Not Measured, not Not Applicable. Justified nonapplicability requires documented domain review. A green pipeline is not even a particularly verbose safety argument.

### Conceptual illustration — not submission evidence

**Worked illustration only.** An approved analysis identifies two applicable hazards. One has reviewed mitigation traceability, witnessed relevant tests and an authorized residual-risk disposition; the other lacks a witnessed test. Python gives QA048 100 × 1/2 = **50%**. This is selected evidence coverage, not a safety probability or regulatory clearance.

Counterexample: a fail-safe test confirms a warning appears but never checks that the hazardous actuator is inhibited. The warning assertion may pass while the mitigation remains unverified. The evidence specification needs hazard identity, control/requirement, hazardous condition, expected safe state, witnessed result, revision and qualified residual-risk decision. No safety observations are supplied here.

topics.title: Beneficialness

prediction.prompt: A user submits a booking unaided, but the appointment is wrong. What would you need before calling it useful task success or benefit?

topics.lecture_markdown:
**Your domain dilemma:** “People completed the task. Does that mean using the product benefited them?”

You are deciding who obtained the intended useful outcome in a specified context. Distinguish correct unassisted attempts from verified benefit journeys before aggregating; a completed interface action must not quietly become evidence that somebody benefited.

Completion is an observation; benefit is an outcome defined for specified users and context. A person can complete an application form yet submit incorrect information, need substantial assistance, or receive no useful service. Begin by asking the affected group what intended benefit means, and write the observable outcome rule before collecting task data. Beneficialness belongs to the 2023 quality-in-use model, distinct from the product interaction-capability page.

QA049 asks whether representative eligible attempts were completed correctly without assistance. Preserve attempt identity, repeat-attempt rule, correctness, assistance and critical-error observations. QA051 asks whether eligible journeys attained the specified beneficial outcome. A loading page is not an outcome, and an unassisted completion is not necessarily the promised benefit. Do not combine task attempts and longer journeys into one denominator.

Look for unequal access to benefit. QA050 compares matched task-success percentages across declared access-needs and reference groups, showing both group counts. If either denominator is zero, the gap is N/A. Different tasks or contexts cannot support a simple access-gap interpretation. Use privacy-safe groups and consented observations; small cohorts can both expose participants and produce unstable estimates.

Use M16 for task/access checks and M13 for the benefit evidence requirements. Azure can hold a finding or a reference, but it cannot supply participant representation or verified benefits without an actual study or outcome source. State selection, nonresponse and context limitations. When only convenience-sample task observations exist, a broader population-benefit claim is Conditional/proxy. Let the result remain modest: “these observed attempts met this criterion.” That sentence can guide useful action without borrowing confidence from people you never observed.

### Conceptual illustration — not submission evidence

**Worked illustration only.** Eight eligible observed attempts include five correct unassisted completions. Python gives QA049 100 × 5/8 = **62.5%**. This is not QA051 beneficial-outcome attainment unless the separately declared outcome was also observed at journey grain.

Counterexample: a participant submits a booking without assistance, but it is for the wrong appointment and provides no intended service. The submission is not correct task success or verified benefit. Evidence specification: retain correctness and assistance rules, task/journey keys, representative cohort/context, privacy-safe observations and a verified outcome record. Without actual study data, no measured user-benefit claim can be issued.

steps.title: Commit the calculation and adequacy decisions

QA049 = 100 × correct unassisted eligible task attempts / eligible task attempts. QA050 compares task-success percentages of the declared access-needs and reference groups only at matched task/context, with both group counts; either zero denominator makes the gap N/A. QA051 = 100 × eligible journeys attaining the separately specified verified beneficial outcome / eligible journeys. topics.title: Freedom from risk

prediction.prompt: A reporting channel has no validated events, but affected users cannot use it. What competing explanation and evidence need must remain visible?

topics.lecture_markdown:
**Your domain dilemma:** “No harm was reported. Can quality-in-use freedom from risk be green?”

You are deciding whether observed impact and exposure support a bounded risk statement. Inspect who could report and how events were validated; silence from an inaccessible reporting channel cannot answer what happened to affected users.

Recorded harm depends on exposure, detection and validation. No report may mean no event, few exposed users, a narrow reporting channel, or people unable to report. Begin with the contexts of use and relevant economic, environmental/societal, health and human-life exposures. Obtain qualified review of category applicability and consequence; do not infer it from a blank incident register. Freedom from risk belongs to quality-in-use, while the Safety page examined the product hazard-control chain. The perspectives relate but are not substitutes.

Define an event-validation rule and an exposure unit before counting. QA052 uses distinct validated user-impacting events per one thousand eligible journeys or user-hours, choosing one unit consistently. Retain category and severity separately. Two reports about one event are not necessarily two events; one event with multiple consequences needs declared category attribution. Do not add unlike exposure units or assume every customer harm becomes an Azure bug.

Use supplementary risk and incident evidence plus approved exposure telemetry. Review detection coverage, time window and who might be absent from the reporting channel. Economic loss estimates and health or environmental consequences need appropriate specialist evidence, not improvised spreadsheet probabilities. Absence of validated events cannot establish absence of risk.

M15 can preserve relevant reviewed risk-control objectives, while M13 records the quality-in-use information need and adequacy limits. Reference an explicit link from the use context to the objective; do not copy product safety coverage into a risk-event rate. If exposure or validation evidence is missing, mark QA052 Not Measured. Assign acquisition and mitigation ownership even when the conclusion is inconclusive. Uncertainty is a reason to inspect the reporting route, not to paint over it.

### Conceptual illustration — not submission evidence

**Worked illustration only.** To illustrate an evidence review rather than QA052, suppose three predeclared use-context risk categories require specialist review and only two have reviewed evidence. Python gives 100 × 2/3 = **66.67% reviewed-category coverage**. This instructor-defined illustration is not a selected new metric, not the QA052 event rate and not a probability of safety.

For QA052 the bounded proof is an evidence specification: validated distinct event keys, risk category/severity, consistent eligible exposure units, observation window, reporting/detection coverage and specialist review. Counterexample: zero reports from a portal that affected users cannot access. The missing channel prevents a “no harm” inference even if the stored count is zero.

visual.trace_prompt: Trace Use-context outcomes → Supplementary sources → Scope and distinct grain → Status versus adequacy. Explain why a reviewed M15 control is only a related input, not a risk-event outcome.
visual.text_equivalent:
Approved domain need branches into Product assertions for product quality and Use-context outcomes for quality in use. Product assertions select configured Azure references and relevant Supplementary sources; Use-context outcomes require Supplementary sources containing actual use evidence. Both source paths reach Scope and distinct grain: validate permissions, source keys, frozen inventories, windows and the correct population. Reconciled or explicitly qualified scope reaches Status versus adequacy: a valid failure can be Measured, yet inadequate for a favorable claim; missing observation is not a pass. Adequacy review leads either to a Bounded domain claim or an Owned evidence gap. The gap feeds back to the Approved domain need through acquisition or claim narrowing. No arrow from a green pipeline directly establishes security, safety or user benefit.

Relationship observation: Controls inform the use-context analysis; actual validated events and consistently measured exposure supply the outcome rate. Missing detection/exposure follows Owned evidence gap, not a direct control-to-no-harm claim.

topics.title: Acceptability

prediction.prompt: An in-product survey excludes people who stopped using the service, while a rule review is from an older jurisdiction. What two limits must a release note disclose?

topics.lecture_markdown:
**Your domain dilemma:** “Most survey respondents trust the product. Can we say users accept it and compliance is complete?”

You are deciding what respondents’ experience and current rule evidence permit you to say. Hold willingness, trust and authoritative applicability apart; neither agreeable answers nor a closed ticket authorizes a universal acceptance or compliance conclusion.

Acceptability needs scoped experience, trustworthiness and applicable-rule evidence, not a single agreeable percentage. Begin with the target users, context, release and time window. Write the survey or interview instrument and response rule before looking at answers. QA053 records eligible respondents’ willingness to continue use under that rule, while trust-item distributions stay visible separately. The approved quality-in-use model supplies the domain; the survey is an original local operational method, not an ISO questionnaire.

Retain the sample frame, invitations, response count and nonresponse/adoption context. People who stopped using the product may be missing from an in-product survey. A high respondent rate can coexist with low participation or serious distrust in a subgroup. Do not turn respondents into “all users” or collapse several trust questions into an unapproved composite. Qualitative interviews can explain an issue but require their own selection and interpretation limits.

Applicable compliance evidence needs authoritative applicability determination and qualified assessment. QA054 asks whether applicable rule/requirement records have current owner-reviewed evidence and responsible dispositions. A closed Boards item is not that assessment; evidence coverage is not legal compliance or organizational conformity. Preserve rule identity, source authority, scope and review date in the reference, with missing evidence explicitly marked.

In M13 keep experience/trust and rule-review requirements separate. Link M09 to required rule assertions when appropriate, while keeping broader review artifacts distinct. Assign nonresponse investigation or missing qualified review to an accountable owner. A defensible conclusion may be “respondents expressed willingness, with unobserved nonrespondents and unresolved rule evidence.” It is less convenient than “accepted and compliant,” and considerably more useful for deciding what to examine next.

### Conceptual illustration — not submission evidence

**Worked illustration only.** Ten eligible target users are invited; four respond and three meet the predeclared willingness rule. Python gives QA053 respondent acceptance 100 × 3/4 = **75%** and response share 100 × 4/10 = **40%**. The latter is context for interpretation, not a new selected ISO metric. Neither establishes willingness among the six nonrespondents; keep trust responses separately.

Counterexample: a rule-related work item is closed but its referenced legal assessment is stale and applies to another jurisdiction. The closure cannot complete QA054’s current applicable-rule evidence. Retain authoritative scope determination, current qualified review and responsible disposition; a survey cannot replace them.

submission:
## Matrix-based performance deliverable — C10-PERF-01

### Decision brief and required submission

Prepare a twelve-domain evidence map for the instructor-controlled candidate: “Which product-quality and quality-in-use claims can this evidence support, what remains unmeasured, and what should each owner do before the decision?” No synthetic overall quality/ISO score and no live-connection claim are permitted. If authentic source prerequisites are unavailable, submit a clearly labelled preparation pack; assessed performance remains blocked until the instructor supplies and reconciles the authentic sources.

1. Deliver the cumulatively populated M05 Source Capability, M09 Requirements Test, M13 Quality Evidence, M14 Compatibility Variants, M15 Threat Hazard and M16 Accessible Review sheets in their named workbooks. M13 must preserve **all twelve distinct domains**, with at least one approved evidence requirement per domain and expanded rows for distinct sources/decisions as needed. Missing required areas remain Not Measured or Conditional/proxy; Not Applicable requires qualified applicability review, not missing equipment. Each requirement has method, grain/cohort, owner, review date, source or acquisition plan, adequacy reasoning and GapAction.
2. Attach frozen inventories, approved scope/window, XML metadata/JSON source provenance or authentic-export manifests, local field mappings and row-key evidence chains. Reconcile required functional/rule requirements, required combination/variant identities, threat-control objectives, distinct hazards and access checks against their full inventories. Separately reconcile any measured requests, intervals, findings, attempts, journeys, respondents and exposure units; do not count relationship rows as populations. Demonstrate a valid failing result that is Measured and a missing required result that is Not Measured, using authentic records when they exist; otherwise show the handling rule and explicitly say the record is unavailable.
3. For selected measured register items, submit reproducible calculation attachments with numerator/denominator or units, UTC period, exclusions, source keys and validity decisions. Show zero-denominator N/A handling. Leave unavailable numbers blank/N/A with reason, not inferred zero. The small worked illustrations in this course are excluded from organizational calculations.
4. Record a **25023-to-2023 gap review in M13 EvidenceAdequacy/GapAction and its EvidenceRef attachment**, not a new matrix. For each relevant selected measure/domain, identify the 2016 conceptual mapping, the 2023 domain, what public approval establishes, what licensed-text review is missing, and a qualified review owner. Prioritize changed domain context such as Flexibility and Safety, and the distinct 25019 quality-in-use model. Copied approval is not proof of full licensed-text coverage.
5. Submit accessible long-format exports of each used sheet with exact headers and text status/outcome labels, plus a 250–350-word plain-text decision note naming two strongest bounded claims, two material gaps, one counterexample to a green-cell inference and owned next actions. Demonstrate keyboard access to the sheets and source summaries without revealing sensitive participant/security detail. No new dashboard implementation is required in this course.

### Acceptance gates: these override average marks

- **Truth:** no fabricated user/production findings, witness/approval, source field or live integration. Illustrations are labelled and excluded from assessed authentic calculations. No credentials or unauthorized raw export access.
- **Inventory and grain:** all twelve domains retained; required unlinked/unobserved inventory members retained; zero unexplained missing/extra identities or unintended duplicate keys; bridges, reruns and multi-control hazard relationships reconciled at the right distinct identity. Instructor-known unresolved evidence gaps must remain disclosed, not misreported as source-complete.
- **Evidence and action:** every claim resolves to valid row-level evidence and bounded adequacy or an explicit missing-source state; valid failures remain failures, not missingness; missing values never pass. Every material gap has Owner, GapAction and ReviewDate; risk acceptance has qualified authority where required.
- **Calculation and access:** all submitted totals reproduce against controlled sources, denominators/exclusions survive filters, zero denominator is N/A, long-format tables retain text meaning and keyboard access, and sensitive data remain restricted. A screenshot alone fails reproducibility.

### Instructor rubric

Score each area 0–3; a 2 is competent and is required in **every** area. Passing also requires all acceptance gates. Level 3 does not compensate for a level 1 elsewhere. Review actual rows and attachments, not the number of green cells.

| Area | 3 — Strong | 2 — Competent | 1 — Developing | 0 — Not demonstrated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Domain evidence fit and applicability | All twelve domains have justified specific evidence requirements, counterexamples and qualified applicability | All twelve retained; selected methods fit each domain; nonapplicability reviewed | Domains present but several methods are unrelated proxies or applicability unclear | Domains omitted or missing evidence declared satisfactory |
| Grain, inventory and reconciliation | Every inventory/source identity reconciles; bridge/rerun/category hazards are tested and documented | Required inventories retained; totals reproduce at declared grain; gaps explicit | Grain or inventory tests incomplete; errors remain for correction | Relationships counted as populations or authentic totals invented |
| Adequacy, validity and provenance | Narrow claims, rival explanations and source-row audit trail survive challenge | Sources/keys, validity and adequacy separate; failure versus missingness correct | References or validity decisions too vague to reproduce | False source/connection claims or outcomes manufactured |
| Standards restraint and gap review | Specific mapping uncertainties prioritized with qualified licensed-text review actions | 25023-to-2023 gaps named and owned; no score/certification claim | Generic disclaimer without concrete mapping gaps/action | Claims exhaustive ISO coverage, certification or conformity |
| Owned decisions and accessible communication | Decision note makes trade-offs clear; tables and restricted evidence routes are keyboard-tested | Owners/dates/actions assigned; exact-header long tables and noncolor text supplied | Actions weakly owned or access/privacy checks incomplete | No actionable gaps, inaccessible-only output or unauthorized disclosure |

Instructor feedback identifies the exact row, requirement and failed gate, supplies a bounded correction task, then rechecks the revised submission. For a developing domain method, request the missing assertion/source rather than “make the quality number better.” For a reconciliation fault, rerun identity comparisons before rewriting the headline. For unavailable specialist/user evidence, accept an honest gap as evidence of sound reasoning but do not award a fabricated measured outcome; assessed execution still depends on the authentic instructor pack. Record revision decisions and any remaining blocker in the final decision note.

title: Data Quality, Ethics, and Trust

introduction.dilemma: The spreadsheet has no blanks, the report refreshed today, and the names are replaced with codes. May I call the evidence accurate and safe to share?
introduction.reply: Not yet. A tidy cell tells you little about the authority behind its value; a refresh tells you little about the last reconciled source; a code tells you little about who can recognize the person. Put those claims on separate desks. First establish what this source can support, then establish what this particular audience may receive. Keep the gaps visible and give each next action an owner. You will build that bounded judgment into the ledger you already use, rather than manufacture a single trust score.

topics.lecture_markdown:
### Your dilemma

‘I removed every blank and kept only one row per bug. Why might my cleanup have destroyed the evidence?’

### The Evidence Desk reply

Start with the decision, not the broom. You are deciding whether a particular extraction can support a release-review claim. You are not awarding a badge to a tidy spreadsheet. Define the project, work-item types, observation window and table grain before you evaluate a value. Each control asks a different question; passing one does not silently answer the others.

Requiredness is conditional. A contact field may be essential for one work-item type and legitimately unused for another. QA055 counts nonblank locally required record-field opportunities against expected required opportunities, not all workbook cells. Replacing a missing required value with ‘unknown’ does not obtain the information. A justified nonrequired opportunity belongs in the documented exclusion inventory. Keep the requiredness rule and its version so another reviewer can reproduce your decision.

Identity depends on grain. A current-item fact uses a complete project/item key; a revision fact also needs revision identity. A daily snapshot needs observation date. QA057 counts rows belonging to repeated complete-key groups against evaluated rows. M08’s local DuplicateKeys convention instead counts distinct repeated complete-key groups. Neither is an extra-row count. Preserve raw rows and investigate the complete key before correction: a join fan-out and legitimate finer-grain observations require different responses.

**Conceptual example from the approved illustration:** an item observed on different dates can legitimately appear more than once. Removing repeated item IDs would erase dated evidence. Test the complete item/day identity for that question; count distinct items separately. A spreadsheet row number cannot repair a wrongly declared business key.

QA056 checks domain and cross-field rules. An allowed State label can still name the wrong state for the item; syntactic consistency is not semantic accuracy. QA060 therefore compares comparable values with a suitable dated reference under recorded matching, normalization and tolerance rules. Retain unmatched, stale, ambiguous and unevaluated cases separately. Without a suitable reference, the comparison remains Not Measured, rather than perfect agreement or punitive zero. A measured rule failure is evidence of failure, not absence of measurement.

Clocks also answer different questions. QA058 measures elapsed hours from the last successfully reconciled extraction to report observation; its denominator is ‘Not a ratio.’ Report refresh can repaint old or unreconciled data. Analytics is a reporting copy, not a real-time operational view, and source-ingestion lag remains a separate limitation. QA059 tests whether evaluated rows have the required stable key, source/revision evidence, extraction timestamp and transformation/run identity. Those last two values come from actual manifests, not invented Azure properties.

Use M06 to trace native source paths into explicitly LOCAL targets, M08 to compare actual page groups and independently controlled key sets, and M04 to contract each control. Matching counts cannot establish matching membership. Keep unknown inputs blank and disclose Not Measured; a known zero denominator produces N/A with its count and reason, not an evidence status. Display exclusions and unevaluated opportunities beside results.

Finally, give each material finding a source pointer, impact and named action owner. Correct with retained evidence, qualify a bounded use, or hold a decision-critical claim. Selected locally operationalized controls informed by ISO/IEC 25012 and 25024 are neither the complete models nor an ISO conformity score. A trustworthy ledger explains exactly what was checked and what could still overturn its claim.

steps.title: Inspect the actual XML/JSON route
steps.instructions: With authorization inspect saved XML from GET https://analytics.dev.azure.com/{organization}/{project}/_odata/v2.0/$metadata, or the instructor’s authentic saved response. Locate entity sets/types, property types and keys before selecting fields. The approved current example is GET https://analytics.dev.azure.com/{organization}/{project}/_odata/v2.0/WorkItems?$select=WorkItemId,Title,State. steps.title: Complete native-to-LOCAL lineage
steps.instructions: In M06 allocate actual MappingId and SourceId per used transformed field. For OData WorkItems map value[].WorkItemId -> LOCAL_CurrentWorkItem.LOCAL_WorkItemId, value[].State -> LOCAL_CurrentWorkItem.LOCAL_State and necessary restricted value[].Title -> LOCAL_CurrentWorkItem.LOCAL_Title. Preserve identifiers, raw state and nulls; apply only approved versioned normalization. For the separate revision alternative map value[].id, value[].rev and value[].fields['System.State'] to LOCAL_WorkItemRevision.LOCAL_WorkItemId, LOCAL_RevisionId and LOCAL_State respectively; validate requested item identity. Map LOCAL_ExtractedUTC only from the actual extraction manifest, LOCAL_TransformRunId from actual transformation/version evidence and LOCAL_ProjectKey from the validated source scope manifest. None is a native Azure property. Populate TargetGrain and complete JoinKey as project/item or project/item/revision, TransformRule type/null handling, UTCOrCalendar elapsed UTC/calendar decision, PrivacyClass, actual Owner and nonsecret restricted EvidenceRef. Every absent property remains a gap.
steps.checkpoint_output: M06 rows for every used field, including a source-State-to-LOCAL trace with key/grain/clock/rule and owner evidence.

steps.title: Contract six distinct trust controls
steps.instructions: In M04 select only QA055–QA060 from the existing 60-measure register. Retain Domain ‘Data trust’ and exact names: QA055 Required-field completeness; QA056 Domain and cross-field rule pass share; QA057 Duplicate business-key row share; QA058 Refresh evidence age; QA059 Source-to-report provenance coverage; QA060 Authoritative-reference agreement. Enter their definitions in FormulaDefinition. QA055 is nonblank required opportunities/expected required opportunities; QA056 passing evaluated record-rule opportunities/evaluated record-rule opportunities; QA057 all rows in repeated complete-key groups/evaluated rows; QA058 elapsed hours since last successfully reconciled extraction with Denominator ‘Not a ratio’; QA059 evaluated rows having stable key, source/revision evidence, extraction timestamp and transformation/run ID/evaluated rows; QA060 comparable agreements under dated matching/normalization/tolerance rules/comparable evaluated values. Complete InformationNeed, GrainCohort, PeriodUTC, Exclusions, Owner, local ThresholdRationale, ReviewCadence, Availability, EvidenceStatus, SourceRef and Limitations. Record requiredness/rule inventories and reference owner/version. Availability is potential capability, not measured evidence; owner-approved thresholds are local, not ISO targets.
steps.checkpoint_output: Six cumulative M04 contracts with separate inventories and no combined trust/ISO score or copied illustrative counts.

steps.title: Evaluate opportunities and investigate repetition
steps.instructions: On the actual restricted cohort enumerate required record-field opportunities, rule opportunities and provenance/reference checks. In EvidenceRef attachments retain complete source key, field/rule version, restricted value/pointer, expected rule/reference, evaluation result, validity disposition, impact and named action owner. Preserve legitimate nulls, missing required values, failed and unevaluable rules separately. Group duplicate candidates by the complete key; retain members and diagnose source duplication, join fan-out or legitimate finer grain before correction. A bridge can repeat a key without being the full fact inventory. Keep before/after evidence and approved correction rule. Leave the duplicate disposition and one reconciliation decision for your independent checking; if no actual fault occurs, use an instructor-retained authentic finding or state the limitation, never manufacture one.
steps.checkpoint_output: Restricted row-level findings and one individually reasoned duplicate/legitimate-grain disposition linked to the same ledger.

steps.title: Reconcile all source page groups
steps.instructions: Populate M08 BatchId per actual partition/page group and reuse M06 SourceId. Enter actual WindowStartUTC, WindowEndUTC, PageCount, independent same-grain SourceExpectedRows and raw ExtractRows. DuplicateKeys counts distinct complete-key groups occurring more than once; document that convention in EvidenceRef. MissingKeys counts expected distinct complete keys absent from extraction. Put unexpected keys and retained-out/deleted dispositions in the restricted comparison attachment, not new columns. Compare complete sets as well as totals and use the actual query artifact/hash for QueryHash. Unknown expectations and missing counts stay blank with Not Measured, not zero. Preserve the supplied reconciliation formula: its Reconciled/Mismatch labels correspond to legacy C05 quiz/game Passed/Failed wording, not permission to overwrite the formula or change original keys. Explain any status/authority limitation in EvidenceRef. M08 actions are owned through SourceId -> M06 Owner and a named action in the finding.
steps.checkpoint_output: All actual M08 page groups and independent count/key-set comparisons, with genuine hash evidence and explicit gaps.

steps.title: Check rates, clocks and the claim gate
steps.instructions: Independently match each numerator/denominator to retained row-level inventories and instructor control answers. On known numeric cells use Excel =IF(denominator_cell=0,"N/A",100*numerator_cell/denominator_cell), replacing placeholders with actual cell references; do not coerce unknown inputs to zero. Show count/reason for N/A and keep evidence statuses Measured, Conditional/proxy, Not Measured or justified Not Applicable separate from outcomes. A measured failed rule stays failed. QA058 uses actual observation UTC minus validated extraction UTC, converted to elapsed hours; Excel datetime subtraction times 24 gives hours only when both validated datetime cells exist. Missing validated extraction means Not Measured. Disclose source-ingestion lag separately. Retain exact calculations; round only display. Name the owner’s evidenced correction, bounded-use or hold decision for every material discrepancy.
steps.checkpoint_output: Reproducible measure-specific inputs and clock trace; signed/recorded owner disposition or explicit pending authority.

steps.title: Save an accessible cumulative handoff
steps.instructions: Save the original named workbooks without overwriting unrelated rows. Export exact-sheet long-format tables with one ordinary header row, unmerged cells, full identifiers, readable dates and text statuses; provide approved UTF-8 CSV/text where helpful without widening access. Add a short decision/finding/gap/owner/next-review summary. Write the Honesty Check: which passed control still leaves uncertainty; what accuracy comparison was unavailable; what legitimate null and grain mistake you avoided; what evidence would change the decision and who will obtain it. A Power BI visual is not required to establish ledger correctness. Check keyboard opening/filtering and noncolor reading; retain actual observations, not an invented access success.

topics.title: Ethical collection and comparison

prediction.prompt: Individually predict: the privacy owner authorizes an internal service-level table with pseudonyms. Does that approval let a director rank individual engineers across unlike services or release its raw rows externally? Identify the two decisions that are still needed.

topics.lecture_markdown:
### Your dilemma

‘The director wants an engineer league table and a public download. We removed names. Can readers decide what the rankings mean?’

### The Evidence Desk reply

You remain responsible for the inference and the disclosure. Write the permitted purpose and receiving audience before choosing fields. A vague future use is not a measurement need, and a person-ranking demand is not made defensible by coding identities. Continue the trust ledger, but now ask two independent questions: what bounded process claim does this evidence support, and what exact artifact may this audience receive?

Start with construct and cohort fit. Elapsed PR time includes waiting, workflow and risk context; it is not a meter of individual labor. Compare common service boundaries, risk/work categories, workflow, exposure, observation period and instrumentation only where matching is supported. If those conditions do not match, present separate scoped descriptions instead of a league table. An actionable process question asks which review queue its owner should investigate. M04 InformationNeed expresses that decision; GrainCohort and Limitations describe its actual boundaries.

Collection and sharing require their own authority. Obtain the actual owner’s purpose/collection or consent decision, access, retention/deletion rules and audience-specific disclosure approval. Do not invent a legal basis or universal minimum cohort size. M06 records every collected and released field’s classification, necessity, approved transformation and owner. Unnecessary personal identifiers or free text should be omitted from the recipient projection, not merely hidden in the author’s workbook. Keep restricted raw evidence available only to authorized reviewers.

Pseudonyms reduce direct identification but can preserve recognizable combinations of role, dates, rare events and service. Use stable identity only if the purpose needs it. Keep the actual lookup separately restricted; never include it in a recipient package. Any LOCAL_PseudonymKey or LOCAL_PublicServiceLabel is your approved local model design, not a native Azure field. Its real source path and transformation still need evidence. A convenient invented identity property would make the lineage less, not more, trustworthy.

**Approved fictional decision demonstration, not observed organizational evidence:** a coded row retains a unique specialist role and rare-incident date. A table hides its sensitive category, yet a download retains raw detail and complementary totals permit reconstruction. The display and the release are different artifacts. Inspect identifying combinations, exports, drillthrough and totals under recipient-equivalent authorized access. Apply the actual local rule and retain real test evidence. ‘Suppressed’ means withheld from that audience, not zero or Passed. An Area Path filter is not permission; Analytics does not enforce Area Path security.

Minimization must also preserve analytical honesty. M08 stays at extraction partition/page-group grain with source expectations and raw counts. Reconcile approved output groups at their own grain in the restricted EvidenceRef attachment, linked also from M06. Explain source-to-output keys, rule version, grouping/suppression and retained full denominator. Do not replace source counts with report groups or quietly use only shareable rows under an unchanged full-population headline.

Finally, ask whose observations are absent. Retained-out history, missing pages, unequal windows, convenience selection and nonresponse can change apparent advantage. Complete extraction of voluntary responses does not represent former users who were not approached. Tie those limits to actual manifests and authorized minimal sampling evidence; never invent their outcomes. Put the limit in the receiving audience’s claim, not only a restricted appendix.

Your handoff may permit bounded internal process use while holding external release. State each disposition, its evidence, actual owner and next review request. Retain a restricted reviewer package and an approved minimized recipient package—or a clearly held design. Real review and repair are necessary; role-play approval, name removal and a passing quiz cannot authorize disclosure or certify practical competence.

Why is there no shortcut from a passed claim-use decision to audience sharing? Follow the repair feedback arrow when a suppressed table has a revealing export. Record what actual evidence each branch requires; the drawing itself records no passed gate.

Lineage supplies keys, rules and clocks to Scoped trust checks; those checks feed bounded evidence to Cohort match and gaps, which tests fit before the Claim use gate. In parallel, lineage supports Minimize release fields, then All disclosure paths, then the Audience share gate using current owner approval. Material unresolved claim gaps or unsafe/unverified disclosure lead to Hold and owned repair; retained correction evidence returns to lineage for rechecking. Claim use and audience share are separate gates: neither arrow asserts that a gate passed.

steps.instructions: In the selected M04 rows rewrite InformationNeed as an owned process decision, for example which service review queue its owner should investigate. steps.title: Audit every actual source and target field
steps.instructions: Review all M06 SourceField/TargetField rows needed for collection or release: identifiers, keys, title/free text, dates and identifying combinations, not just names. Record necessity/classification in PrivacyClass, omission or approved minimization in TransformRule, actual Owner and review EvidenceRef. Keep SourceEntity/SourceField and source pointers restricted while explaining absent fields in the shared target. If used, LOCAL_PublicServiceLabel and LOCAL_PseudonymKey are explicitly local fields; validate their actual source paths in the provisioned export and never invent a native identity property. steps.instructions: In the actual workbook/export omit unnecessary personal fields rather than hiding columns. Where stable pseudonyms are required, use the approved mapping process with consistent joins and separately restricted lookup/actual access owner. Using the recipient-equivalent authorized artifact inspect identifying combinations, sensitive groups, row drillthrough, CSV/download and complementary totals/adjacent categories. Complete one path and independently decide another applicable path, documenting actual observations or an unverified gap. A filtered author chart is not the recipient access test; Analytics does not enforce Area Path security. Text-label suppressed values without exposing defeating counts, never zero/Passed. Absent reviewer, rule or access observation means hold sharing and request the actual owner’s evidence, not a universal cutoff.

For supplementary responses inspect only approved minimal sampling-frame/response/nonresponse evidence; without it limit claims to observed respondents. Add specific effects in M04 Exclusions/Limitations and a rival missingness/selection explanation in the linked note. A justified matched window requires owner approval and reconciled included/excluded observations; absent match means separate descriptions. Never impute absent records as success/failure or call elapsed time personal productivity.

Check keyboard opening/filtering, full headers and noncolor text reading with genuine permitted recipient/reader observations. Write two Honesty Check sentences: ‘This evidence supports [bounded claim] because [scoped evidence], but does not establish [excluded inference].’ ‘This audience may/may not receive [artifact] because [actual approval/gap].’ Name absent experience and an alternate output risk. Contribute these to the original 150–250-word performance note; arrange the actual instructor challenge, revise the existing rows/note and retain the finding/reason, not another report.

Source key sets reconcile before transformation; approved output groups and full denominators reconcile afterward at their own grain. Suppression does not redefine the population; M08 stays source-grain.

Actual purpose/access/retention and applicable disclosure-path reviews are retained or sharing remains explicitly held. No personal league table, invented consent, filter-as-permission or public identity lookup.

games.title: The Disclosure Desk
games.objective: Decide whether an evidence artifact can be shared under the explicitly stated local policy.
games.rules: The cards are fictional policy exercises, not legal advice or an ISO threshold. Choose SHARE or HOLD for each round under this practice policy: external release needs approved purpose and audience, no direct or reasonably identifying combinations, checked downloads/drillthrough, and current owner approval. title: The Story: Build the Logical Sequence

introduction.dilemma: The evidence is mixed. Must the story end happily?
introduction.reply: No. A useful story ends with a defensible decision, which may be “not ready.” Put the observations in an inspectable order, keep rival explanations visible, and give the reader an owned next action rather than a reassuring finale.

outcomes: Distinguish change over time from configuration difference and reject an unlike-grain comparison; success evidence is a justified time beat C12-V01 and category beat C12-V02 for one declared decision.

Keep the QA011 eligible denominator separate from full planned inventory, missing pairs and excluded outcomes; success evidence is an individually reconstructed calculation and exact controlled-source reconciliation at the declared candidate/test/configuration grain.
Bound a composition or event interpretation without attributing causation or team capability; success evidence is a canvas paragraph with CounterEvidence, SourceRef and a named ActionOwner.
Sequence context, complication, evidence, interpretation and recommendation without hiding adverse evidence; success evidence is the individual's exactly 180-word spine linked to C12-V01–C12-V03.

Keep an action-changing gap in the executive layer while analytical and restricted appendix layers deepen the same argument; success evidence is a consistent headline, three analytical beats, uncertainty paragraph and appendix plan.

Revise a bounded recommendation after a real reviewer challenge and changed controlled evidence scope; success evidence is an individual revision note, source-linked M17 C12-V03 and named action owner/review point.

topics.title: Time and character stories

prediction.prompt: Before discussion, write your prediction: if the share of recorded results from a difficult configuration shrinks, could the pooled rate improve while neither configuration improves? Which comparison would you request before writing a headline?

topics.lecture_markdown:
### Your question: change, difference, or an unsafe comparison?

“Dear Evidence Desk: our pooled acceptance pass percentage rose. One colleague wants an improving line; another wants a table ranking configurations. Which story is true?”

Start with the decision, not the chart: your release owner needs to decide whether the candidate evidence justifies the next review action. A **time story** follows a declared population through ordered, matched observation windows. A **character story** compares meaningful categories, distributions, composition or trade-offs within a defensible scope. Here, character means a category's role in the evidence, not a personality or capability score for a team. Both stories can be truthful while a confident general-improvement headline is not.

For time, declare the baseline before seeing which earlier week looks weakest. Keep the candidate, observation windows, test selection, configuration mapping and calculation grain inspectable. A baseline anchors the comparison; a trend describes direction. Seasonality requires a repeatable calendar pattern, an event supplies context, and a possible change point is a shift to investigate. One favorable week does not establish these patterns. An eight-week export may suggest a weekly pattern but cannot establish annual seasonality. Annotating a process change does not show that it caused the recorded change.

For categories, show counts as well as percentages and explain why the configurations are comparable. A pooled rate can change because the outcome mix changes, not because every category improves. A table ranking unlike teams cannot repair differences in risk, instrumentation or units. Result attempts and unique acceptance test/configuration pairs are different populations. Decline or qualify an unsupported comparison rather than decorating it.

**Conceptual example — approved worked illustration only.** These are invented tiny counts, not authentic Azure observations. Each window plans ten pairs in configuration A and ten in B. Baseline A has nine passes among ten eligible pairs; baseline B has three among ten. Later A has eight among ten; later B has zero among two. Eight later B pairs lack a valid result, for an unknown reason. The pooled recorded share moves from 12/20, or 60.00%, to 8/12, or 66.67%, although both category rates fall. A time beat can report that pooled recorded change; a category beat exposes the changed mix; an inventory-gap beat constrains what either can support. Do not infer deliberate selection, missing execution or missing publication from the arithmetic.

QA011, Release acceptance-test pass share, counts latest valid Passed pairs divided by pairs whose latest valid outcome is Passed or Failed within the frozen candidate acceptance inventory. Sum eligible counts to pool; do not average category percentages. Preserve reruns, selecting the latest valid result only within the same candidate/test/configuration under the approved ordering rule. Missing, blocked, skipped, not-run and inconclusive pairs remain visible beside the rate. A zero eligible denominator is N/A with count and reason; zero passes with two eligible results is a measured zero, not N/A. QA011 is not a product-wide quality score or an ISO-prescribed readiness threshold.

Translate the decision into M17, Chart Decision: one message/evidence beat per row. Your canvas paragraph links decision, audience, evidence, visual, owned action and caveat through those same rows; it is not a new worksheet. Read DenominatorRule while filtering. If the filter changes the question, update FilterScope and reconsider the claim explicitly. Finally, name evidence that could weaken your finding. A defensible narrative can survive inspection and revision; it does not have to finish with approval.

visual.alt: Fixed scope branches into time, category and evidence-gap beats; bounded interpretation reaches three truthful layers and owned review.
visual.trace_prompt: Trace Fixed scope and lineage to Time beat and Category beat, then follow both arrows into Bounded interpretation. Why is the Evidence gap beat a third input rather than a footnote? Point to the original 12.1 proof table's eligible and planned columns that justify your answer.
visual.text_equivalent: Decision and audience declares Fixed scope and lineage. Scope branches into Time beat via matched periods, Category beat via comparable configurations, and Evidence gap beat via inventory versus records. Time contributes observed change, Category contributes mix and differences, and Gap contributes limits on readiness to Bounded interpretation. Interpretation branches into Executive boundary carrying the action-changing limit, Analytical counts carrying counts and alternatives, and Restricted source appendix carrying the reconstruction path. All three layers support Owned action and review; new evidence at review may revise Fixed scope and lineage. These arrows express justification and revision, not proof of causation. Arrows do not confer release authorization.

steps.title: Freeze grain, scope and the selected-result rule
steps.instructions: Declare candidate/test/configuration grain, UTC matched windows, source-as-of time and frozen inventory version before comparing. Select the latest valid result only within the same candidate/test/configuration using the existing approved deterministic ordering rule; never silently cross candidates/builds. steps.title: Reconcile inventory and reconstruct QA011
steps.instructions: At the existing evidence-model grain, reconcile retained attempts to their source id/context, then selected latest-valid pairs to the frozen inventory. Check authoritative expected counts at that same scope/grain; a successful HTTP response alone cannot prove completeness. Reconstruct QA011 = latest-valid Passed pairs / latest-valid (Passed + Failed) pairs. Keep full inventory, missing pairs and blocked/skipped/not-run/inconclusive exclusions beside it. Sum numerator/eligible counts for pooling, not category percentages. Show zero eligible denominator as N/A with count/reason; zero passes over a nonzero eligible denominator stays zero. Unknown completeness stays Not Measured. When referencing prior C05 M08, preserve its existing formula: actual Reconciled/Mismatch corresponds to legacy quiz Passed/Failed terminology; never overwrite the formula or relabel M17 measurement statuses with those outcomes.
steps.checkpoint_output: Restricted same-scope reconciliation and reconstructible numerator/eligible/inventory/gap counts, or a precise Not Measured blocker.

steps.title: Create the time beat C12-V01
steps.instructions: Enter VisualId C12-V01 and the shared Audience/Decision. Write a scoped observed Claim. Set MetricId to the existing QA011 contract and MatrixId to the existing underlying evidence artifact M10 for acceptance provenance, not M17 itself. Comparison declares justified baseline/later matched windows and documented event context. VisualForm is “time trend with counts and event annotations.” FilterScope states candidate/window/configuration, timezone and source-as-of. DenominatorRule describes latest valid eligible pairs plus companion inventory/missing counts. CounterEvidence retains selection, seasonality, publication and other-event alternatives.
steps.checkpoint_output: One bounded time row with a prespecified comparison and inspectable denominator; no causal headline.

steps.title: Complete the category beat C12-V02 independently
steps.instructions: Add VisualId C12-V02 for the same decision/contract/frozen scope. Choose Comparison and explain what makes configurations comparable; do not copy a best/worst ranking. VisualForm is “category comparison with counts; distribution detail if contracted.” Retain numerator, eligible denominator and missing planned inventory by configuration. If risk, scope, mapping or instrumentation does not support matching, qualify or decline the comparison. Claim states a recorded difference, not a proven explanation or team-capability judgement.
steps.checkpoint_output: A category row and your own comparability explanation; unsupported comparison is explicitly refused or limited.

steps.title: Complete statuses, lineage and the canvas
steps.instructions: For both rows, EvidenceStatus is Measured only after scoped calculation and row-level reconciliation; Conditional/proxy labels a qualified indirect inference; Not Measured marks unavailable evidence. Passed/Failed are result outcomes, not this status. SourceRef locates contract, controlled query/export/version/as-of, inventory, transformation/selection rule, reconciliation and source-row IDs under authorized access. ActionOwner names the next-action owner, not “team.” Write the Data Story Canvas paragraph: decision → audience → evidence → proposed visual → owned action → caveat, anchored to the existing M17 fields. Read DenominatorRule while filtering and explicitly repair FilterScope if the question changes.
steps.checkpoint_output: Same two-row draft and canvas paragraph with honest statuses and restricted reconstruction references.

steps.title: Validate and export the same draft
steps.instructions: Check unique VisualId values, one shared decision contract, justified baseline, both comparison types and exact source counts. Test a missing-source and zero-denominator case without fabricating outcomes; no historical claim may depend only on a present-day link. Export only these two beat rows to long-format UTF-8 CSV with the fourteen exact headers, no merged cells and textual statuses. Navigate with the keyboard and read the text claim/count/caveat. Keep the draft for two-pass review and individual slice-B replacement; do not start another full assignment.
steps.checkpoint_output: C12-V01/C12-V02 draft workbook, exact-header CSV, canvas, restricted reconciliation locators and validation/access notes.

completion_checks: Exactly the fourteen M17 headers and unique beat IDs; one shared audience/decision contract and an existing underlying evidence matrix.

Matched windows and comparable configurations are justified; full planned inventory and eligible-rate denominator are distinct; latest valid results never pool rerun attempts or cross candidates silently.
Every asserted count reconstructs from approved source rows and authoritative same-grain expected counts; unavailable completeness is Not Measured, not a guessed success.

Claim states observation separately from interpretation; CounterEvidence preserves selection/publication/seasonality alternatives and SourceRef contains no credentials or unauthorized raw identifiers.
Every controlled count matches exactly; no silent exclusion, invented source row or unauthorized disclosure. Keep every material gap visible in the recommendation.
Save your last checked step and scope version; resume in a roughly 5–12-minute segment without recopying the build.

recall.prompt: Close the notes. A chart can tell you either 'what changed?' or 'how do categories differ?' Explain why using both views still does not establish why the results changed.

questions.prompt: A release owner asks whether recorded outcomes changed over eight weeks. Which comparison answers the time-story question most defensibly?

options.text: Compare the newest week with whichever older week has the lowest rate.
Compare prespecified matched windows, show each week's counts, and annotate scope and publication changes.
Rank teams by their latest pass percentage.
Compare one current snapshot with the sum of all historical snapshot rows.

questions.prompt: In the worked illustration, pooled eligible acceptance pass share rises from 60.00% to 66.67%, while both configuration-specific rates fall and eight planned configuration-B pairs lack a later valid result. Which headline is supported?

options.text: The release is safer because pooled pass share rose.
Configuration B improved because fewer failures were recorded.
Pooled recorded share rose, but changed configuration mix and missing results prevent a general improvement conclusion.
Replace the eight missing results with passes to preserve the planned denominator.

questions.prompt: You want a character story about two configurations of the same release. Which M17 entry makes the category comparison defensible?

options.text: Comparison identifies both configurations, FilterScope fixes candidate and window, and DenominatorRule states eligible pairs plus the full inventory gap count.

games.title: Which story is this?
games.objective: Distinguish change over time, category differences and invalid comparisons.
games.rules: For each round type T for a time story, C for a character/category story, or X for an invalid comparison. Then write the requested one-line boundary. Work untimed; inspect the solution after answering. Each round earns one point for the classification and one for the boundary.

rounds.prompt: Round 1: One service's weekly recorded outcomes are compared across prespecified equal windows; an inventory change is marked in week 5. Type T/C/X and state what the event marker does not prove.
Round 2: The same candidate and UTC window are split into configurations A and B; eligible pair counts and missing planned pairs are shown. Type T/C/X and name the comparison boundary.
Round 3: Team Red's low-risk API result attempts are ranked against Team Blue's high-risk device acceptance pairs as if the percentages measured identical work. Type T/C/X and identify the mismatch.

games.scoring: Maximum 6 points; 5-6 indicates a usable distinction, 3-4 calls for revisiting the boundary, and 0-2 calls for guided practice. No score affects the exam; replay freely.
games.accessible_alternative: Use plain text T/C/X and a sentence, or keyboard-select the code and dictate the sentence. No timing, dragging, color, audio or animation is required.

games.title: Denominator detective
games.objective: Select evidence that can challenge an apparent improvement and repair the resulting claim.
games.rules: Each round supplies three numbered evidence cards. Type one card number, then the requested repair. One point for the card and one for the repair, untimed. A semantically equivalent bounded repair receives credit.

rounds.prompt: Round 1: Pooled share rises in the worked illustration. Cards: 1 = a more attractive headline; 2 = configuration-specific passed/eligible counts and planned inventory; 3 = another team's latest rate. Which card tests a composition explanation? Write the resulting caution.

Round 2: Eight planned B pairs lack a later valid result. Cards: 1 = source-run publication/retention inventory and export manifest; 2 = an assumption that blanks mean pass; 3 = a current bug-count card. Which card helps distinguish missing publication from missing execution? Name what remains unknown until checked.

Round 3: The director asks whether a new practice caused the change. Cards: 1 = the date the practice began alone; 2 = a reordered chart; 3 = matched period/scope evidence plus test-selection, publication and contemporaneous-change records. Choose the strongest next evidence and write a bounded conclusion now.

games.scoring: Maximum 6 points. Review any missing boundary, then retry with your repaired claim. Feedback: 'This card is useful for another question; follow the current claim's denominator or provenance instead.' Practice only.
games.accessible_alternative: Respond with 1/2/3 and plain text using keyboard or dictation. Cards remain visible throughout; there is no clock or drag interaction.

returns.prompt: Closed-note: a fixed planned configuration inventory exists, but fewer pairs have valid results in the later window. What two populations must the narrative distinguish, and why?
Closed-note: a reviewer wants to rank two teams using one team's result attempts and another's unique acceptance pairs. Explain the first repair or refusal, without calculating a rate.
Closed-note: a trend shifts near a process event. Name two rival explanations you would keep visible and one kind of evidence you would request before strengthening the explanation.

remediation.task: Label the approved illustration’s eligible-rate and full-inventory populations in text. Repair the faulty Comparison or DenominatorRule in your same M17 draft; ask the actual instructor which population the sentence describes. Explain a fresh conceptual scope without invented counts.
remediation.recheck: After real feedback, reconstruct the declared denominator and gap separately, retain one rival explanation and reattempt the unchanged topic quiz as needed. Concept-only repair cannot clear an authentic-source blocker.

topics.stretch: Using already approved reconciled evidence only, test whether a scoped claim survives a different matched window or configuration cut. Declare the new comparison before viewing its result, document alternatives and preserve inventory gaps. topics.title: Layered narrative

prediction.prompt: Write privately: your executive reader will see only one sentence. A missing configuration could change the recommended action, but its raw result IDs are restricted. What must appear in that sentence, and what should remain at deeper access-controlled detail?

topics.lecture_markdown:
### Your question: can brevity hide an uncomfortable limit?

“Dear Evidence Desk: the director wants three evidence beats and one short recommendation. I have a pooled improvement, a configuration decline and a gap. Can I put the uncomfortable material in the appendix?”

No, if removing that material could change the action. Layering changes detail, not truth. Your executive reader may never open the analytical paragraphs or restricted appendix, so the first layer must not imply an approval that deeper evidence contradicts. You can protect raw result identifiers without concealing the existence and decision impact of missing evidence.

Build your argument in five moves. **Context** names the reader's decision and the candidate or period. **Complication** explains why an obvious answer is unsafe. **Evidence** states what the declared records show, including counts and scope. **Interpretation** says what those observations support and what remains a rival explanation. **Recommendation** names the proposed action, accountable owner and next decision point. Draft these as separate labelled sentences before polishing. A proposed action is not an observation; a plausible mechanism is not an established finding.

Choose three essential beats by asking what uncertainty each reduces. Carry forward your matched time comparison and comparable configuration view. Add the evidence-sufficiency beat: full planned inventory versus valid-result-bearing pairs and its effect on the decision. Three favorable charts of the same pooled percentage are one argument repeated, not three distinct contributions. If removing the uncomfortable beat makes your recommendation stronger, that beat is material and belongs back in the first layer.

**Conceptual example — approved worked illustration only.** The invented 12.1 counts show pooled recorded share rising from 12/20 to 8/12 while both configuration rates fall and eight later B pairs have no valid result. “Our new practice improved quality. Pass share is 66.67%. Release” turns a recorded observation into an untested causal and readiness claim. Instead, establish the review decision, explain incomplete configuration coverage, give the time/category/gap observations, retain mix and publication alternatives, and propose reconciliation before the owner's next review. This demonstrates a logical repair, not an authentic organizational finding or completed reconciliation.

The executive headline states a finding, the proposed action and its material boundary in one or two sentences. The analytical layer supplies a paragraph for each beat, with counts, categories, windows and alternatives. A separate uncertainty paragraph names rival explanations and the evidence that could reverse your interpretation. The restricted source appendix is a reconstruction path: existing metric contract and evidence matrix, frozen inventory, documented export or metadata-backed source, query/version, as-of time, LOCAL transformations, latest-valid selection and reconciliation locators. A screenshot alone cannot provide that path. Keep restricted IDs in approved storage and use authorized reference notes in the audience export.

Expand your five moves into exactly 180 words, excluding the heading and separate beat annotations. This constraint makes you choose essential reasoning, not invent numbers to fill space. State a specific evidence request and owner in the prose; a review point belongs there or in a reference note, not a new M17 ReviewDate column. “Not ready” is useful when it tells the reader what must happen before reconsideration without pretending that work already happened.

Test your first layer with a real reader asynchronously. Ask them to record the action and limitation before seeing deeper layers, then compare their inference with your intended position. Repair misleading wording and retain the original sentence, actual challenge and individual revision. If new authorized evidence changes the gap or comparison, revise every affected layer and action. The goal is a clear inspectable decision, not a polished draft protected from contradiction.

games.title: Five-sentence filing desk
games.objective: Order context, complication, evidence, interpretation and recommendation.
games.rules: In each round type the five letter labels in context-to-recommendation order. The first point is for correct order; the second is for answering the round's challenge sentence. Work untimed and use the key after attempting.

rounds.prompt: Round 1 cards: A = QA lead should reconcile missing pairs before the next release review. B = Recorded pooled share rose, but both configurations' rates fell. Round 2 cards: A = The trend may reflect missing publication rather than changed execution. B = QA lead should compare the source-run inventory with the export manifest before review. C = Eight expected pairs have no retained valid result in the later extract. D = The reviewer must decide whether the evidence is sufficient. E = A report labelled complete has an unresolved gap. Order the cards and say whether A is proven.

Round 3 cards: A = The latest two periods do not yet support a general improvement claim. B = The agreed decision is whether to publish that claim. C = Counts and scope definitions differ across those periods. D = Analyst should rebuild the comparison at matched scope for the owner's next review. E = The draft headline calls the trend universally better. Order the cards and name the sentence that should be weakened.

rounds.prompt: Round 1: Draft headline is 'Results improved; release.' Choices: 1 = add passed/eligible counts, both configuration rates, full planned inventory and missing-pair count; 2 = add the same number in a brighter font; 3 = compare it with another team's unrelated rate. Choose and name the worked illustration's later pooled counts and gap.

Round 3: Appendix contains only a dashboard screenshot. Choices: 1 = mark the screenshot as ISO conformity; 2 = remove the appendix so the story stays short; 3 = include contract ID, query/version and export provenance, transformation/latest-result rule and source-row IDs under approved access. games.scoring: Maximum 6 points. Feedback for omitted limits: 'Keep the detail short, but keep the decision-changing limit in view.' Review the relevant layer and replay. No practice score affects an exam.

topics.lecture_markdown:
### The Letter

“Dear Evidence Desk: the failure line is lower, although we stopped publishing one troublesome configuration. Should I use a tight vertical axis to show the improvement? Our release target also looks like a convenient control limit.”

### The Evidence Desk reply and lecture

First write the comparison in a sentence without mentioning a chart. “Recorded attempt failure share changed within this configuration and period” is testable. “Quality improved” is a larger claim requiring evidence the line does not contain. Put the omitted configuration beside the series, not beneath an optimistic headline. A disappearing test suite can produce a lovely trend with no change to the product.

You are deciding which comparison the evidence supports, not choosing an attractive decoration. Use an ordered line for time observations, zero-based bars for category magnitudes, a distribution for completed durations, and a matrix for required coverage. A Pareto ordering helps prioritize recorded categories for investigation; it does not prove their causes. If one record has multiple categories, disclose that counting rule. Otherwise a cumulative display can make category occurrences look like distinct failed records.

Protect the population before interpreting the shape. QA010 Published attempt pass share is Passed divided by Passed plus Failed published attempts, retaining retries. Show other outcomes separately. A reconciled period with no eligible attempts has an undefined rate: leave the numeric value blank and show N/A, its reason and zero eligible count. An absent extract is Not Measured. Neither means a measured zero failure share. Do not calculate a pooled share by averaging weekly percentages; pool the qualifying numerator and denominator counts at the agreed scope.

For category bars, length carries magnitude, so start the magnitude axis at zero. A line may use a narrower scale to reveal movement, but disclose its scale, actual rates and counts, period, scope and rival explanations. Screen slope is not practical importance. Annotate the documented selection or process change rather than removing inconvenient weeks. Keep the full required configuration list in a companion table even if an empty cell cannot render on the chart.

A statistical limit and a release target answer different questions. The target is an owned decision criterion. A p-chart estimates expected variation only under a defensible stable, comparable, independent binary-opportunity model with adequate samples. Retrying the same tests, changing selection or missing publication can undermine that model. Use an annotated run chart with limits withheld when you cannot defend the assumptions. Do not apply a binary probability model to defects per 100 changes merely because it is expressed as a rate.

**Approved worked illustration only, not organizational measurement:** periods contain failures/opportunities (2,20), (4,40), (3,30). The pooled share is 0.10; all three observed shares are 10%, but their conditional upper limits are 30.12%, 24.23%, 26.43%. Use UCL = min(1, p̄ + 3√(p̄(1−p̄)/n)) and LCL = max(0, p̄ − 3√(p̄(1−p̄)/n)). The tiny samples demonstrate arithmetic, not operational adequacy or stability. A zero n has no limits.

QA017 Final elapsed defect resolution uses distinct finally closed defects, including reopen intervals. An open defect's age is not a completed duration. Show unresolved counts separately, reject negative pairs and require final history. In the approved duration illustration [1,2,2,3,12] hours, the mean is 4, median 2 and inclusive-interpolation p85 6.6 hours. Five records do not establish a stable tail. Your count, quantile method and history limitations belong beside the result.

topics.lecture_markdown:
### The Letter

“Dear Evidence Desk: joining requirements, attempts, commits and incidents gives me one enormous table. It is easy to chart, but deployment totals grow when I add commit detail. Can a measure fix this without rebuilding?”

### The Evidence Desk reply and lecture

A measure cannot rescue an undeclared population. Start with the question “one row per what?” and keep the answers separate. Requirement scope, planned points, published attempts, latest acceptance results, logical deployments and incidents are different populations. A convenient flat join can multiply events and erase unlinked requirements simultaneously. That is an efficient machine for making confident mistakes.

You will build from saved, controlled exports, not an asserted tenant connection. Released Boards OData v2.0 metadata is the starting contract. Test and pipeline Analytics require locally confirmed preview metadata; documented REST responses are alternatives. Inspect the saved XML EntityType, Property, Key and navigation relationships, then the actual JSON list structure. A generic Boards view is not a test-result inventory, and you must not invent an OData PR entity. Append every supplied page only after its operation-specific completeness controls reconcile.

Native source properties and LOCAL model columns are different claims. A test response supplies documented id, outcome and completedDate; the request/manifest supplies run context. Your project/run/result AttemptKey and reviewed point/configuration/build mapping are local transformations. A deployment record id does not natively supply a governed logical production event, service boundary or incident attribution. Keep SourceFile, SourceRowKey, ExtractedUTC and TransformVersion local and traceable. Preserve nulls and parse errors as gaps or exceptions, not zero durations.

Create full requirement, planned-point and acceptance inventories first. Left-join reviewed summaries so unlinked required rows survive. Keep published attempts with retries separate from the latest valid acceptance record. Select that record deterministically inside each test/configuration/release/build group and window, using descending completion time and documented identity. Retain later Blocked or other nonqualifying warnings; an older pass is not an unqualified current pass. Count production events in their reconciled event fact, not commit/retry bridges. Current work-item rows cannot establish final closure or reopened histories.

**Approved fictional identity-card illustration, not measured release evidence:** required tests A, B and C share one configuration/build. A has Failed then Passed attempts; B has two Passed attempts; C has Blocked. Attempt pass share is 3/4 = 75%, latest valid acceptance pass share is 2/2 = 100%, and execution coverage is 2/3 = 66.67%. Each answers a different question. C remains visible. The 100% value cannot imply that the full plan passed.

Use unique scope dimensions and one-to-many single-direction relationships. Keep outcome filters and bridges from back-filtering the inventory denominator. DIVIDE without a zero alternate result preserves undefined arithmetic, but a blank alone cannot prove source validity. Each contract/scope needs a resolved CoverageGate approved from reconciliation. Suppress numeric claims for absent or conflicting gates. COALESCE may display an empty count only after the gate is Measured. Show the gate reason and last reconciled extraction, not merely the rendering or refresh time.

Build four local views: Quality decision overview, QA/test operations, SDLC/engineering flow, and Quality evidence/compliance-readiness. Change their decisions, not their facts. Test Passed selection and added commit detail against unchanged required inventories and logical event counts. Keep all twelve domain labels with applicability, evidence status and adequacy separate from outcome. Missing production or incident sources remain Not Measured even if build data exists. No average of domain percentages establishes ISO conformity. A labelled permitted evidence route and long-format export make each claim checkable; publishing and refresh still require separate authorization.
