steps.title: Explicit raw LOCAL DAX dictionary with correct formats; raw numbers not yet published
steps.instructions:
In **Modeling → New measure**, create these explicit **LOCAL** measures. Use the table/column names derived above, decimal fraction format for rates, hours for durations and whole numbers for counts. `Outcome` comes from published result JSON; all keys, validity flags and duration fields below are local derived columns. These are raw arithmetic measures and **must** receive the coverage wrappers before publication.

```dax
Passed Attempts =
    CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(FactAttempt), FactAttempt[Outcome] = "Passed")
Failed Attempts =
    CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(FactAttempt), FactAttempt[Outcome] = "Failed")
Eligible Attempts = [Passed Attempts] + [Failed Attempts]
Attempt Pass Share Raw = DIVIDE([Passed Attempts], [Eligible Attempts])
Other Outcome Attempts =
    COUNTROWS(FILTER(FactAttempt,
        NOT(FactAttempt[Outcome] IN {"Passed", "Failed"})))

Required Requirements =
    CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(FactRequirementScope),
        REMOVEFILTERS(FactRequirementScope[HasValidLinkedResult]))
Requirements With Evidence =
    CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(FactRequirementScope),
        FactRequirementScope[HasValidLinkedResult] = TRUE())
Traceability Raw = DIVIDE([Requirements With Evidence], [Required Requirements])
Planned Points =
    CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(FactPlannedPoint),
        REMOVEFILTERS(FactPlannedPoint[HasValidExecution]))
Executed Points =
    CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(FactPlannedPoint),
        FactPlannedPoint[HasValidExecution] = TRUE())
Execution Coverage Raw = DIVIDE([Executed Points], [Planned Points])
Acceptance Passed =
    CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(FactAcceptance), FactAcceptance[Outcome] = "Passed")
Acceptance Failed =
    CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(FactAcceptance), FactAcceptance[Outcome] = "Failed")
Acceptance Pass Share Raw =
    DIVIDE([Acceptance Passed], [Acceptance Passed] + [Acceptance Failed])
Acceptance Missing Or Other =
    COUNTROWS(FILTER(FactAcceptance,
        NOT(FactAcceptance[Outcome] IN {"Passed", "Failed"})))

PR Median Hours Raw = MEDIAN(FactPR[ElapsedHours])
PR P85 Hours Raw = PERCENTILEX.INC(FactPR, FactPR[ElapsedHours], 0.85)
Pipeline Median Hours Raw = MEDIAN(FactPipeline[DurationHours])
Pipeline P95 Hours Raw =
    PERCENTILEX.INC(FactPipeline, FactPipeline[DurationHours], 0.95)
Work Item Lead Median Hours Raw = MEDIAN(FactWorkItemCompleted[LeadHours])
Work Item Cycle P85 Hours Raw =
    PERCENTILEX.INC(FactWorkItemCompleted, FactWorkItemCompleted[CycleHours], 0.85)
Daily WIP Raw = DISTINCTCOUNT(FactWIP[WorkItemKey])

Production Deployments Raw =
    CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(FactDeployment), FactDeployment[QualifyingProduction] = TRUE())
Intervention Deployments =
    CALCULATE([Production Deployments Raw],
        FactDeployment[RequiresIntervention] = TRUE())
Change Fail Rate Raw = DIVIDE([Intervention Deployments], [Production Deployments Raw])
Incident Caused Unplanned Deployments =
    CALCULATE([Production Deployments Raw],
        FactDeployment[IncidentCausedUnplanned] = TRUE())
Deployment Rework Rate Raw =
    DIVIDE([Incident Caused Unplanned Deployments], [Production Deployments Raw])
Change Lead Median Hours Raw = MEDIAN(FactChange[LeadHours])
Change Lead P85 Hours Raw = PERCENTILEX.INC(FactChange, FactChange[LeadHours], 0.85)
Failed Deploy Recovery Median Hours Raw =
    CALCULATE(MEDIAN(FactRecovery[RecoveryHours]),
        FactRecovery[IsDeploymentCaused] = TRUE(), FactRecovery[IsRestored] = TRUE())
Failed Deploy Recovery P95 Hours Raw =
    PERCENTILEX.INC(
        FILTER(FactRecovery,
            FactRecovery[IsDeploymentCaused] = TRUE() && FactRecovery[IsRestored] = TRUE()),
        FactRecovery[RecoveryHours], 0.95)
Mature Escape Raw =
    DIVIDE(SUM(FactEscapeCohort[AcceptedPostReleaseDefects]),
           SUM(FactEscapeCohort[ShippedChanges]))
Defect Resolution Median Hours Raw = MEDIAN(FactDefectClosed[ResolutionHours])
Defect Resolution P85 Hours Raw =
    PERCENTILEX.INC(FactDefectClosed, FactDefectClosed[ResolutionHours], 0.85)
```

steps.title: Per-contract/scope wrappers and guarded domain measures; absent/conflicting gates suppressed
steps.instructions:
Wrap QA010 as follows; clone the pattern with each contract's `MetricId`, source scope and raw measure, not a single universal gate for the whole report. A Conditional/proxy value may be shown only with a reviewed, explicitly qualified separate measure; do not relabel it Measured.

```dax
QA010 Gate State =
    VAR Gates = CALCULATETABLE(CoverageGate, CoverageGate[MetricId] = "QA010")
    RETURN IF(COUNTROWS(Gates) = 1,
              MAXX(Gates, CoverageGate[Status]), "Not Measured")
Attempt Pass Share =
    IF([QA010 Gate State] = "Measured", [Attempt Pass Share Raw], BLANK())
Attempt Pass Display =
    SWITCH(TRUE(),
        [QA010 Gate State] <> "Measured", "Not Measured: see source/validity gap",
        COALESCE([Eligible Attempts], 0) = 0, "N/A: zero Passed/Failed opportunities",
        FORMAT([Attempt Pass Share], "0.0%"))
Attempt Numerator Display =
    IF([QA010 Gate State] = "Measured", FORMAT(COALESCE([Passed Attempts], 0), "0"),
       "Not Measured")
Attempt Denominator Display =
    IF([QA010 Gate State] = "Measured", FORMAT(COALESCE([Eligible Attempts], 0), "0"),
       "Not Measured")
Domain Evidence Status =
    IF(HASONEVALUE(FactQualityEvidence[LocalEvidenceRequirementKey]),
       SELECTEDVALUE(FactQualityEvidence[EvidenceStatus], "Not Measured"),
       "Review requirement rows; no combined pass")
Domain Adequacy =
    IF(HASONEVALUE(FactQualityEvidence[LocalEvidenceRequirementKey]),
       SELECTEDVALUE(FactQualityEvidence[EvidenceAdequacy], "Not reviewed"),
       "Review requirement rows")
```

`COALESCE` in the display is permitted **only after the source gate is Measured**; it displays a reconciled empty count, not an absent source as zero. Use no zero alternate result in numeric `DIVIDE`. Raw counts stay hidden on unreconciled cards. Reject conflicting or absent gate rows; `SELECTEDVALUE` alone is not proof that every selected scope passed. Add the table's `Reason` and `LastReconciledExtractUTC` to a companion scope-status table. Preserve incomplete-week and partial-history states. Percentages format decimal fractions as percent; defects-per-100-changes is labelled that way, not a probability.

topics.lecture_markdown:
### The Letter

“Dear Evidence Desk: the report looks clear to me. The status matrix is red and green, its caveat is in a tooltip, and an analyst can export raw rows. Is that enough for a reader who uses a keyboard or cannot receive sensitive incident details?”

### The Evidence Desk reply and lecture

“Clear to me” describes one observer, not a completed access test. Give the reader a route through the decision: find the scope, change an allowed filter, read the finding and caveat, inspect permitted evidence, and return or reset. Test that route without a mouse in the actual client. Platform support is a starting capability, not proof that your page's focus order and controls work.

You are testing a user task, not awarding one blanket score to a report. In M16, write the task, access need, method, expected behavior, owner and planned permitted evidence reference before execution. Leave ObservedBehavior blank and EvidenceStatus Not Measured until the task actually occurs. A prediction, screenshot or automatic check cannot fill that column with a successful observation. Record the installed client and artifact version in the evidence notes so another reviewer can understand what was tested.

Name each visual by purpose and scope; arrange supported tab order from page navigation and scope to summary, comparison, gaps, evidence, action and reset. Remove decoration from the focus sequence where possible. Test visible focus, activation and sensible return with the keys actually supported by the installed client. Do not assume one universal Power BI shortcut. If drillthrough is unsupported or inaccessible, a labelled, tested evidence table can supply the equivalent route. A blocked route remains blocked rather than being relabelled successful.

Essential caveats must persist beyond mouse hover. After a filter changes the period, your visible summary, denominator and caveat must describe the current state. Where dynamic alt text is unsupported, provide a scope-aware text summary and test it after filtering. Outcomes, measurement status, adequacy and applicability have distinct meanings: Failed is not the same as Not Measured, and Measured evidence can still be inadequate for release. Text labels and a legend must carry these distinctions without red/green perception. Inspect enlargement, clipping, high contrast and available screen-reader or assisted reading routes; state unavailable checks honestly.

**Bounded conceptual demonstration, not an observed test:** a green cell contains a missing requirement result coerced to zero failures. Repair it to persistent text: “Not Measured — result publication absent; required scope retained; QA owner to investigate.” Keep the rate blank and the requirement in the long-format table. The repair protects both meaning and access; it does not prove whole-report conformance.

Your export must retain required missing rows, headers, units, scope, numerator, denominator, evidence state and caveat. Reconcile its keys and totals against the same controlled scope. If client export truncates, produce the equivalent output through Power Query/Excel. A readable table with identifiable restricted incident notes is still unauthorized. Obtain the actual evidence owner's decision on minimization, suppression, permitted keys and audience access. Report filters are not authorization boundaries; Analytics does not enforce Area Path security.

Finally, obtain two actual people's uncued comprehension attempts. Let each identify scope and denominator, find a gap and owner, explain a comparison without color, trace permitted evidence, and state an action with a rival explanation. Do not coach the first response. Record each reader/task separately, compare misunderstandings with M17, repair the same report and retest failed tasks on a versioned revision. The instructor may be one reader, never an invented second. You may continue studying while reviewers are unavailable, but observation and practical completion remain pending.

Local C13 performance rubric (unchanged):
Score each area 0–3: **0 = absent or materially false; 1 = partially built with consequential errors; 2 = competent, reconciled and bounded; 3 = competent plus well-tested explanation of counterexamples and revisions**. Six areas total 18 points. Require at least **15/18** (ceiling of 80%) and at least **2 in every area**, plus every absolute gate below. This is a local performance rubric, not a new program-wide assessment weighting.

| Area | Evidence needed for competent (2) | Distinguishing evidence for 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Decision and audience fit | Four required audiences, owned decisions, three-to-five-visual storyboard per view in M17, same contracts across views | Readers locate actions and counter-evidence independently; documented audience-specific repairs preserve facts |
| Local acquisition and model | Saved verified metadata/JSON design, native-to-LOCAL dictionary, grain-specific queries, inventory-first joins, explicit single-direction relationships and permitted detail route | Controlled duplicate/fan-out/cross-build faults are shown to fail tests before corrected version passes |
| Measures and reconciliation | M04 contracts and explicit gated measures; all controlled keys/counts reconcile, correct zero/N/A/Not Measured and grain/censoring/reopening/deployment/rework handling | Tested date, outcome and commit-detail perturbations retain intended denominators and produce explained scope changes |
| Chart integrity and variation | Justified forms/scales, counts/denominators/exclusions, medians/tails and change annotations; limits used only with defensible assumptions | Counterexamples demonstrate why a narrowed axis, changed scope or unstable opportunity process would mislead; chosen repair is documented |
| Evidence readiness and restraint | Complete twelve-domain M13 with applicability/status/adequacy separately shown, provenance/freshness, owned gaps and no conformity claim | Explicit conflicting/conditional evidence triggers a bounded hold or collection action, with review trace rather than a synthetic score |
| Accessible and authorized use | M16 actual keyboard, summary, noncolor, table/export and permitted-access tests; two-person comprehension observations; unresolved limits disclosed | Retested repairs demonstrate better comprehension and safe evidence navigation, including equivalent restricted-access delivery where needed |

**Absolute gates override points:** truthful connection/source/observation claims; no credentials or unauthorized exports; reproducible controlled reconciliation with no unintended grain fan-out; correct available defect/reopening/rework calculations; visible required missing evidence; minimum keyboard use, text summaries and noncolor meaning. A breached gate requires correction. High visual polish cannot purchase an exception.

**Feedback/remediation:** the instructor names the failing row/measure/task and asks for a counterexample, not a personality judgment. A denominator fault requires rebuilding and reconciling inventory paths; a deployment fault requires logical-event/bridge correction; an access fault requires a tested alternative route and M16 retest. An absent authentic source requires provision or an explicit Not Measured view, never fabricated evidence. Learners resubmit corrected artifacts with versioned evidence and a short account of the change.

prediction.prompt: Before discussion, write one source check for each proposed headline: 'the retry passed, so planned scope is covered'; 'our release cadence increased, so quality improved'; 'the file is in Azure, so the required assurance is evidenced'. Which check could reverse each headline, and why? Keep this private, unscored precommit before opening feedback; record confidence.

topics.lecture_markdown:
### The Letter

“Dear Evidence Desk: three teams want the same board headline. One has a perfect pass card and fewer bugs, one deploys more often, and one cannot let us inspect its raw evidence. Can we write ‘quality improved’ and sort out the footnotes later?”

### The Evidence Desk reply and lecture

Start with the decision, not the headline. You can inspect whether a release owner should authorize a particular candidate with unresolved acceptance gaps. You cannot establish every meaning of ‘quality improved’ from one attractive card. In each clinic, name the decision owner, fixed build or service window, permitted audience and a source observation that would make you withdraw your recommendation. A challenge is useful when it can change an action, not merely when it sounds skeptical.

Clinic A asks you to connect results to their populations. Freeze the planned-point inventory before selecting outcomes. Retain every valid attempt, including the failure preceding a passing retry. Then select the latest valid acceptance result within the same test/configuration/build under a declared completion-time and tie-break rule. Attempts, eligible latest acceptance pairs and all planned points answer different questions. A blocked point remains visible but is not a valid Passed/Failed execution; an unpublished point retains blank result keys. Neither disappears because your latest-pass card looks better without it.

**Approved fictional illustration, not organizational evidence:** four planned points include P1 failing then passing, P2 passing, P3 blocked and P4 unpublished. The source illustration distinguishes an attempt share of 66.7%, a latest-valid share of 100% among two eligible pairs and execution coverage of 50% of four planned points. These are compatible observations, not evidence of safe release. For defects, compare accepted nonduplicate reports with an authoritative shipped-change denominator and equally mature observation. First detection, severity, customer-reporting exposure and reopen history can alter the interpretation of a shrinking bug count. An open defect has no final closure; preserve its censoring rather than inventing a completion.

Clinic B asks you to connect production events to instability. One deployment may have several commits, retries and incident relationships. Keep those rows for traceability, but count distinct governed logical deployment keys for cadence and event-rate denominators. Include qualifying hotfixes. A deployment requiring intervention and an incident-caused unplanned deployment are different classifications; similar rates do not mean identical event sets. Recovery needs qualified deployment-caused impairment and service-restoration evidence, not the age of a closed bug. A missing incident link means ‘none’ only when complete follow-up and an approved no-event disposition support that meaning. Otherwise the incident-dependent finding is Not Measured.

Clinic C asks whether the evidence can answer the required assertion and be inspected by the authorized audience. Reconciled pipeline rows cannot create observed user benefit or witnessed safety review. Keep all twelve existing quality-domain labels and required gaps in M13. Missing instrumentation is not an inapplicability justification. A witnessed failure can be measured evidence while inadequate for acceptance; absent observation is a different state. Analytics does not enforce Area Path security, and report filters do not authorize raw export sharing.

End all three clinics with a scoped finding, rival explanation, uncertainty, action owner and next review. If assurance is not ready, you may recommend bounded collection or repair without pretending the broader claim passed. Begin one candidate M18 intervention with outcomes pending. The clinic tests a recommendation; it does not prove that a future intervention worked.

Each disposition contains a source-based rival explanation, uncertainty, action owner and next review; C retains required assertions/all twelve domains.

self_review_steps: Pass 1, advocate then closed-draft verifier: retain your original A/B/C prediction, close the polished headline and independently compare each denominator/member list to frozen inventory, revisions, logical-event and follow-up evidence. Record changed fields and one source-based objection per clinic outside the matrices.

Pass 2, decision/access review: check assertion adequacy, permitted audience, missing-source status, qualified owner and reversibility. Reopen the draft and record an accepted and a retained/rejected objection with reasons; do not call either self-review peer participation.
asynchronous_review.request_prompt: Send an authorized accessible A/B/C draft and minimized source-key excerpts to a real peer/instructor in an agreed flexible exchange window: ‘For each clinic, show a retained missing point, logical event or required assertion behind my headline. Cite the exact field/member evidence, what observation would make me withdraw it, and who owns repair. Please challenge all three clinics, not only your favorite.’ Keep raw private rows, endpoints, tokens and protected assessment responses out of the exchange. In peer exchanges rotate advocate, navigator/recorder, verifier and decision-review functions across A/B/C; log only actual contributions.
asynchronous_review.reviewer_prompt: Independently annotate each A/B/C draft with a specific source/field, rival explanation, decision impact and proposed repair. Ask ‘Which expected key or assertion could be absent?’ and ‘Which observation reverses the recommendation?’ Acknowledge what cannot be inspected. Praise or a hypothetical reviewer does not count. The learner must individually answer, check the cited source and record accepted/rejected repair with evidence and owner.
required_real_evidence: Actual reviewer identity or approved pseudonym, exchange dates/versions, clinic/role/action and source-linked annotations in a separate authorized repair ledger.
Individual response for each clinic plus own revised rationale and accepted/rejected objection with checked evidence; all clinics retained regardless of shared recommendations.

Solo route: actual instructor challenge for each clinic and individual repair/rebuttal after two-pass self-review; absent instructor interaction is pending, not invented peer credit. Pair/triad asynchronous exchanges preserve distinct advocate and verifier functions.
asynchronous_review.pending_message: You may browse 14.2 and practice ahead while authentic source checks or real challenge are pending. Keep Evidence submitted / awaiting review, or blocked/not yet assessed where inputs are absent. Self-review, quiz scores and shared outputs cannot auto-verify source competence or issue a certificate.

recall.prompt: Close notes: In one sentence per clinic, explain why a correct narrow observation can still support the wrong board headline. Name the missing relationship, not an exact formula or endpoint. Commit the response and confidence before requesting feedback; then record confidence and a correction reason.

questions.prompt: In the worked illustration, four acceptance points are planned on one build. P1 fails then passes; P2 passes; P3 is blocked; P4 has no published result. Which statement preserves all three populations?

options.text: The release has 100% test coverage because every latest valid result passed.
Attempt pass share is 66.7%; latest-valid acceptance pass share is 100% among two eligible pairs; execution coverage is 50% of four planned points, with two gaps disclosed.
Attempt pass share is 100% after removing the first failed attempt.
Execution coverage is 75% because blocked counts as executed acceptance evidence.

questions.prompt: A complete matched-service ledger shows four logical production deployments in the baseline week and six afterward. The later six include two incident-caused hotfixes; two deployments required intervention. What is the defensible clinic finding?

options.text: Quality improved because deployment frequency increased.
Exclude hotfixes from all deployment denominators to isolate success.
Count commit bridge rows as deployments to reflect engineering effort.
Cadence rose from four to six; later change fail rate and rework rate are each 33.3%, so challenge the improvement claim with instability and follow-up evidence.

questions.prompt: Clinic C has a reconciled pipeline export but no user study, safety review or production observation. The sponsor asks for a release assurance statement. What should the reviewer submit?

options.text: A not-ready memo for the assurance claim, with required gaps marked Not Measured and named owners for collection and residual-risk decisions.
A green quality-evidence cell for every domain because the source is Azure.
An ISO conformity statement qualified by a small footnote.
Zero customer incidents, inferred from the absence of incident rows.

games.title: Evidence Triage Tray
games.objective: Assign the extra evidence that can challenge each clinic’s favored story.
games.rules: Play three rounds without a timer. For every lettered card type A, B or C: A = test/defect clinic, B = deployment/incident clinic, C = adequacy/access clinic. Submit a mapping such as x:A, y:C. Classify by the specific question the card addresses, not by where its file is stored. Consult the solution after answering; retry any round freely.

rounds.prompt: Cards: x = frozen planned-point inventory with blocked and unpublished results; y = logical production event ledger with retry identities; z = approval decision for who may inspect raw user-study evidence. Assign x, y and z to clinics A, B or C.

Cards: x = first-detection dates, severity and matched customer-reporting exposure for release defects; y = deployment-caused impairment and restoration timestamps; z = missing witnessed hazard-control review for a required safety assertion. Assign x, y and z.

Cards: x = a required acceptance point with no linked result; y = an incident-caused hotfix that also has several commit bridge rows; z = a green pipeline offered as proof of user benefit without observed task outcomes. Assign x, y and z.

games.scoring: One practice point per round only when all three card assignments are correct; maximum 3. Feedback is corrective: identify the misassigned card’s decision question and replay. These points do not enter exam scores.
games.accessible_alternative: All cards and mappings are plain text. Use keyboard typing or speak the mappings to a facilitator; there is no dragging, color dependency, audio requirement or time limit.

games.title: Repair the Board Sentence
games.objective: Replace overclaims with an evidence-bounded finding and an owned next action.
games.rules: Three untimed rounds. Rewrite each quoted sentence in at most three sentences. Include every required element in the prompt and avoid the listed forbidden inference. Exact wording is not required: the solution is a model answer. Award a round point only if all required elements are present and the forbidden inference is absent; compare with the explanation and retry.

rounds.prompt: Repair: ‘Every test passed, so release is safe.’ Worked illustration: four planned acceptance points on one build; three Passed/Failed attempts contain two passes; two eligible latest pairs pass; one point is blocked and one unpublished. Required: both pass populations, full-inventory execution coverage, both gaps, and an action owned by the QA lead. Forbidden: a safety or full-coverage conclusion.

Repair: ‘Six deployments beat four, proving our new process worked.’ Worked illustration: complete matched-service weeks; baseline has four deployments and one requiring intervention; later has six deployments, two requiring intervention, and two other incident-caused unplanned hotfix deployments. Required: cadence, both change fail rates, later rework rate, a release-owner investigation, and a noncausal caveat. Forbidden: counting bridge rows or declaring causation.

Repair: ‘Our restricted dashboard confirms acceptable user and safety outcomes.’ Actual task situation: no user study, hazard review or production observation is supplied. Required: unavailable sources, Not Measured status for required assertions, bounded/not-ready decision, an evidence-collection owner, and no live-connection claim. Forbidden: organizational conformity or invented observations.

games.scoring: Maximum 3 practice points, one per fully compliant repair. Equivalent precise wording earns credit. Missing elements receive respectful element-specific feedback and unlimited retries; no exam credit and no speed bonus.
games.accessible_alternative: Read and answer in plain text using a keyboard; a facilitator may transcribe the learner’s wording. All constraints and model answers remain available without visual effects, color or sound.

returns.prompt: Closed notes: A required acceptance point appears in the frozen inventory but not in published results. Where does it belong in the reasoning, and what must remain unknown? State confidence before answering and after correction.

Closed notes: A qualifying production hotfix is linked to multiple commits. What are the separate questions of event identity and rework classification, and why does one not answer the other? Reflect on confidence before/after.

Closed notes: A sponsor offers a perfectly reconciled pipeline export for a required user-benefit assertion. Write a defensible decision and the kind of evidence that could change it. Record confidence before/after feedback.

remediation.task: Use row/claim-specific instructor feedback to locate the failed relationship. In the same Desk Test repair one inventory-to-result member list for A, logical-event-to-incident mapping for B or assertion/source/GapAction chain for C; explain the correction and try a different controlled record. No wholesale rebuild, speed penalty or fabricated expected count.
remediation.recheck: Submit the repaired field/member evidence and changed decision for actual instructor source check; repeat closed-note relationship explanation and the unchanged quiz as needed. Missing authentic provision remains blocked.

topics.stretch: Defend a narrower alternative recommendation using the same reconciled evidence against an actual instructor objection. Identify source evidence that could falsify both recommendations and explain why equal-looking failure/rework rates require separate sets. No manufactured outcome or combined quality score.
topics.resume_checkpoint: Save your last completed W-step, matrix/source version, remaining A/B/C gaps and next unfinished action in a private resume note. This is a learner-managed checkpoint, not live progress storage. Resume the same cumulative Desk Test.
accessibility: Use the full graph text and key tables with status words rather than color-only meaning. Typed, dictated or learner-confirmed scribed responses are equivalent; practice is untimed.
Use approved authentic anonymized exports and accessible non-screen-sharing text/table review. No secrets, unauthorized raw rows or compulsory synchronous attendance.

Memory clip script/pending media production is offered only in quiz feedback after a committed practice attempt; read the equivalent explanation there now. No rendered audio/video exists. Future production needs captions/transcript, visual descriptions, keyboard controls and pause/skip/mute; text remains equivalent.

topics.title: Decision Memo and 30-day experiment

prediction.prompt: Individually predict: A checklist has been approved but no follow-up has been collected. The sponsor wants OutcomeEvidence = 'effective' and offers to pick whichever measure improves later. What would you write instead, and what must be decided before action? Commit a private unscored response and confidence before requesting feedback.

topics.lecture_markdown:
### The Letter

“Dear Evidence Desk: the clinic found a real gap. Our team proposes a checklist, and the sponsor wants a seven-minute recommendation. Can we promise improvement now and choose the success measure after a month?”

### The Evidence Desk reply and lecture

Write the requested action before preparing the opening line. Your memo should enable a decision, not merely win approval of a presentation. Name the person who can authorize the action, the person who will execute it and the real capacity or budget constraint. These may differ. If you do not know a constraint, ask for it explicitly rather than inventing a reassuring estimate. The five-to-seven-minute presentation scope is a planning guide; an accessible written or scribed memo must carry the same evidence and limitations without a speed test.

Build three essential evidence beats from your existing clinics: a scoped finding, its strongest consequential challenge and a bounded action. Link each beat through M17 to the M04 contract and actual source/version. Keep detailed keys and calculation work in the appendix, but leave a decision-changing gap visible in the main message. If you cannot support assurance, say not ready and ask for collection or repair. A passing test card does not supply missing user observations merely because your request sounds confident.

Next develop the same M18 candidate row, not another experiment. Before acting, freeze a comparable baseline cohort/source, defined intervention, contracted success measure and criterion with local rationale. Predeclare instability and privacy guardrails, a stop/revise rule, accountable owner and specific day-30 review date. Put collection method, observation-completeness procedure and approvals in the referenced protocol document: M18 has no CollectionMethod column. Approval of that protocol is not an outcome observation. Keep outcome EvidenceStatus Not Measured and OutcomeEvidence pending collection until appropriate authentic follow-up is collected and reviewed.

**Conceptual example:** your clinic identifies unpublished acceptance evidence. A bounded trial could ask the QA lead to match frozen planned-point keys to published results at the existing candidate review and route gaps for disposition. That is an inspectable process action. Counting repeated attempts instead of distinct planned points would change the success population, not demonstrate the trial's effect. The success criterion must use its frozen M04 denominator and cannot silently abandon missing points or waive separate release criteria. This is a proposed local scenario, not an observed learner trial or management approval.

At day 30, the owner would obtain the approved follow-up, complete the recorded page/partition flow, reconcile expected and member keys through M08, and calculate the original success and guardrail measures with both counts. Distinguish three dispositions. Favorable criterion attainment with adequate observation and satisfied guardrails may justify bounded continuation. Missing required observation leaves effectiveness or guardrail evidence Not Measured and requires the prescribed pause/defer and owned collection. Verified access harm requires the written stop/contain/escalation route. Do not invent a harm event from an empty ledger, and do not let a favorable metric compensate for a verified breach.

Even a properly scoped improvement after an intervention does not by itself establish causation. Release risk mix, test selection, concurrent changes and reporting exposure may change too. Preserve the observed comparison, record confounders and request better matched evidence before strengthening the inference.

Finally obtain two substantive real reviews, answer their source-linked objections individually and retain rejected-to-final revisions. Test whether real authorized readers can find the headline, evidence and consequential caveat. Self-review is useful preparation, not a substitute for real reviewers or observed access. Your final portfolio integrates the existing source/model/four-report work; a polished memo, quiz pass or planned protocol cannot replace instructor verification of every evidence and access gate.

visual.alt: C14 reasoning map: counter-evidence constrains a bounded memo and protocol; future evidence determines continue, revise or stop with scope repair.
visual.trace_prompt: Trace Q Counter-evidence challenge → M Bounded decision memo → P Predeclared protocol → V Future evidence review → D Continue, revise or stop → S Scope and access. On your actual M18 row locate SuccessCriterion, Guardrail, StopRule, Owner and ReviewDate. Write which field could prevent automatic continuation and explain what the P-to-V arrow observes today: it is a planned dependency, not collected effectiveness. Identify a concrete source/scope repair that could follow D without inventing a result.
visual.text_equivalent: S Scope and access constrains R Reconciled source keys. R branches to A Points and defects, B Deploys and incidents and C Assertion adequacy; all feed Q Counter-evidence challenge. Q informs M Bounded decision memo, which defines P Predeclared protocol. P specifies V Future evidence review; V informs D Continue, revise or stop. D returns scope/source repair to S. In M18, SuccessCriterion, Guardrail and StopRule constrain the future disposition; Owner and ReviewDate locate responsibility. OutcomeEvidence stays pending until authentic collection/review. A missing observation prompts bounded hold/collection, not invented success or harm. Planned arrows do not establish observed results or causation.

preconditions: Open your existing 14.1 M18 candidate, all three clinic dispositions, cumulative contracts/reconciliation/model/report evidence and approved next-cycle stakeholder/access brief. Develop the same portfolio, not a second dashboard or experiment.

Use the parent-provided exact workbook copies and C14 graph. Have the approved authentic baseline and source/page/partition dictionaries, authorization/constraint evidence and real review/access arrangements, or retain explicit pending status.

Resume in short learner-managed segments with a saved artifact version and next action. Documentation stays open. No user tenant connection, recorded walkthrough, live progress queue or actual future intervention is claimed by this authored content.

steps.title: Choose the bounded request and revalidate contracts
steps.instructions: Choose one defensible clinic finding for intervention while retaining all three clinic texts. State authorizing decision owner, executing action owner, affected audience and actual approved or explicitly requested capacity/budget constraint. In M04 Metric Contract confirm the selected success and guardrail register IDs and every exact field, especially InformationNeed/FormulaDefinition/GrainCohort/Numerator/Denominator/PeriodUTC/Exclusions/ThresholdRationale/SourceRef/Limitations. An unknown constraint is a request, not an approved fact. A local criterion is not an ISO target.
steps.checkpoint_output: Same M04 contracts with changed-scope rationale and a decision/owner/constraint paragraph linked to authentic clinic evidence.

steps.title: Predeclare the same M18 protocol before action
steps.instructions: In M18 Improvement Experiment complete ExperimentId/Decision/Owner/BaselineCohort/BaselineSource/Intervention/SuccessMeasureId/SuccessCriterion/Guardrail/StopRule/ReviewDate/EvidenceStatus/OutcomeEvidence/Confounders in their exact order. Tie SuccessMeasureId to M04 and define the denominator using distinct contracted point/event keys, not attempts/bridge rows. Freeze comparable pre-change scope, local criterion/rationale and qualified guardrails before any action. Put collection/completeness/approvals in the referenced protocol, never a new CollectionMethod column. Choose the specific UTC day-30 review date from the actual approved start; no illustrative date is an actual approval. Before outcomes exist, mark them Not Measured and OutcomeEvidence pending collection with protocol reference. Use QA004's action-closure versus effectiveness-review distinction without populating a measured scheduled-review cohort from this single proposed protocol.
steps.checkpoint_output: One versioned M18 row and referenced pre-action protocol with outcome evidence pending and authorization/constraint requests distinguished from facts.

steps.title: Write the actual future collection and disposition procedure
steps.instructions: In the protocol name who freezes follow-up inventory, which approved retained Azure responses/authentic exports are used and who retains restricted raw evidence. Reuse W2 source inspection from 14.1: metadata-first OData keys/types and @odata.nextLink, operation-specific REST pagination, environment continuation token/top versus separate Classic Release source. Validate native paths against responses; LOCAL test inventory/attempt, deployment event/bridge and incident fields are governed mappings, not promised native Azure properties. Record mapping grain/build/service and M08 authoritative same-grain/member-key completeness checks; preserve its existing Reconciled/Mismatch formula and blanks. Specify day-30 success/guardrail counts under the frozen contracts. Missing required follow-up stays Not Measured and triggers pause/defer/owned collection; verified access harm triggers the stated stop/contain/notify route; failed criterion triggers approved revise/stop. Reject negative durations, retain open censoring and confounders, and require approval/versioning before a future protocol changes. These are proposed local future actions, not scheduled automation or actual outcomes.
steps.checkpoint_output: Secure source/paging/member-key collection procedure and separately written favorable, missing-observation, failed-criterion and verified-harm dispositions with responsible owners.

steps.title: Build three M17 evidence-to-decision beats
steps.instructions: In M17 Chart Decision enter exactly one row for each essential beat: scoped observation, challenging gap/instability and bounded action. Use every exact field, link MetricId/MatrixId/SourceRef to actual M04 and clinic sources, and document Comparison/FilterScope/DenominatorRule/CounterEvidence. Use long-format evidence rather than a combined conformity score. Keep consequence-bearing Not Measured states in the main memo. Write the source-backed evidence-to-action justification and why you rejected the more attractive claim.
steps.checkpoint_output: Three M17 rows and source-linked memo draft with visible consequential caveat.

steps.title: Verify the existing Matrix and two source trails
steps.instructions: Open the existing local Power BI C13 model, not a new deployed dashboard. Confirm staged M13/M18 LOCAL keys and blanks; select the quality-evidence Matrix visual. Use M13 DomainId/Characteristic and approved evidence requirement as row context, not raw result attempts directly joined to domains. Show validated local EvidenceStatus/adequacy/source-reference detail through the existing measures/detail route. Inspect planned-point/result and deployment/commit bridges separately: domain/date filtering must retain required missing points/requirements in contracted denominators and never turn bridge rows into deployment counts. Drill from TWO memo aggregates to member-key tables and original EvidenceRef; reconcile both counts against Excel. If restricted, use the approved Excel/Power Query model, pivot/accessible long-format table and a learner-provided recorded or approved equivalent Power BI relationship/Matrix-design explanation demonstrating the same design. Label design evidence truthfully; do not claim an actual .pbix or recording you did not supply.
steps.checkpoint_output: Two reproducible aggregate-to-contract/model/member-key/source trails and existing report/equivalent verification with truthful connection/build mode.

steps.title: Conduct real access and two-person comprehension checks
steps.instructions: In M16 Accessible Review plan CheckId/Artifact/UserTask/AccessNeed/TestMethod/ExpectedBehavior for finding the headline, changing a relevant filter, opening source detail and reading the caveat. Conduct the approved keyboard/focus, readable-label, noncolor-status, text-summary/tabular-export and applicable screen-reader checks using the prior access plan. Only after actual checks enter ObservedBehavior/Finding/EvidenceStatus/Owner/EvidenceRef/Remediation. Ask TWO actual approved people to identify the requested decision and consequential counter-evidence through written task responses or permitted interaction; record their actual interpretation and task behavior, not a fictional successful user study. Retest repairs. Keep raw observations restricted and summaries minimally identifying. If people or tools are unavailable, leave observations blank and test pending/Not Measured.
steps.checkpoint_output: M16 actual-or-pending task rows, approved restricted observation references, both real comprehension responses and retest evidence where applicable.

steps.title: Prepare and challenge one accessible memo
steps.instructions: Author an accessible written memo/transcript and chosen presentation equivalent. In the inherited five-to-seven-minute planning scope, use 0–1 for decision/owner/constraint, 1–3 for finding/source trail, 3–4 for rival explanation/gaps, 4–5 for intervention/guardrail, 5–7 for review/reversal and approval request. These are neither countdowns nor speed grades; never hide material uncertainty to fit a window. Commit your request/strongest counter-evidence/stop condition before reviews. Use the real asynchronous two-cycle procedure below; each reviewer independently gives at least TWO source/field-linked objections with decision impact and proposed repair, then you individually answer both central objections. Reviews are not release approval or instructor grades.
steps.checkpoint_output: Same source-linked memo plus precommit, two actual substantive review exchanges, individual replies and dated accepted/rejected change ledger.

steps.title: Revise, export and seek individual assessment
steps.instructions: Keep dated rejected/final drafts and concise change account: objection, old claim/field, evidence checked, new claim/field or justified retention, action owner. Reconcile changed counts against original sources or explicitly version changed extracts/contracts. Assemble query/XML/JSON provenance and paging/history/retention/refresh evidence; model/dictionary/bridges, contracts, QA plan, uncertainty ledger; all three clinics; four prior dashboard files or approved equivalents and accessible status report/storyboard; source-linked memo, M13 gaps, M16 actual checks, M17 beats, M18 protocol, both reviews/revisions. Export the NINE assigned cumulative matrices as authorized exact-header UTF-8 long-format CSVs plus learner Excel copies and accessible member-key appendix. Exclude credentials/unauthorized personal evidence and preserve permitted restricted lineage. During the original integration allowance obtain actual instructor row/claim feedback, make individual corrections and defend the two source trails. Submit truthful design/protocol/blocked-source ledger and request assessed-build resumption if gates remain blocked.
steps.checkpoint_output: One individually owned revised final portfolio, same proposed protocol, source/access/review evidence and explicit pending gates for authorized instructor assessment.

completion_checks: All claims resolve to exact contracts/source versions and controlled member keys; required inventories/unknowns remain visible, retries/reopenings/rework/censoring/event grains are correct, and there is no unintended fan-out.

M18 contains accountable owner, authentic approved or explicitly requested constraints, comparable baseline/source, predeclared success/guardrail/stop-review rules and referenced collection/completeness procedure; pending outcomes are acceptable only for a proposed experiment.

Both real substantive reviews with individual responses and actual required access/two-person comprehension evidence exist, or explicitly pending/not yet assessed; self-review/AI-simulated discussion earns no peer credit.

Authorized instructor checks all absolute gates and every local rubric area at least competent; technical/capstone score must also meet the inherited >=80% requirement. Polish cannot compensate for evidence/access/privacy faults.

your_turn.task: Individually version the SAME selected M04/M18 protocol, M17 beats and final portfolio under an instructor-controlled authentic next-cycle scope/authorization brief. Without an answer-bearing exemplar, revalidate baseline, actual constraints, collection/completeness, guardrails and reversal rules. Use a genuine Clinic B event-reconciliation intervention where the brief supports it, or your Clinic A intervention on the changed candidate. Explain why favorable observation, unknown follow-up and verified harm require different dispositions. Finalize one protocol and memo, not a second experiment.
your_turn.changed_condition: Use a different approved next-cycle matched service/release window and adjusted actual authorized inspection audience from the guided build. Owners, capacity and approval come only from the brief. If absent, label conceptual rehearsal: the next cohort uses another service; reviewer receives aggregates only; required incident follow-up is unavailable. Authentic assessment remains blocked and no outcome is claimed.
submission: Individual versioned M04/M18 protocol and three M17 beats; accessible written/scribed memo with the inherited five-to-seven-minute content scope.
Same final portfolio's source/member-key/access evidence, actual-or-pending M16 observations, both substantive review cycles and individual response/change account.
Changed-scope defense, instructor-feedback corrections and explicit blocked/pending inputs; no invented budget, management approval, participant or follow-up result.
success_checks: Revalidate comparable baseline and authorization rather than carrying the guided figures forward; preserve exact schemas, sources and pending outcome status.
Explain continue/revise/stop/defer and causal limits independently using the predeclared fields.
Meet individual capstone rubric and absolute source/access/privacy/review gates or retain pending assessment; concept games cannot clear practical gates.

self_review_steps: Pass 1: commit your bounded request/strongest counter-evidence/predicted objection, close the polished memo and independently verify grain, keys, denominators, history/censoring, bridge fan-out and missingness. Record one potential disconfirming row and repair in a separate ledger.

Pass 2: check authorizer/executor, actual constraints, affected audience, authorized source route, access/harm/completeness/stop logic and visible caveat. Record possible revision/stop/defer outcomes and confirm pending evidence is not called success. These two self-review passes do not count as the two real capstone reviews.
asynchronous_review.request_prompt: Arrange two distinct actual peers, or a real peer plus instructor under the approved pair route, for separate asynchronous cycles on authorized written memo/protocol/key tables. Cycle 1 asks ‘Show exact member keys; which missing/repeated/historical row would change this claim?’ Cycle 2 asks ‘How can the authorized affected audience reach the consequential caveat, and who stops/revises when harm or completeness fails?’ Ask each reviewer to independently precommit objections before seeing the other's feedback, cite at least two concrete rows/protocol fields, state decision impact and propose repair. Use written task responses for the approved two-person comprehension checks if needed; no mandatory screen sharing or synchronous attendance.
asynchronous_review.reviewer_prompt: Reviewer 1 challenges grain/history/missingness with at least two specific source-linked objections. Reviewer 2 challenges audience/authority/access/harm/reversal with at least two specific field/task-linked objections. Return actual annotations, not ‘looks good’. The author individually responds to both central objections, checks cited source/member keys, retains accepted/rejected feedback with reasons and versions the same artifact. Neither cycle is a popularity vote, release approval or protected exam review.
required_real_evidence: Separate protected review/change ledger with actual reviewer identities or approved pseudonyms, role/lens, date/version, at least two objections per review, cited field/source/task, impact, repair, learner response and follow-up owner.

Two distinct actual review cycles, individual written central-objection answers and dated rejected-to-final change account. The two substantive reviews retain their separate place in unchanged program assessment weighting; do not merge them into self-review or game points.

M16 actual interpretations/behavior from two approved comprehension readers, required actual access checks and retests, or explicit pending/Not Measured entries. Review encounters may also carry these tasks; never invent successful readers.

Solo preparation may use two actual instructor challenge passes after two-pass self-review, but does not automatically erase the original real-peer/two-person gates. Arrange actual peer exchanges or request an explicitly approved equivalent; until accepted and performed, unmet gates remain pending/not yet assessed. No AI-simulated peer, self-signoff or invented attendance counts.
asynchronous_review.pending_message: You may continue reading, practice, take formative work and prepare exports while review is pending. Evidence submitted / awaiting review is not Verified complete. Retain unmet real-review/access/source gates; only the authorized instructor can verify individual evidence and permit completion under the original rules, never quizzes alone.

recall.prompt: Close notes: Explain the difference between an action being completed, a success criterion being observed and the intervention being proved causal. What may the Decision Memo responsibly request at each stage? Commit your response/confidence before feedback, then record confidence and one correction reason.

questions.prompt: Which M18 entry makes a proposed 30-day experiment reviewable before it starts?

options.text: SuccessCriterion = ‘dashboard looks greener’; ReviewDate = ‘later’.
OutcomeEvidence = ‘improved’ before any follow-up is collected.
A named owner, frozen baseline/source, defined intervention, contracted success criterion, instability/privacy guardrail, predeclared stop rule and a specific day-30 review date.
A promise to choose the best-looking outcome measure after day 30.

questions.prompt: On day 30 the success metric meets its criterion, but the predeclared privacy guardrail has been breached. Which Decision Memo disposition is correct?

options.text: Continue unchanged because the success metric has greater presentation impact.
Apply the stop/revise rule, contain the exposure, notify the accountable owner and record the breach before reconsidering continuation.
Delete the guardrail column so the assessment reflects the final decision.
Label the experiment ISO-certified because its success criterion passed.

questions.prompt: An owned intervention is followed by higher planned execution coverage. During the same month, release scope shrinks and customer-report collection changes. Which conclusion belongs in the day-30 memo?

options.text: The intervention caused the improvement because it preceded it.
The observed improvement is meaningless and all follow-up should be discarded.
Recalculate only the periods that make the intervention look best.
Report the scoped observation, document both confounders, assess guardrails and collect a matched follow-up before claiming causal effectiveness.

games.title: Protocol Assembly Bench
games.objective: Assemble a predeclared experiment in the correct columns and temporal order.
games.rules: Three untimed rounds use different assembly moves. Submit the requested letter order, field mappings or letter selection. Each round has one defined correct solution. Reveal the solution after answering, explain any mismatch using the real M18 columns, and retry freely.

rounds.prompt: Order these steps before and after action: A = collect the 30-day follow-up under the approved contract; B = obtain owner approval of the frozen baseline, intervention, criterion, guardrail and stop rule; C = review evidence and record continue/revise/stop disposition on day 30; D = carry out the approved intervention. Type the four-letter sequence.

Map cards to M18 columns. x = ‘QA009 under the M04 frozen-point contract’; y = ‘pause expansion if incident observation is incomplete or any raw evidence is disclosed outside approved access’; z = ‘release scope shrank and reporting-channel coverage changed’. Choose each from SuccessMeasureId, StopRule, Confounders. Type x:column; y:column; z:column.

Choose the one entry safe to write before collection. A = OutcomeEvidence: ‘effectiveness proven’; B = EvidenceStatus: ‘Measured outcomes’; C = OutcomeEvidence: ‘pending collection; approved protocol reference retained, no outcome observations yet’; D = Confounders: ‘none possible’. Type A, B, C or D.

games.scoring: One practice point per entirely correct round, maximum 3. Report which ordering or column choice needs correction and allow unlimited replay; practice points are separate from assessments.
games.accessible_alternative: All sequencing and mapping use plain text and keyboard entry, with facilitator transcription if needed. No timed interaction, drag gesture, sound or color signal is required.

games.title: The Skeptical Review Hearing
games.objective: Choose a continuation decision and defend it against a specific skeptical objection.
games.rules: Play three independent day-30 hearings without a timer. For each, choose one disposition: A = continue the bounded trial with scheduled review; B = stop/contain and seek owner review under the guardrail; C = defer effectiveness conclusion and collect matched or complete evidence. Then write one sentence answering the quoted objection. One round point requires both the correct letter and the required reasoning shown in the model solution; wording may vary. These are fictional decision cards, not collected outcomes.

rounds.prompt: Hearing 1: The predeclared success criterion is met; reconciled matched cohorts and complete observation support the calculation; all guardrails pass; the owner has approved continuation within the same budget. Objection: ‘Then can we say the intervention caused the gain?’ Choose A, B or C and answer.

Hearing 2: Execution coverage meets the success criterion, but identifiable raw user evidence was exported outside the approved audience. The stop rule says contain unauthorized disclosure immediately. Objection: ‘Can’t the coverage gain compensate?’ Choose A, B or C and answer.

Hearing 3: A coverage chart rises, but half the planned inventory is absent from the extract and incident follow-up is unavailable. No harm event is verified. The rule pauses expansion if required observation is incomplete. Objection: ‘There are no incident rows, so why wait?’ Choose A, B or C and answer.

games.scoring: One practice point per correct disposition plus adequate defense, maximum 3. Give specific respectful feedback on the missing evidence boundary or rule, permit unlimited retries, and do not add practice points to exam scores.
games.accessible_alternative: Choose letters and write or dictate the defense using plain text. All branches and feedback are readable; no timer, sound, animation, drag-only action or color-only meaning is used.

returns.prompt: Closed notes: The owner has approved a protocol today. Explain why the outcome entry must remain pending and name the pre-action commitments that make a later unfavorable result reviewable. Reflect on confidence before/after.

Closed notes: Contrast a missing required observation with a verified access harm during a trial. What different actions should the predeclared protocol trigger, and who must be involved? Record confidence before/after.

Closed notes: A matched-looking chart improves after a process change, but release risk mix and the reporting channel also changed. Draft the inference boundary and the next evidence request without discarding the scoped observation. Reflect on confidence before/after.

remediation.task: Use actual instructor row/claim feedback to repair one missing M18 success/guardrail/stop/owner/source field or unsupported claim in the same protocol. Write its unfavorable-outcome disposition and trace one memo aggregate to original member keys; retest an actual access fault when relevant. No fabricated observations or second wholesale build.
remediation.recheck: Return repaired source-linked field, individual explanation and access retest to the authorized instructor. Repeat conceptual recall/unchanged quiz as needed; unavailable reviewers or source/access tests stay pending.

topics.stretch: Against an actual instructor challenge, compare a feasible alternative intervention using the same constraints and evidence, identify competing explanations and propose a stronger future evidence design for qualified owner review. Keep noncausal limits; do not run or claim an instrumented study, generated media or day-30 results.
topics.resume_checkpoint: Save last W-step, memo/protocol/matrix/source versions, both review-cycle status and next unfinished correction in your private resume note. Resume the same final portfolio. A planned day-30 review is not scheduled by this content.
accessibility: Accessible written memo/transcript and typed, dictated or learner-confirmed scribed defense carry the same decision/evidence scope; five-to-seven-minute planning scope is not a timed test.

Use full graph text, keyboard/focus source route, readable labels, status words, approved table export and non-screen-sharing review. M16 needs actual approved observations; automated success alone is not conformance.

Memory clip script/pending media production is released only within quiz feedback after a committed practice attempt. Read its equivalent there now; no rendered/recorded clip is claimed. Future media require captions/transcript, visual descriptions, keyboard pause/skip/mute and equivalent static text.

submission: One individually owned final portfolio: authorized learner Excel copies and nine cumulative exact-header UTF-8 CSVs M04/M08/M10/M11/M12/M13/M16/M17/M18, three A/B/C dispositions, reproducible source/member-key appendix, query/XML/JSON request/version/paging/history/refresh/retention evidence, model/dictionary/bridges, QA plan, contracts and uncertainty ledger.

Four existing dashboard files or approved equivalents, accessible status report/storyboard, source-linked written memo/transcript, one proposed M18 protocol with collection/completeness/approval detail separately referenced, real M16 access/two-person comprehension checks and retests.

Precommits, two substantive actual review-cycle annotations with at least two objections each, individual written replies, dated rejected-to-final drafts and change account, instructor corrections and changed-scope defense. Include truthful connection/build mode and explicit pending/blocked gates. Proposed experiment outcomes may remain pending; measured effectiveness may not be claimed without authentic follow-up.
reviewer_checks: First inspect truthful mode, secret/privacy/authorization boundaries, keyboard/noncolor/text source access, required evidence statuses and defect/rework arithmetic. Noncompensable faults require repair, never a compensating polish average.

Verify all controlled totals/member keys at declared grains, zero unintended duplicates/fan-out, retained inventories, retries/reopenings, mature exposure, distinct logical events, rework and censoring. Reproduce two memo aggregates through model/member keys/raw references and inspect all three dispositions.

Check actual two substantive reviews, individual objection responses/revisions and real required access/two-person comprehension observations; self-review or fictional participants cannot replace them. Verify M18 predeclared protocol, owner, constraints, baseline/source, collection, success/guardrail/stop and day-30 rules.

Apply the original local four-level rubric to EACH area: 3 strong, 2 competent, 1 developing, 0 absent/unsupported; require at least 2 in every area plus technical/capstone >=80% and every absolute gate. Areas are Decision/business relevance; Audience fit; Evidence/model accuracy; QA management and improvement; Narrative logic and challenge; Visual access; Ethical restraint. These local performance levels are not additional program weights.

Decision/business relevance at competent: bounded request, authorizer/executor, approved or explicitly requested constraint and inspectable M18 need/review. Strong compares feasible alternatives and explicit reversal evidence. Generic promises, invented approval/budget or no owned action are developing/unsupported.

Audience fit at competent: M17 three beats fit decision-maker/affected audience and understandable counts/caveats in written/presentation versions. Strong uses both actual comprehension checks and audience-specific form without changing facts. Hidden caveat/uncomprehended headline/missing affected group are developing/unsupported.

Evidence/model accuracy at competent: exact M04/M08/M10/M11/M12 contracts/key reconciliation, correct grains, inventories, retries, mature cohorts, reopenings, censoring and event/incident bridges. Strong lets a challenger reproduce two aggregates and tests difficult gaps. Fan-out, attempted-count coverage, missing denominator, first-closure substitution, bug restoration or bridge rework require correction.

QA management and improvement at competent: existing QA plan/approvals and M13 gap owners support predeclared M18 intervention, baseline/source, success, instability/privacy guardrails, stop/revise, collection and day-30 review. Strong distinguishes closure/effectiveness, missing follow-up/confounding and approval/escalation. Post-hoc criterion, invented effectiveness or missing qualified owner/stop rule is developing/unsupported.

Narrative logic and challenge at competent: all three bounded clinic dispositions, claim/evidence/counter-evidence/action and two substantive reviews plus rejected-to-final account. Strong defends both central skeptical objections with checked rows and retains a justified rejected interpretation. Praise, untested rival explanation or persuasion without sources is insufficient.

Visual access at competent: four prior views/equivalents reconcile; M16 actual keyboard/noncolor/text-summary/export and two-person comprehension, with required rows and blank/status meanings retained. Strong includes mouse-free source detail, found consequential gap and recorded retests. Missing keyboard route, fabricated user testing, color-only readiness or missing denominators under filters are absolute faults.

Ethical restraint at competent: measured/proxy/not measured/justified inapplicable states distinguished, mode truthful, privacy/access/retention respected, no conformity or unsupported causal claim. Strong challenges minimized disclosure while retaining secure lineage and lets uncertainty alter action. Fake integration, secrets, unauthorized raw sharing, synthetic proof passed as authentic and unsupported user/safety claims are noncompensable.

Return precise matrix/field/source correction and reassess individual repaired evidence. Original program overall >=80%, all topic quizzes/checkpoints 3/3, each course final 4/5, separate program final 29/36, technical/capstone >=80%, competence in every area/all gates and separately weighted real review cycles remain required; original program weights remain unchanged and are not redefined here.
